modules.title: The action of `SL(2, ℂ)` on bispinor indices
modules.doc:
A bispinor index is a left-handed and a right-handed Weyl index side by side, and the Pauli
matrices carry four-vector indices to bispinor indices.

## i. Overview

A bispinor index `(α, α̇)` is a left-handed and a right-handed Weyl index side by side, on which
`M ∈ SL(2, ℂ)` acts by `M_{αβ} conj(M_{α̇β̇})` (`bispinorMatrix`).

The covariant Pauli matrices change a four-vector index `μ` into a bispinor index,
`μ ↦ (σ_μ)_{αα̇}`. On every index of a coefficient tensor this is `pauliTransform`. As
`M σ_μ Mᴴ = Σ_ν Λ_{νμ} σ_ν`, it carries the action of the Lorentz matrix `Λ` of `M` to that of
`M` on bispinor indices, and by the trace orthogonality of the Pauli matrices it is injective (A).
On tensors this is `complexLorentzTensor.pauliTensorMap`, in
`PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.Bispinors.ComplexifiedAction`.

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.bispinorMatrix` : the action of `SL(2, ℂ)` on one bispinor index.
- `Lorentz.pauliTransform` : the change from four-vector indices to bispinor indices.
- `Lorentz.act_bispinorMatrix_pauliTransform` : it intertwines the two actions.
- `Lorentz.pauliTransform_injective` : it is injective.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. From four-vector indices to bispinor indices

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: Lorentz.bispinorMatrix
declarations.doc:
The matrix by which `M ∈ SL(2, ℂ)` acts on one bispinor index `(α, α̇)`, a left-handed and a
right-handed Weyl index, `M_{αβ} conj(M_{α̇β̇})`.
declarations.statement: def bispinorMatrix (M : SL(2,ℂ)) : Fin 2 × Fin 2 → Fin 2 × Fin 2 → ℂ

declarations.name: Lorentz.pauliTransform
declarations.doc:
The change from a four-vector index to a bispinor index by the covariant Pauli matrices,
`μ ↦ (σ_μ)_{αα̇}`, on every index of a coefficient tensor.
declarations.statement:
def pauliTransform {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :
    ((ι → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ) →ₗ[ℂ] ((ι → Fin 2 × Fin 2) → ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.sum_pauliLower_mul_bispinorMatrix
declarations.doc:
The covariant Pauli matrices move as a covector, `M σ_μ Mᴴ = Σ_ν Λ_{νμ} σ_ν`, written
entrywise against the action on a bispinor index.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_pauliLower_mul_bispinorMatrix (M : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (q : Fin 2 × Fin 2) :
    ∑ p : Fin 2 × Fin 2, PauliMatrix.pauliLower μ p.1 p.2 * bispinorMatrix M q p
      = ∑ ν, (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup M).1 ν μ : ℝ) : ℂ) * PauliMatrix.pauliLower ν q.1 q.2

declarations.name: Lorentz.act_bispinorMatrix_pauliTransform
declarations.doc:
The Pauli change of indices carries the action of the Lorentz matrix of `M` on four-vector
indices to the action of `M` on bispinor indices.
declarations.statement:
lemma act_bispinorMatrix_pauliTransform {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (M : SL(2,ℂ))
    (c : (ι → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ) :
    act (bispinorMatrix M) (pauliTransform c)
      = pauliTransform (act (fun a b => (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup M).1 a b : ℝ) : ℂ)) c)

declarations.name: Lorentz.sum_pauliLower_mul_pauliLower_swap
declarations.doc: The trace orthogonality of the covariant Pauli matrices, `tr (σ_μ σ_ν) = 2 δ_{μν}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_pauliLower_mul_pauliLower_swap (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    ∑ p : Fin 2 × Fin 2, PauliMatrix.pauliLower μ p.1 p.2 * PauliMatrix.pauliLower ν p.2 p.1
      = 2 * if μ = ν then 1 else 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.pauliTransform_injective
declarations.doc: The Pauli change of indices is injective. Half the transposed Pauli matrices undo it.
declarations.statement:
lemma pauliTransform_injective {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :
    Function.Injective (pauliTransform (ι := ι))

modules.title: The complexified Lorentz group acting on Weyl tensors
modules.doc:
The complex Lorentz tensors with Weyl colours carry an action of `SL(2, ℂ) × SL(2, ℂ)` with the
same invariant tensors as `SL(2, ℂ)`.

## i. Overview

The complexified Lorentz group `SL(2, ℂ) × SL(2, ℂ)` acts on the complex Lorentz tensors with Weyl
colours, `(M, N)` acting on each undotted index by `M`, on each dotted index by `N`, and on their
duals by the inverse transposes (`complexifiedAction`, A.1). Restricted along the complexification
`M ↦ (M, M̄)` it is the action of `SL(2, ℂ)` (A.2).

On undotted indices followed by dotted ones, each factor acts on its own indices only. The
Reynolds elements of the two factors, applied one after the other, fix an invariant and send every
product of tensors to a product of invariant tensors, so the invariants of the complexified action
are spanned by the products of an invariant tensor of the undotted indices and one of the dotted
indices (B).

The invariant tensors of the two actions are the same (C). One direction is the restriction. For
the other, take a real square-zero `G`, such as `E` or `F`, and the line `1 + z G` in `SL(2, ℂ)`
(C.1). Along `t ↦ 1 + c₀ t G`, for real `t`, the matrices of the undotted colours are holomorphic
in `c₀ t` and those of the dotted colours antiholomorphic (C.2). So the derivative of the
components of an invariant tensor is `c₀` times the action of `G` on its undotted indices plus `c̄₀`
times that on its dotted ones, and it vanishes. Taking `c₀ = 1` and `c₀ = i` shows that `G` kills
the invariant tensor on its undotted indices alone. The components along `s ↦ (1 + s z G, 1)` then
have derivative zero at the identity, hence everywhere by the group law, so the invariant tensor is
fixed by `(1 + z G, 1)` (C.3). These elements generate `SL(2, ℂ) × 1`, and
`(1, N) = (N̄, N) (N̄⁻¹, 1)` (C.4). With B, the invariant tensors with undotted indices followed by
dotted ones are spanned by products of invariant tensors of each chirality,
`invariants_append_eq_map₂_prodT`.

Two consequences follow here. A left- and a right-handed Weyl index carry no invariant tensor, the
element `-1` negating a single Weyl index, and with them neither do the ranges of equivariant maps
out of such tensors (D). The Pauli matrices change `n` four-vector indices into `n` left- and `n`
right-handed Weyl indices, `pauliTensorMap`, injectively and equivariantly. For odd `n` the
invariants on the Weyl side are products of invariants of `n` left-handed indices, of which there
are none, so an odd number of four-vector indices carries no invariant tensor (E). The bispinor
classifications of `PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.Bispinors.MetricPairing` and the classification of
four four-vector indices in `PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.Tensors.ComplexTensor.Vector.ContractionTensor`
build on the same results.

## ii. Key results

- `complexLorentzTensor.complexifiedAction` : the action of `SL(2, ℂ) × SL(2, ℂ)` on the complex
  Lorentz tensors with Weyl colours.
- `Lorentz.SL2C.toComplexified` : the complexification `M ↦ (M, M̄)`.
- `complexLorentzTensor.complexifiedAction_comp_toComplexified` : restricted along it, the
  complexified action is the action of `SL(2, ℂ)`.
- `complexLorentzTensor.invariants_complexifiedAction_append` : on undotted indices followed by
  dotted ones, the complexified invariants are spanned by products of invariants.
- `complexLorentzTensor.invariants_complexifiedAction` : the two actions have the same invariant
  tensors.
- `complexLorentzTensor.invariants_append_eq_map₂_prodT` : the invariant tensors with undotted
  indices followed by dotted ones are spanned by products of invariants.
- `complexLorentzTensor.invariants_upL_upR_eq_bot` : a left- and a right-handed Weyl index carry
  no invariant tensor.
- `Lorentz.reducesInvariantsTo_bot_leftRight` : nor does the range of an equivariant map out of
  them or out of their duals.
- `complexLorentzTensor.pauliTensorMap` : the Pauli change of indices on tensors.
- `complexLorentzTensor.invariants_up_pow_eq_bot_of_odd` : an odd number of four-vector indices
  carries no invariant tensor.
- `Lorentz.ComplexVector.reducesInvariantsTo_bot_of_odd` : nor does the range of an equivariant
  map out of them.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The complexified action
  - A.1. The action of `SL(2, ℂ) × SL(2, ℂ)`
  - A.2. The restriction to `SL(2, ℂ)`
- B. Undotted indices followed by dotted ones
- C. The invariants of the two actions agree
  - C.1. The unipotent lines
  - C.2. The derivatives of the colours
  - C.3. The derivative argument
  - C.4. The invariants
- D. A left- and a right-handed Weyl index
  - D.1. The invariant tensors
  - D.2. The reduction to zero
  - D.3. Peeling the pair spans off a Lorentz-stable submodule
- E. Four-vector indices through the Pauli matrices
  - E.1. The Pauli change of indices on tensors
  - E.2. An odd number of four-vector indices

## iv. References

* R. F. Streater and A. S. Wightman, *PCT, Spin and Statistics, and All That*.

sections.text:
## A. The complexified action

### A.1. The action of `SL(2, ℂ) × SL(2, ℂ)`
### A.2. The restriction to `SL(2, ℂ)`
## B. Undotted indices followed by dotted ones

## C. The invariants of the two actions agree

### C.1. The unipotent lines

A square-zero matrix `G` with `det (1 + z G) = 1`, such as `E` or `F`, gives the line
`z ↦ 1 + z G` in `SL(2, ℂ)`, on which multiplication adds the parameters.

### C.2. The derivatives of the colours

Along `t ↦ 1 + c₀ t G`, for real `t` and real `G`, the matrix of an undotted colour is holomorphic
in `c₀ t` and that of a dotted colour antiholomorphic, so its derivative at the identity is `c₀`
times an undotted generator plus `c̄₀` times a dotted one. Along `t ↦ (1 + c₀ t G, 1)` the dotted
colours do not move.
### C.3. The derivative argument

### C.4. The invariants

`SL(2, ℂ)` is generated by the unipotent elements `1 + z E` and `1 + z F`, so an invariant tensor
with Weyl colours is fixed by `(M, 1)` for every `M`. It is fixed by `(M, M̄)`, being invariant,
and so by `(1, N) = (N̄, N) (N̄⁻¹, 1)` for every `N` as well.

## D. A left- and a right-handed Weyl index

### D.1. The invariant tensors

A tensor with a left- and a right-handed Weyl index is, by C, a combination of products of an
invariant tensor with one left-handed index and one with one right-handed index. The element `-1`
negates a single Weyl index, so there are none.

### D.2. The reduction to zero

The dual colours `![.downL, .downR]` are the two indices of `![.upL, .upR]` dualised in turn, so
they carry no invariant tensor but zero either (`invariants_tensorRep_eq_bot_of_dual`).

### D.3. Peeling the pair spans off a Lorentz-stable submodule

An equivariant map out of `ℂT[.downL, .downR]` carries no invariant, so the span of its
components, here the join of the lines through them, reduces to `⊥`. Each such span is stable under
the Lorentz group, so `ReducesInvariantsTo.biSup` combines the reductions over a finite family of
them, and a whole join is discarded from a Lorentz-stable submodule.

## E. Four-vector indices through the Pauli matrices

The Pauli matrices change each of `n` four-vector indices into a bispinor index, a left- and a
right-handed Weyl index (`Lorentz.pauliTransform`). Listing the `n` left-handed indices first and
then the `n` right-handed ones, this is an injective equivariant map `pauliTensorMap n` from the
tensors with `n` four-vector indices into the tensors with colours
`Fin.append (fun _ => .upL) (fun _ => .upR)` (E.1). By C the invariants of the latter are products
of invariants with `n` left-handed and with `n` right-handed indices. For odd `n` there are none,
the element `-1` negating an odd number of Weyl indices, and so the tensors with an odd number of
four-vector indices carry no invariant but zero (E.2).

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.complexifiedFactor
declarations.doc:
The factor of the complexified Lorentz group `SL(2, ℂ) × SL(2, ℂ)` under which a colour
transforms. The undotted colours `upL` and `downL` transform under the first factor `M`. The
dotted colours `upR` and `downR`, whose representations are conjugate, transform under the
conjugate of the second factor `N`, so that a dotted index transforms under `N` itself. The
vector colours, which carry an index of each kind, are not part of the construction, and are put
under the first factor only so that every colour has one.
declarations.statement: def complexifiedFactor : Color → SL(2,ℂ) × SL(2,ℂ) →* SL(2,ℂ)

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.complexifiedFactor_τ
declarations.doc: A colour and its dual transform under the same factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma complexifiedFactor_τ (k : Color) :
    complexifiedFactor (complexLorentzTensor.τ k) = complexifiedFactor k

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.complexifiedAction
declarations.doc:
The complexified Lorentz group `SL(2, ℂ) × SL(2, ℂ)` acting on the complex Lorentz tensors
with Weyl colours: `(M, N)` acts on an undotted index by `M`, on a dotted index by `N`, and on
their duals by the inverse transposes.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def complexifiedAction {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → Color) :
    Representation ℂ (SL(2,ℂ) × SL(2,ℂ)) ℂT(c)

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.complexifiedAction_apply
declarations.doc: An element of `SL(2, ℂ) × SL(2, ℂ)` acts on the index `i` through the factor of its colour.
declarations.statement:
lemma complexifiedAction_apply (g : SL(2,ℂ) × SL(2,ℂ)) :
    complexifiedAction c g =
      PiTensorProduct.map fun i => complexLorentzTensor.rep (c i) (complexifiedFactor (c i) g)

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.basis_repr_complexifiedAction
declarations.doc: The components of `g • t` under the complexified action.
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_repr_complexifiedAction (g : SL(2,ℂ) × SL(2,ℂ)) (t : ℂT(c))
    (φ : ComponentIdx (S := complexLorentzTensor) c) :
    (Tensor.basis c).repr (complexifiedAction c g t) φ = ∑ ψ, (∏ i, LinearMap.toMatrix
      (complexLorentzTensor.basis (c i)) (complexLorentzTensor.basis (c i))
      (complexLorentzTensor.rep (c i) (complexifiedFactor (c i) g)) (φ i) (ψ i)) *
      (Tensor.basis c).repr t ψ

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.complexifiedAction_prodT
declarations.doc: The complexified action acts on a product of tensors factor by factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma complexifiedAction_prodT {m : ℕ} {c1 : Fin m → Color} (g : SL(2,ℂ) × SL(2,ℂ)) (t : ℂT(c))
    (t1 : ℂT(c1)) :
    complexifiedAction (Fin.append c c1) g (prodT t t1) =
      prodT (complexifiedAction c g t) (complexifiedAction c1 g t1)

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.toComplexified
declarations.doc:
The complexification `M ↦ (M, M̄)` of `SL(2, ℂ)` into the complexified Lorentz group
`SL(2, ℂ) × SL(2, ℂ)`, with `M̄` the entrywise conjugate of `M`.
declarations.statement: def toComplexified : SL(2,ℂ) →* SL(2,ℂ) × SL(2,ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.toComplexified_apply
declarations.doc: The complexification of `M` is `(M, M̄)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toComplexified_apply (M : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    toComplexified M = (M, SpecialLinearGroup.map (starRingEnd ℂ) M)

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.map_starRingEnd_map_starRingEnd
declarations.doc: Conjugating an element of `SL(2, ℂ)` twice gives it back.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_starRingEnd_map_starRingEnd (M : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    SpecialLinearGroup.map (starRingEnd ℂ) (SpecialLinearGroup.map (starRingEnd ℂ) M) = M

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.complexifiedFactor_toComplexified
declarations.doc: Each colour transforms under `M` when restricted along `M ↦ (M, M̄)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma complexifiedFactor_toComplexified (k : Color) (M : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    complexifiedFactor k (toComplexified M) = M

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.complexifiedAction_toComplexified
declarations.doc: Restricted along `M ↦ (M, M̄)`, the complexified action is the action of `SL(2, ℂ)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma complexifiedAction_toComplexified (M : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    complexifiedAction c (toComplexified M) = complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep c M

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.complexifiedAction_comp_toComplexified
declarations.doc: Restricted along `M ↦ (M, M̄)`, the complexified action is the action of `SL(2, ℂ)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma complexifiedAction_comp_toComplexified :
    (complexifiedAction c).comp toComplexified = complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep c

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.complexifiedAction_eq_tensorRep_fst
declarations.doc: On undotted colours the complexified action of `(M, N)` is the action of `M`.
declarations.statement:
lemma complexifiedAction_eq_tensorRep_fst (hL : ∀ i, cL i = .upL ∨ cL i = .downL)
    (g : SL(2,ℂ) × SL(2,ℂ)) :
    complexifiedAction cL g = complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep cL g.1

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.complexifiedAction_eq_tensorRep_snd
declarations.doc:
On dotted colours the complexified action of `(M, N)` is the action of `N̄`, under which a
dotted index transforms by `N`.
declarations.statement:
lemma complexifiedAction_eq_tensorRep_snd (hR : ∀ i, cR i = .upR ∨ cR i = .downR)
    (g : SL(2,ℂ) × SL(2,ℂ)) :
    complexifiedAction cR g =
      complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep cR (SpecialLinearGroup.map (starRingEnd ℂ) g.2)

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.complexifiedAction_append_prodT
declarations.doc:
The complexified action on a product of a tensor with undotted indices and one with dotted
indices.
declarations.statement:
lemma complexifiedAction_append_prodT (hL : ∀ i, cL i = .upL ∨ cL i = .downL)
    (hR : ∀ i, cR i = .upR ∨ cR i = .downR) (g : SL(2,ℂ) × SL(2,ℂ)) (x : ℂT(cL)) (y : ℂT(cR)) :
    complexifiedAction (Fin.append cL cR) g (prodT x y) =
      prodT (complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep cL g.1 x)
        (complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep cR (SpecialLinearGroup.map (starRingEnd ℂ) g.2) y)

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.invariants_complexifiedAction_append
declarations.doc:
The invariants of the complexified action on undotted indices followed by dotted ones are
spanned by the products of an invariant tensor of the undotted indices and one of the dotted
indices. The Reynolds elements of the two factors, applied one after the other, fix an
invariant and send every product of tensors to a product of invariant tensors.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_complexifiedAction_append (hL : ∀ i, cL i = .upL ∨ cL i = .downL)
    (hR : ∀ i, cR i = .upR ∨ cR i = .downR) :
    (complexifiedAction (Fin.append cL cR)).invariants =
      Submodule.map₂ (prodT (S := complexLorentzTensor))
        (complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep cL).invariants
        (complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep cR).invariants

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.inv_one_add_smul
declarations.doc: For a square-zero matrix `G`, the inverse of `1 + z G` is `1 - z G`.
declarations.statement: lemma inv_one_add_smul (hGG : G * G = 0) (z : ℂ) : (1 + z • G)⁻¹ = 1 + (-z) • G

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.one_add_smul_mul_one_add_smul
declarations.doc: For a square-zero matrix `G`, multiplying `1 + a G` and `1 + b G` adds the parameters.
declarations.statement:
lemma one_add_smul_mul_one_add_smul (hGG : G * G = 0) (a b : ℂ) :
    (1 + a • G) * (1 + b • G) = 1 + (a + b) • G

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.unipotentLine
declarations.doc:
The element `1 + z G` of `SL(2, ℂ)`, for a matrix `G` with `det (1 + z G) = 1` for every
`z`, such as `E = !![0, 1; 0, 0]` or `F = !![0, 0; 1, 0]`.
declarations.statement: def unipotentLine (hG : ∀ z : ℂ, (1 + z • G).det = 1) (z : ℂ) : SL(2,ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.coe_unipotentLine
declarations.statement: lemma coe_unipotentLine (z : ℂ) : (unipotentLine hG z : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) = 1 + z • G

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.unipotentLine_zero
declarations.statement: lemma unipotentLine_zero : unipotentLine hG 0 = 1

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.unipotentLine_add
declarations.doc: For a square-zero `G`, multiplication on the line `z ↦ 1 + z G` adds the parameters.
declarations.statement:
lemma unipotentLine_add (hGG : G * G = 0) (a b : ℂ) :
    unipotentLine hG (a + b) = unipotentLine hG a * unipotentLine hG b

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.undottedGenerator
declarations.doc:
The derivative at the identity of the matrices of `t ↦ 1 + t G` on the undotted colours,
`G` on `upL` and `-Gᵀ` on `downL`, and zero on the other colours.
declarations.statement: def undottedGenerator (G : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) : (k : Color) → basisIdx k → basisIdx k → ℂ

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.dottedGenerator
declarations.doc:
The derivative at the identity of the matrices of `t ↦ 1 + t G`, for real `G`, on the dotted
colours, `G` on `upR` and `-Gᵀ` on `downR`, and zero on the other colours.
declarations.statement: def dottedGenerator (G : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) : (k : Color) → basisIdx k → basisIdx k → ℂ

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.mul_eq_mul_add_star_mul_zero
declarations.doc: The derivative on `upL`, written against the two generators.
declarations.statement: lemma mul_eq_mul_add_star_mul_zero (c₀ x : ℂ) : c₀ * x = c₀ * x + star c₀ * 0

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.neg_mul_eq_mul_neg_add_star_mul_zero
declarations.doc: The derivative on `downL`, written against the two generators.
declarations.statement: lemma neg_mul_eq_mul_neg_add_star_mul_zero (c₀ x : ℂ) : -c₀ * x = c₀ * -x + star c₀ * 0

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.star_mul_eq_mul_zero_add_star_mul
declarations.doc: The derivative on `upR`, written against the two generators.
declarations.statement:
lemma star_mul_eq_mul_zero_add_star_mul {x : ℂ} (hx : star x = x) (c₀ : ℂ) :
    star (c₀ * x) = c₀ * 0 + star c₀ * x

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.star_neg_mul_eq_mul_zero_add_star_mul_neg
declarations.doc: The derivative on `downR`, written against the two generators.
declarations.statement:
lemma star_neg_mul_eq_mul_zero_add_star_mul_neg {x : ℂ} (hx : star x = x) (c₀ : ℂ) :
    star (-c₀ * x) = c₀ * 0 + star c₀ * -x

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.toMatrix_rep_one_add_smul_zero
declarations.doc:
At the identity of the line `t ↦ 1 + c₀ t G` the matrix of every colour is the unit
matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrix_rep_one_add_smul_zero (k : Color) (c₀ : ℂ) (p q : basisIdx k) :
    LinearMap.toMatrix (complexLorentzTensor.basis k) (complexLorentzTensor.basis k)
      (complexLorentzTensor.rep k (unipotentLine hG (c₀ * ((0 : ℝ) : ℂ)))) p q =
      if p = q then 1 else 0

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.toMatrix_rep_complexifiedFactor_zero
declarations.doc:
At the identity of the line `t ↦ (1 + c₀ t G, 1)` the matrix of every colour under the
complexified action is the unit matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrix_rep_complexifiedFactor_zero (k : Color) (c₀ : ℂ) (p q : basisIdx k) :
    LinearMap.toMatrix (complexLorentzTensor.basis k) (complexLorentzTensor.basis k)
      (complexLorentzTensor.rep k
        (complexifiedFactor k (unipotentLine hG (c₀ * ((0 : ℝ) : ℂ)), 1))) p q =
      if p = q then 1 else 0

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.hasDerivAt_toMatrix_rep_one_add_smul
declarations.doc:
Along the line `t ↦ 1 + c₀ t G` of `SL(2, ℂ)`, for a real square-zero `G`, the matrix of a
Weyl colour has derivative `c₀` times its undotted generator plus `c̄₀` times its dotted
generator at the identity.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_toMatrix_rep_one_add_smul {k : Color} (hk : k ≠ .up ∧ k ≠ .down) (c₀ : ℂ)
    (p q : basisIdx k) :
    HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => LinearMap.toMatrix (complexLorentzTensor.basis k)
      (complexLorentzTensor.basis k) (complexLorentzTensor.rep k (unipotentLine hG (c₀ * t))) p q)
      (c₀ * undottedGenerator G k p q + star c₀ * dottedGenerator G k p q) 0

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.hasDerivAt_toMatrix_rep_complexifiedFactor
declarations.doc:
Along the line `t ↦ (1 + c₀ t G, 1)` of the complexified Lorentz group, the matrix of a Weyl
colour under the complexified action has derivative `c₀` times its undotted generator at the
identity: the dotted colours transform under the second factor, which stays at the
identity.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_toMatrix_rep_complexifiedFactor {k : Color} (hk : k ≠ .up ∧ k ≠ .down)
    (c₀ : ℂ) (p q : basisIdx k) :
    HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => LinearMap.toMatrix (complexLorentzTensor.basis k)
      (complexLorentzTensor.basis k)
      (complexLorentzTensor.rep k (complexifiedFactor k (unipotentLine hG (c₀ * t), 1))) p q)
      (c₀ * undottedGenerator G k p q) 0

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.sum_undottedGenerator_mul_repr_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
An invariant tensor with Weyl colours is killed by the undotted generator acting on its
undotted indices, one at a time. Along the line `t ↦ 1 + c₀ t G` its components are constant,
and their derivative is `c₀` times this action plus `c̄₀` times that on the dotted indices.
Taking `c₀ = 1` and `c₀ = i` separates the two.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_undottedGenerator_mul_repr_eq_zero {t : ℂT(c)}
    (ht : t ∈ (complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep c).invariants)
    (φ : ComponentIdx (S := complexLorentzTensor) c) :
    ∑ s, ∑ q, undottedGenerator G (c s) (φ s) q *
      (Tensor.basis c).repr t (Function.update φ s q) = 0

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.complexifiedAction_one_add_smul_one
declarations.doc:
An invariant tensor with Weyl colours is fixed by `(1 + z G, 1)` under the complexified
action. Along `s ↦ (1 + s z G, 1)` the derivative of its components at the identity is `z` times
the undotted generator acting on them, which vanishes, so by the group law they are constant.

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.complexifiedAction_mk_one_apply
declarations.doc: An invariant tensor with Weyl colours is fixed by `(M, 1)` under the complexified action.

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.invariants_complexifiedAction
declarations.doc:
The invariant tensors with Weyl colours are the same for `SL(2, ℂ)` and for the complexified
Lorentz group `SL(2, ℂ) × SL(2, ℂ)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_complexifiedAction (hc : ∀ i, c i ≠ .up ∧ c i ≠ .down) :
    (complexifiedAction c).invariants = (complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep c).invariants

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.invariants_append_eq_map₂_prodT
declarations.doc:
The invariant tensors with undotted indices followed by dotted ones are spanned by the
products of an invariant tensor of the undotted indices and one of the dotted indices.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_append_eq_map₂_prodT (hL : ∀ i, cL i = .upL ∨ cL i = .downL)
    (hR : ∀ i, cR i = .upR ∨ cR i = .downR) :
    (complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep (Fin.append cL cR)).invariants =
      Submodule.map₂ (prodT (S := complexLorentzTensor))
        (complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep cL).invariants
        (complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep cR).invariants

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.invariants_upL_upR_eq_bot
declarations.doc: The only invariant tensor with a left- and a right-handed Weyl index is zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_upL_upR_eq_bot :
    (complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep ![.upL, .upR]).invariants = ⊥

declarations.name: Lorentz.reducesInvariantsTo_bot_leftRight
declarations.doc:
The invariants of the range of an equivariant map out of the tensors with a left- and a
right-handed Weyl index, or with their duals, reduce to `⊥`. A Lorentz invariant of
`LinearMap.range f ⊔ S`, for `S` a Lorentz-stable submodule, lies in `S`.

declarations.name: Lorentz.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_biSup_dualLeftRightWeyl_span
declarations.doc:
A finite join of the spans of families with a dual left- and a dual right-handed Weyl index
carries no Lorentz invariant modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule. Such a family has no invariant,
so each span reduces to `⊥`, and `ReducesInvariantsTo.biSup` combines the reductions. A Lorentz
invariant of the join together with `S` lies in `S`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_lorentz_invariant_biSup_dualLeftRightWeyl_span {ι : Type} [DecidableEq ι]
    {T : ι → Fin 2 × Fin 2 → B} (hT : ∀ i, complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant ![.downL, .downR]
      repLorentz (liftComponents (T i ∘ pairIdx)))
    (S : Submodule ℂ B) (hS : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) (s : Finset ι)
    {x : B} (hx : x ∈ (⨆ i ∈ s, ⨆ l, ℂ ∙ T i l) ⊔ S)
    (hinv : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: Lorentz.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_iSup_dualLeftRightWeyl_span
declarations.doc:
The version of `mem_of_lorentz_invariant_biSup_dualLeftRightWeyl_span` joining over a
whole finite index type.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_lorentz_invariant_iSup_dualLeftRightWeyl_span {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    [DecidableEq ι] {T : ι → Fin 2 × Fin 2 → B}
    (hT : ∀ i, complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant ![.downL, .downR] repLorentz
      (liftComponents (T i ∘ pairIdx))) (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hS : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) {x : B}
    (hx : x ∈ (⨆ i, ⨆ l, ℂ ∙ T i l) ⊔ S)
    (hinv : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.bispinorIdx
declarations.doc:
The component indices of a tensor with `n` left-handed Weyl indices followed by `n`
right-handed ones, as `n` bispinor indices, the `s`-th left-handed index paired with the `s`-th
right-handed one.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def bispinorIdx (n : ℕ) : ComponentIdx (S := complexLorentzTensor)
    (Fin.append (fun _ : Fin n => Color.upL) (fun _ : Fin n => Color.upR)) ≃
      (Fin n → Fin 2 × Fin 2)

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.toMatrix_rep_basisIdxCongr
declarations.doc: The matrix entry of a colour, transported along an equality of colours.
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrix_rep_basisIdxCongr {k k' : Color} (h : k = k') (g : SL(2,ℂ)) (x y : basisIdx k) :
    LinearMap.toMatrix (complexLorentzTensor.basis k) (complexLorentzTensor.basis k)
      (complexLorentzTensor.rep k g) x y =
    LinearMap.toMatrix (complexLorentzTensor.basis k') (complexLorentzTensor.basis k')
      (complexLorentzTensor.rep k' g) (basisIdxCongr h x) (basisIdxCongr h y)

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.prod_bispinorMatrix_bispinorIdx
declarations.doc:
On `n` bispinor indices, the product of the matrix entries of `g` over the `2 n` Weyl indices
is the product of the entries of the bispinor matrix of `g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma prod_bispinorMatrix_bispinorIdx (n : ℕ) (g : SL(2,ℂ))
    (φ ψ : ComponentIdx (S := complexLorentzTensor)
      (Fin.append (fun _ : Fin n => Color.upL) (fun _ : Fin n => Color.upR))) :
    ∏ s, bispinorMatrix g (bispinorIdx n φ s) (bispinorIdx n ψ s) =
      ∏ i, LinearMap.toMatrix
        (complexLorentzTensor.basis (Fin.append (fun _ : Fin n => Color.upL) (fun _ => .upR) i))
        (complexLorentzTensor.basis (Fin.append (fun _ : Fin n => Color.upL) (fun _ => .upR) i))
        (complexLorentzTensor.rep (Fin.append (fun _ : Fin n => Color.upL) (fun _ => .upR) i) g)
        (φ i) (ψ i)

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.pauliTensorMap
declarations.doc:
The change of every four-vector index of a tensor into a bispinor index by the covariant
Pauli matrices, `μ ↦ (σ_μ)_{αα̇}`, landing in the tensors with the left-handed Weyl indices of
the bispinor indices followed by their right-handed ones.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pauliTensorMap (n : ℕ) : ℂT(fun _ : Fin n => Color.up) →ₗ[ℂ]
    ℂT(Fin.append (fun _ : Fin n => Color.upL) (fun _ : Fin n => Color.upR))

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.pauliTensorMap_smul
declarations.doc: The Pauli change of indices commutes with `SL(2, ℂ)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma pauliTensorMap_smul (n : ℕ) (g : SL(2,ℂ)) (t : ℂT(fun _ : Fin n => Color.up)) :
    pauliTensorMap n (g • t) = g • pauliTensorMap n t

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.pauliTensorMap_injective
declarations.doc: The Pauli change of indices is injective.
declarations.statement: lemma pauliTensorMap_injective (n : ℕ) : Function.Injective (pauliTensorMap n)

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.pauliTensorMap_mem_invariants
declarations.doc: The Pauli change of indices maps invariant tensors to invariant tensors.
declarations.statement:
lemma pauliTensorMap_mem_invariants {n : ℕ} {t : ℂT(fun _ : Fin n => Color.up)}
    (ht : t ∈ (complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep (fun _ : Fin n => Color.up)).invariants) :
    pauliTensorMap n t ∈ (complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep
      (Fin.append (fun _ : Fin n => Color.upL) (fun _ : Fin n => Color.upR))).invariants

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.invariants_up_pow_eq_bot_of_odd
declarations.doc:
There are no invariant tensors with an odd number of four-vector indices but zero. The Pauli
change of indices sends them injectively to invariant tensors with `n` left- and `n`
right-handed Weyl indices, products of invariants with `n` left-handed indices, of which there
are none for odd `n`, the element `-1` negating them.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_up_pow_eq_bot_of_odd {n : ℕ} (hn : Odd n) :
    (complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep (fun _ : Fin n => Color.up)).invariants = ⊥

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector.reducesInvariantsTo_bot_of_odd
declarations.doc:
The range of an equivariant map out of the tensors with an odd number of four-vector indices
reduces to `⊥`. A Lorentz invariant of `LinearMap.range f ⊔ S`, for `S` a Lorentz-stable
submodule, lies in `S`.
declarations.statement:
lemma ComplexVector.reducesInvariantsTo_bot_of_odd {B : Type*} [AddCommGroup B]
    [Module ℂ B] {repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) B} {n : ℕ} (hn : Odd n)
    {f : ℂT(fun _ : Fin n => Color.up) →ₗ[ℂ] B}
    (hf : complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant (fun _ : Fin n => .up) repLorentz f) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (fun g : SL(2,ℂ) => repLorentz g) (LinearMap.range f) ⊥

modules.title: The metric pairings of bispinor indices
modules.doc:
The invariant tensors with left-handed Weyl indices followed by as many right-handed ones are the
products of Weyl metric pairings of each chirality.

## i. Overview

By `complexLorentzTensor.invariants_append_eq_map₂_prodT` the invariant tensors with undotted
indices followed by dotted ones are spanned by the products of an invariant tensor of the undotted
indices and one of the dotted indices. With two left-handed and two right-handed indices the
factors are the metrics `ε` and `ε̄`, so the invariant tensors are the line through `ε ⊗ ε̄` (A).
With four of each they are the two products of metrics of each chirality, so the invariant tensors
are the span of the four products `bispinorPairingTensor`, `ε ε ⊗ ε̄ ε̄` (B). The latter is what
the classification of the invariants of four four-vector indices uses, through the Pauli matrices.

On coefficient functions, the Pauli change of indices sends the Minkowski metric to `2 ε ⊗ ε̄`,
the Fierz identity, matching the single invariant of two four-vector indices with that of two
bispinor indices (C).

## ii. Key results

- `complexLorentzTensor.invariants_upL_upL_upR_upR_eq_span_bispinorMetric` : the invariant tensors
  with two left- and then two right-handed Weyl indices.
- `complexLorentzTensor.invariants_upL_pow_four_upR_pow_four_eq_span_range_bispinorPairing` : the
  invariant tensors with four left- and then four right-handed Weyl indices.
- `Lorentz.pauliTransform_minkowskiMatrix` : the Pauli change sends the Minkowski metric to
  `2 ε ⊗ ε̄`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Two left- and two right-handed Weyl indices
- B. Four left- and four right-handed Weyl indices
- C. The Fierz identity

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Two left- and two right-handed Weyl indices

## C. The Fierz identity

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.bispinorMetricTensor
declarations.doc:
The tensor `ε ⊗ ε̄` with two left-handed and then two right-handed Weyl indices, the product of
the metrics of the two chiralities.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def bispinorMetricTensor : ℂT(Fin.append ![Color.upL, .upL] ![Color.upR, .upR])

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.invariants_upL_upL_upR_upR_eq_span_bispinorMetric
declarations.doc:
The invariant tensors with two left-handed and then two right-handed Weyl indices are the line
through `ε ⊗ ε̄`.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_upL_upL_upR_upR_eq_span_bispinorMetric :
    (complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep (Fin.append ![Color.upL, .upL] ![Color.upR, .upR])).invariants =
      ℂ ∙ bispinorMetricTensor

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.bispinorPairingTensor
declarations.doc:
The four products `ε ε ⊗ ε̄ ε̄` of a pairing of four left-handed Weyl indices and one of four
right-handed ones, as tensors with the left-handed indices first.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def bispinorPairingTensor (ij : Fin 2 × Fin 2) :
    ℂT(Fin.append (fun _ : Fin 4 => Color.upL) (fun _ : Fin 4 => Color.upR))

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.invariants_upL_pow_four_upR_pow_four_eq_span_range_bispinorPairing
declarations.doc:
The invariant tensors with four left-handed and then four right-handed Weyl indices are the
span of the four products of pairings `ε ε ⊗ ε̄ ε̄`.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_upL_pow_four_upR_pow_four_eq_span_range_bispinorPairing :
    (complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep
      (Fin.append (fun _ : Fin 4 => Color.upL) (fun _ : Fin 4 => Color.upR))).invariants =
      Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range bispinorPairingTensor)

declarations.name: Lorentz.bispinorMetric
declarations.doc:
The product `ε_{α₀α₁} ε_{α̇₀α̇₁}` of the Weyl metrics of the two chiralities on two bispinor
indices.
declarations.statement: def bispinorMetric (α : Fin 2 → Fin 2 × Fin 2) : ℂ

declarations.name: Lorentz.pauliTransform_minkowskiMatrix
declarations.doc:
Through the Pauli matrices the Minkowski metric is twice `ε ⊗ ε̄`, the Fierz identity
`η^{μν} (σ_μ)_{αα̇} (σ_ν)_{ββ̇} = 2 ε_{αβ} ε_{α̇β̇}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma pauliTransform_minkowskiMatrix :
    pauliTransform (fun d : Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 => ((minkowskiMatrixZ (d 0) (d 1) : ℤ) : ℂ))
      = (2 : ℂ) • bispinorMetric

modules.title: The Pauli tensor is the unique invariant
modules.doc:
Up to scale, the Pauli tensor `σ^{μ α α̇}` is the only invariant with a vector, a left-handed and a
right-handed Weyl index.

## i. Overview

The covariant Pauli matrices `σ_μ = η_{μμ} σ^μ` move under `M ∈ SL(2, ℂ)` as a covariant vector,
`M σ_μ Mᴴ = Σ_ν Λ_{ν μ} σ_ν`, so `e_μ ↦ σ_μ` is an equivariant linear map `contrToLeftRight`
from the complex four-vectors to `LeftHandedWeyl ⊗ RightHandedWeyl` (A). By the Fierz completeness
relation the `σ_μ` span all `2 × 2` matrices, so this map is onto. Applied to the second index of
the metric `η^{μν}` it gives the Pauli tensor `pauliVal`, the two lowerings cancelling (B).

The map `contrToLeftRight` is onto between spaces of dimension four, so it is bijective, and so
is `id ⊗ contrToLeftRight`. It carries the invariants of `ComplexVector ⊗ ComplexVector`, the line
through the metric, onto those of `ComplexVector ⊗ (LeftHandedWeyl ⊗ RightHandedWeyl)`, which are
therefore the line through `σ` (C). The tensor product is tensorial, so section D restates this
for the tensor `toTensor pauliVal`, relabelled as the tensor `pauliTensor` of
`ℂT[.up, .upL, .upR]`, the line through which is the invariant tensors with a four-vector and a
left-right Weyl pair of indices, and for its dual-Weyl form in `ℂT[.up, .downR, .downL]`. It then
applies this to equivariant maps out of these tensors, the shape of the fermion kinetic term.

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.ComplexVector.contrToLeftRight` : the equivariant map `e_μ ↦ σ_μ`.
- `Lorentz.ComplexVector.lTensor_contrToLeftRight_metricVal` : it carries the metric to the Pauli
  tensor.
- `Lorentz.ComplexVector.invariants_tprod_eq_span_pauliVal` : the invariants are the line through
  the Pauli tensor.
- `Lorentz.pauliTensor` : the Pauli tensor as a tensor of `ℂT[.up, .upL, .upR]`.
- `complexLorentzTensor.invariants_up_upL_upR_eq_span_pauli` : the invariant tensors with the
  indices of the Pauli tensor are the line through `pauliTensor`.
- `Lorentz.invariantReductionToPauliVal`, `Lorentz.invariantReductionToPauliValDualWeyl` : the
  invariants of the range of an equivariant map reduce to the image of the Pauli tensor.
- `Lorentz.isEquivariant_upDownRDownL_mul` : a one-index family times a once-derived one of the
  other chirality is an equivariant map out of `ℂT[.up, .downR, .downL]`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Pauli matrices as an equivariant map
- B. The metric goes to the Pauli tensor
- C. The Pauli tensor is the unique invariant
- D. The Pauli tensor as a complex Lorentz tensor
  - D.1. The invariant tensors
  - D.2. Dual Weyl indices
  - D.3. Maps from dual components
  - D.4. Once-derived one-index Weyl families and their products

## iv. References

The Pauli tensor `ComplexVector.pauliVal` and the intertwining map `ComplexVector.pauli` are in
`Physlib.Relativity.Bispinors.Pauli.Basic`, where sections A to C are written to move. The
uniqueness of the metric of the complex four-vectors is in
`PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.Tensors.ComplexTensor.Metrics.Pre`. The tensorial structures of the
three factors are in `PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.Tensors.ComplexTensor.Vector.Tensorial` and
`PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.Fermions.Weyl.Tensorial`.

sections.text: ## A. The Pauli matrices as an equivariant map
## B. The metric goes to the Pauli tensor
## C. The Pauli tensor is the unique invariant

## D. The Pauli tensor as a complex Lorentz tensor

Complex four-vectors and Weyl fermions are tensorial, so
`ComplexVector ⊗ (LeftHandedWeyl ⊗ RightHandedWeyl)` is tensorial through
`TensorSpecies.Tensorial.prod`. Its tensors carry the indices
`Fin.append ![.up] (Fin.append ![.upL] ![.upR])`, and the Pauli tensor is the tensor
`toTensor pauliVal`. The equivalence `toTensor` carries the action of `SL(2, ℂ)` on the tensor
product to the action on tensors, so the invariant tensors are the line through
`toTensor pauliVal`. Relabelling the colours as the plain list `![.up, .upL, .upR]`
(`isReindexing_append_three`), the invariant tensors of `ℂT[.up, .upL, .upR]` are the line
through the relabelled tensor `pauliTensor`. For an equivariant map `f` out of these tensors every
Lorentz invariant in the range of `f` is then a multiple of `f pauliTensor`, modulo a
Lorentz-stable submodule, `invariantReductionToPauliVal` (D.1).

The Standard Model's fermion symbols are `Module.Dual`-valued, so their spinor indices are dual
Weyl indices, and a family of them is an equivariant map out of `ℂT[.up, .downR, .downL]`.
Dualising both Weyl indices, `dualWeylMap`, is an equivariant surjection onto these tensors, so
every invariant in the range of such a map `f` is a multiple of
`f (dualWeylMap pauliTensor)`, the image of the Pauli tensor with dual Weyl indices (D.2).
A family indexed by a four-vector, a dual left-handed and a dual right-handed Weyl index is
relabelled by `dualIndexEquiv`, and its map is equivariant when it obeys the transformation law
of these indices (D.3). A one-index Weyl family times a once-derived one of the other chirality
is such a family, the shape of the fermion kinetic term (D.4).
### D.1. The invariant tensors

### D.2. Dual Weyl indices

A family `T^μ{}_{α' α}` with a four-vector index and a dual right- and a dual left-handed Weyl
index is an equivariant map out of `ℂT[.up, .downR, .downL]`. Dualising both Weyl indices,
`dualWeylMap`, is an equivariant surjection onto these tensors from the tensors with the indices
of the Pauli tensor. Composing with it gives an equivariant map with the same range out of the
latter, and section D.1 applies.

### D.3. Maps from dual components

A family `T (μ, α, α')` of vectors, indexed by a four-vector index, a dual left-handed and a
dual right-handed Weyl index, is relabelled by `dualIndexEquiv`, and its map
`liftComponents (T ∘ dualIndexEquiv)` sends `e_μ ⊗ e_α' ⊗ e_α` to `T (μ, α, α')`. It is
equivariant when the vectors are moved as the basis tensors are.

### D.4. Once-derived one-index Weyl families and their products

A once-derived fermion symbol carries a four-vector index, from the derivative, besides its
spinor index. The derivative slot moves by the columns of the Lorentz matrix and the spinor
slot by the contragredient of the Weyl representation of its chirality, conjugated for the
dotted one. Only the value index of a fermion symbol is dualised, so the derivative slot keeps the
plain Lorentz law. A one-index family of one chirality times a once-derived family of the other
is an equivariant map out of `ℂT[.up, .downR, .downL]`, in either order.

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector.contrToLeftRightLinear
declarations.doc:
The covariant Pauli matrices as a map `e_μ ↦ σ_μ` from complex four-vectors to a left- and a
right-handed Weyl index.
declarations.statement: def contrToLeftRightLinear : ComplexVector →ₗ[ℂ] LeftHandedWeyl ⊗[ℂ] RightHandedWeyl

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector.contrToLeftRightLinear_basis
declarations.doc: The basis vector `e_μ` is sent to the lowered Pauli matrix `σ_μ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma contrToLeftRightLinear_basis (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    contrToLeftRightLinear (ComplexVector.basis μ) = leftRightToMatrix.symm (pauliLower μ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector.contrToLeftRightLinear_rep
declarations.doc: The covariant Pauli matrices move as a covariant vector, so `e_μ ↦ σ_μ` is equivariant.
declarations.statement:
lemma contrToLeftRightLinear_rep (M : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : ComplexVector) :
    contrToLeftRightLinear (ComplexVector.SL2CRep M v) =
      TensorProduct.map (LeftHandedWeyl.rep M) (RightHandedWeyl.rep M)
        (contrToLeftRightLinear v)

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector.contrToLeftRight
declarations.doc:
The covariant Pauli matrices as an intertwining map `e_μ ↦ σ_μ` from complex four-vectors to
a left- and a right-handed Weyl index.
declarations.statement:
def contrToLeftRight :
    ComplexVector.SL2CRep.IntertwiningMap (LeftHandedWeyl.rep.tprod RightHandedWeyl.rep)

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector.contrToLeftRight_basis
declarations.doc: The basis vector `e_μ` is sent to the lowered Pauli matrix `σ_μ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma contrToLeftRight_basis (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    contrToLeftRight (ComplexVector.basis μ) = leftRightToMatrix.symm (pauliLower μ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector.contrToLeftRight_surjective
declarations.doc:
The covariant Pauli matrices span the `2 × 2` matrices, by the Fierz completeness relation,
so `e_μ ↦ σ_μ` is onto.
declarations.statement: lemma contrToLeftRight_surjective : Function.Surjective contrToLeftRight

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector.lTensor_contrToLeftRight_metricVal
declarations.doc:
Applying `e_μ ↦ σ_μ` to the second index of the metric `η^{μν}` gives the Pauli tensor. The
lowering in `σ_μ` cancels the metric.
declarations.statement:
lemma lTensor_contrToLeftRight_metricVal :
    contrToLeftRight.lTensor ComplexVector.SL2CRep ComplexVector.metricVal =
      ComplexVector.pauliVal

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector.contrToLeftRight_bijective
declarations.doc: The map `e_μ ↦ σ_μ` is bijective: it is onto, between spaces of dimension four.
declarations.statement: lemma contrToLeftRight_bijective : Function.Bijective contrToLeftRight

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector.invariants_tprod_eq_span_pauliVal
declarations.doc:
The `SL(2,ℂ)`-invariants of `ComplexVector ⊗ (LeftHandedWeyl ⊗ RightHandedWeyl)` are the line
through the Pauli tensor `σ^{μ α α̇}`. The bijection `id ⊗ contrToLeftRight` carries the
invariants of `ComplexVector ⊗ ComplexVector`, the line through the metric, onto them.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_tprod_eq_span_pauliVal :
    (ComplexVector.SL2CRep.tprod (LeftHandedWeyl.rep.tprod RightHandedWeyl.rep)).invariants =
      ℂ ∙ ComplexVector.pauliVal

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector.toTensor_SL2CRep_tprod
declarations.doc:
The equivalence `toTensor` carries the action of `SL(2, ℂ)` on
`ComplexVector ⊗ (LeftHandedWeyl ⊗ RightHandedWeyl)` to the action on tensors.
declarations.statement:
lemma ComplexVector.toTensor_SL2CRep_tprod (g : SL(2,ℂ))
    (x : ComplexVector ⊗[ℂ] (LeftHandedWeyl ⊗[ℂ] RightHandedWeyl)) :
    toTensor ((ComplexVector.SL2CRep.tprod (LeftHandedWeyl.rep.tprod RightHandedWeyl.rep)) g x)
      = g • toTensor x

declarations.name: Lorentz.pauliTensor
declarations.doc:
The Pauli tensor `σ^{μ α α̇}` as a tensor of `ℂT[.up, .upL, .upR]`, the tensor
`toTensor pauliVal` with its colours `Fin.append ![.up] (Fin.append ![.upL] ![.upR])` relabelled
as the plain list.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def pauliTensor : ℂT[.up, .upL, .upR]

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.invariants_up_upL_upR_eq_span_pauli
declarations.doc:
The invariant tensors with a four-vector index and a left-right Weyl pair are the line
through the Pauli tensor. The equivalence `toTensor` carries the invariants of the tensor
product, the line through `pauliVal`, onto the invariant tensors of the colours of the
tensorial structure, and relabelling the colours carries these onto those of the plain list.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.complexLorentzTensor.invariants_up_upL_upR_eq_span_pauli :
    (complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep ![.up, .upL, .upR]).invariants = ℂ ∙ pauliTensor

declarations.name: Lorentz.invariantReductionToPauliVal
declarations.doc:
For an equivariant map `f` out of the tensors with the indices of the Pauli tensor, the
Lorentz invariants of the range of `f` reduce to the span of the image `f pauliTensor` of the
Pauli tensor.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def invariantReductionToPauliVal {B : Type*} [AddCommGroup B] [Module ℂ B]
    {repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) B} {f : ℂT[.up, .upL, .upR] →ₗ[ℂ] B}
    (hf : complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant ![.up, .upL, .upR] repLorentz f) :
    InvariantReductionToSpan (fun g : SL(2,ℂ) => repLorentz g) (LinearMap.range f)

declarations.name: Lorentz.dualWeylMap
declarations.doc:
Dualising the two Weyl indices of a tensor with the indices of the Pauli tensor, the dual
indices listed in the order of `ℂT[.up, .downR, .downL]`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def dualWeylMap : ℂT[.up, .upL, .upR] →ₗ[ℂ] ℂT[.up, .downR, .downL]

declarations.name: Lorentz.dualWeylMap_equivariant
declarations.doc: Dualising the Weyl indices commutes with the action of `SL(2,ℂ)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma dualWeylMap_equivariant (g : SL(2,ℂ)) (t : ℂT[.up, .upL, .upR]) :
    dualWeylMap (g • t) = g • dualWeylMap t

declarations.name: Lorentz.dualWeylMap_surjective
declarations.doc:
Dualising the Weyl indices is surjective. The dualisations are inverted by raising the
indices again, and the relabelling by its inverse.
declarations.statement: lemma dualWeylMap_surjective : Function.Surjective dualWeylMap

declarations.name: Lorentz.isEquivariant_comp_dualWeylMap
declarations.doc:
Composing with the dualisation of the Weyl indices gives an equivariant map out of the
tensors with the indices of the Pauli tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_comp_dualWeylMap :
    complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant ![.up, .upL, .upR] repLorentz (f ∘ₗ dualWeylMap)

declarations.name: Lorentz.range_comp_dualWeylMap
declarations.doc: Composing with the dualisation of the Weyl indices does not change the range.
declarations.statement: lemma range_comp_dualWeylMap : LinearMap.range (f ∘ₗ dualWeylMap) = LinearMap.range f

declarations.name: Lorentz.invariantReductionToPauliValDualWeyl
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz invariants of the range of `f` reduce to the span of the image
`f (dualWeylMap pauliTensor)` of the Pauli tensor with dual Weyl indices, the kinetic term of a
Weyl fermion.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def invariantReductionToPauliValDualWeyl :
    InvariantReductionToSpan (fun g : SL(2,ℂ) => repLorentz g) (LinearMap.range f)

declarations.name: Lorentz.dualIndexEquiv
declarations.doc:
The component indices of a tensor of `ℂT[.up, .downR, .downL]`, as a four-vector index, a
dual left-handed and a dual right-handed Weyl index.
declarations.statement:
def dualIndexEquiv : ComponentIdx (S := complexLorentzTensor) ![.up, .downR, .downL] ≃
    (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × Fin 2 × Fin 2

declarations.name: Lorentz.isEquivariant_liftComponents_upDownRDownL
declarations.doc:
The map of a family relabelled by `dualIndexEquiv` is equivariant when `T (μ, α, α')` is moved
as `T^μ{}_{α α'}`, the vector index by the Lorentz matrix, the dual left index by `(g⁻¹)ᵀ` and
the dual right index by `(g⁻¹)ᴴ`, the summed index first in each factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_liftComponents_upDownRDownL
    {repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) B} (T : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × Fin 2 × Fin 2 → B)
    (hT : ∀ (g : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (l : Fin 2 × Fin 2),
      repLorentz g (T (μ, l)) = ∑ (ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3), ∑ (a : Fin 2 × Fin 2),
        ((((SL2C.toLorentzGroup g).1 ν μ : ℝ) : ℂ)
          * ((g.1⁻¹)ᵀ a.1 l.1 * (g.1⁻¹)ᴴ a.2 l.2)) • T (ν, a)) :
    complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant ![.up, .downR, .downL] repLorentz
      (liftComponents (T ∘ dualIndexEquiv))

declarations.name: Lorentz.invariantReductionToPauliValDualWeylOfComponents
declarations.doc:
For a family whose map is equivariant, the Lorentz invariants of the span of the family
reduce to the span of the image under `liftComponents (T ∘ dualIndexEquiv)` of the Pauli tensor
with dual Weyl indices, `dualWeylMap pauliTensor`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def invariantReductionToPauliValDualWeylOfComponents
    {repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) B} {T : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) × Fin 2 × Fin 2 → B}
    (hT : complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant ![.up, .downR, .downL] repLorentz
      (liftComponents (T ∘ dualIndexEquiv))) :
    InvariantReductionToSpan (fun g : SL(2,ℂ) => repLorentz g)
      (Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range T))

declarations.name: Lorentz.isEquivariant_upDownRDownL_mul
declarations.doc:
An undotted family times a once-derived dotted one is an equivariant map out of
`ℂT[.up, .downR, .downL]`, the derivative supplying the four-vector index.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_upDownRDownL_mul {X : Fin 2 → B} {Y : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Fin 2 → B}
    (hX : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (a : Fin 2), repLorentz Λ (X a) = ∑ β, (Λ⁻¹).1 a β • X β)
    (hY : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : Fin 2), repLorentz Λ (Y μ a)
      = ∑ ν, ∑ β, ((((SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 ν μ : ℝ) : ℂ) * star ((Λ⁻¹).1 a β)) • Y ν β) :
    complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant ![.up, .downR, .downL] repLorentz
      (liftComponents ((fun p => X p.2.1 * Y p.1 p.2.2) ∘ dualIndexEquiv))

declarations.name: Lorentz.isEquivariant_upDownRDownL_mul_swap
declarations.doc:
A dotted family times a once-derived undotted one is an equivariant map out of
`ℂT[.up, .downR, .downL]`, the two spinor slots exchanged.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_upDownRDownL_mul_swap {X : Fin 2 → B} {Y : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Fin 2 → B}
    (hX : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (a : Fin 2), repLorentz Λ (X a) = ∑ β, star ((Λ⁻¹).1 a β) • X β)
    (hY : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : Fin 2), repLorentz Λ (Y μ a)
      = ∑ ν, ∑ β, ((((SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 ν μ : ℝ) : ℂ) * (Λ⁻¹).1 a β) • Y ν β) :
    complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant ![.up, .downR, .downL] repLorentz
      (liftComponents ((fun p => X p.2.2 * Y p.1 p.2.1) ∘ dualIndexEquiv))

modules.title: Light cones in time and space
modules.doc:
Causal future and past of sets in time and space and in Minkowski spacetime.

## i. Overview

Causal future and past of sets in time and space and in Minkowski spacetime. Causal futures of
compact sets are closed and causal diamonds are compact.

## ii. Key results

- `causalFuture` : The causal future of a set of spacetime points, in units where the speed of light
  is `1`.
- `causalPast` : The causal past of a set of spacetime points.
- `precedes_iff_time_space` : In any speed-of-light units the existing geometric causal relation has
  the familiar elapsed-time and spatial-distance characterization.
- `causallyFollows_iff_norm` : The existing Lorentzian causal order is equivalently the spatial norm
  bounded by elapsed Lorentz time.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Minkowski causal geometry for Green operators
- B. Causal support of the retarded solution

## iv. References

None.

## A. Minkowski causal geometry for Green operators

Lemmas: `causallyFollows_iff_displacement`, `causallyFollows_iff_norm`, `norm_space_eq_spatialPart`,
`precedes_iff_time_space`, `isClosed_causalFuture_zero`, `causalFuture_eq_add`,
`isClosed_causalFuture`, `causalPast_eq_add_neg`, `isClosed_causalPast`,
`component_bound_of_causalDiamond` and more.

## B. Causal support of the retarded solution

- `causalFuture` : The causal future of a set of spacetime points, in units where the speed of light
  is `1`.
- `causalPast` : The causal past of a set of spacetime points.

Lemmas: `isClosed_causalFuture`.

declarations.name: Minkowski.causallyFollows_iff_displacement
declarations.doc: Causal precedence depends only on the displacement between events.
declarations.statement:
lemma causallyFollows_iff_displacement (p q : SpaceTime d) :
    causallyFollows p q ↔ causallyFollows 0 (q - p)

declarations.name: Minkowski.causallyFollows_iff_norm
declarations.doc:
The existing Lorentzian causal order is equivalently the spatial norm bounded by elapsed
Lorentz time. Nonnegative elapsed time follows from this inequality.
declarations.statement:
lemma causallyFollows_iff_norm (p q : SpaceTime d) :
    causallyFollows p q ↔ ‖(q - p).spatialPart‖ ≤ (q - p).timeComponent

declarations.name: Minkowski.causalRelation
declarations.doc: Minkowski causal geometry reuses the existing Lorentzian future relation.
declarations.statement: def causalRelation (d : ℕ) : CausalRelation (SpaceTime d)

declarations.name: Minkowski.norm_space_eq_spatialPart
declarations.doc: Physlib's physical-space norm agrees with the Euclidean norm of the Lorentz spatial part.
declarations.statement: lemma norm_space_eq_spatialPart (p : SpaceTime d) : ‖p.space‖ = ‖p.spatialPart‖

declarations.name: Minkowski.precedes_iff_time_space
declarations.doc:
In any speed-of-light units the existing geometric causal relation has the familiar
elapsed-time and spatial-distance characterization. This is an application representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma precedes_iff_time_space (c : SpeedOfLight) (p q : SpaceTime d) :
    (causalRelation d).Precedes p q ↔
      (p.time c).val ≤ (q.time c).val ∧
        ‖q.space - p.space‖ ≤ (c : ℝ) * ((q.time c).val - (p.time c).val)

declarations.name: Minkowski.isClosed_causalFuture_zero
declarations.doc: The future causal cone at the origin is closed.
declarations.statement: lemma isClosed_causalFuture_zero : IsClosed ((causalRelation d).causalFuture {0})

declarations.name: Minkowski.causalFuture_eq_add
declarations.doc: Futures are translations of the existing future cone, combined over the source set.
declarations.statement:
lemma causalFuture_eq_add (K : Set (SpaceTime d)) :
    (causalRelation d).causalFuture K = K + (causalRelation d).causalFuture {0}

declarations.name: Minkowski.isClosed_causalFuture
declarations.doc: Causal futures of compact source sets are closed.
declarations.statement:
lemma isClosed_causalFuture {K : Set (SpaceTime d)} (hK : IsCompact K) :
    IsClosed ((causalRelation d).causalFuture K)

declarations.name: Minkowski.causalPast_eq_add_neg
declarations.doc: Causal pasts are translations of the negated future cone.
declarations.statement:
lemma causalPast_eq_add_neg (K : Set (SpaceTime d)) :
    (causalRelation d).causalPast K = K + -((causalRelation d).causalFuture {0})

declarations.name: Minkowski.isClosed_causalPast
declarations.doc: Causal pasts of compact source sets are closed.
declarations.statement:
lemma isClosed_causalPast {K : Set (SpaceTime d)} (hK : IsCompact K) :
    IsClosed ((causalRelation d).causalPast K)

declarations.name: Minkowski.component_bound_of_causalDiamond
declarations.doc: Every component in a causal diamond is bounded by the bounds on its endpoint sets.
declarations.statement:
lemma component_bound_of_causalDiamond {A B : ℝ} (hA : 0 ≤ A) (hB : 0 ≤ B)
    {k x l : SpaceTime d} (hk : ‖k‖ ≤ A) (hl : ‖l‖ ≤ B)
    (hkx : (causalRelation d).Precedes k x) (hxl : (causalRelation d).Precedes x l)
    (i : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) : |x i| ≤ 2 * A + B

declarations.name: Minkowski.hasCompactCausalDiamonds
declarations.doc:
Minkowski causal diamonds between compact endpoint sets are compact in every spatial
dimension.
declarations.statement: lemma hasCompactCausalDiamonds (d : ℕ) : (causalRelation d).HasCompactCausalDiamonds

declarations.name: Minkowski.local_causalPast_bound
declarations.doc: Each event has a compact future observation bound whose causal past is a neighborhood.
declarations.statement:
lemma local_causalPast_bound (p : SpaceTime d) :
    ∃ K : Set (SpaceTime d), IsCompact K ∧ (causalRelation d).causalPast K ∈ 𝓝 p

declarations.name: Minkowski.local_causalFuture_bound
declarations.doc: Each event has a compact past observation bound whose causal future is a neighborhood.
declarations.statement:
lemma local_causalFuture_bound (p : SpaceTime d) :
    ∃ K : Set (SpaceTime d), IsCompact K ∧ (causalRelation d).causalFuture K ∈ 𝓝 p

declarations.name: TimeSpace.causalFuture
declarations.doc: The causal future of a set of spacetime points, in units where the speed of light is `1`.
declarations.statement: def causalFuture (K : Set (ℝ × E)) : Set (ℝ × E)

declarations.name: TimeSpace.isClosed_causalFuture
declarations.doc: The causal future of a compact source region is closed.
declarations.statement:
lemma isClosed_causalFuture {K : Set (ℝ × E)} (hK : IsCompact K) :
    IsClosed (causalFuture K)

declarations.name: TimeSpace.causalPast
declarations.doc: The causal past of a set of spacetime points.
declarations.statement: def causalPast (K : Set (ℝ × E)) : Set (ℝ × E)

modules.title: The gamma matrices need four dimensions
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A Clifford family is a choice of `n × n` complex matrices `γ^μ`, one for each Lorentz index,
with `γ^μ γ^ν + γ^ν γ^μ = 2 η^{μν} 1`. Dirac (1928) found one with `n = 4`, and no smaller
size works. Each `γ^μ` squares to `± 1`, so it is invertible, and `γ^0 γ^1 = -γ^1 γ^0` forces
`det (γ^0 γ^1) = (-1)ⁿ det (γ^0 γ^1)`: the size is even. Size two is excluded by the three
Pauli matrices: `γ^0, i γ^1, i γ^2, i γ^3` would be four anticommuting `2 × 2` involutions, and
`2 × 2` holds at most three. The Dirac endomorphisms `gamma` of Physlib, written as `4 × 4`
matrices, attain the bound.

## ii. Key results

- `IsCliffordFamily` : the relation `γ^μ γ^ν + γ^ν γ^μ = 2 η^{μν} 1`.
- `IsCliffordFamily.even` : a Clifford family has even size.
- `IsCliffordFamily.ne_two` : there are no `2 × 2` Clifford families.
- `IsCliffordFamily.four_le` : a nonempty Clifford family has size at least four.
- `isCliffordFamily_gamma` : the Dirac gamma matrices are a Clifford family.
- `isLeast_size_isCliffordFamily` : the smallest size of a Clifford family is four.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Clifford families
- B. The size is even
- C. Size two is excluded
- D. Dirac's matrices attain the bound

## iv. References

* P. A. M. Dirac, *The quantum theory of the electron*, Proc. R. Soc. London A 117 (1928)
  610–624.

sections.text: ## A. Clifford families
## B. The size is even
## C. Size two is excluded
## D. Dirac's matrices attain the bound

declarations.name: Fermion.Dirac.IsCliffordFamily
declarations.doc: A family of `n × n` matrices with `γ^μ γ^ν + γ^ν γ^μ = 2 η^{μν} 1`.
declarations.statement: def IsCliffordFamily {n : ℕ} (γ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) : Prop

declarations.name: Fermion.Dirac.IsCliffordFamily.mul_self
declarations.statement: lemma mul_self (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : γ μ * γ μ = (minkowskiMatrix μ μ : ℂ) • 1

declarations.name: Fermion.Dirac.IsCliffordFamily.mul_comm_of_ne
declarations.statement: lemma mul_comm_of_ne {μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3} (h : μ ≠ ν) : γ ν * γ μ = -(γ μ * γ ν)

declarations.name: Fermion.Dirac.IsCliffordFamily.det_ne_zero
declarations.doc: Each member squares to `± 1`, so it is invertible.
declarations.statement: lemma det_ne_zero (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : (γ μ).det ≠ 0

declarations.name: Fermion.Dirac.IsCliffordFamily.even
declarations.doc: **A Clifford family has even size.**
declarations.statement: lemma even : Even n

declarations.name: Fermion.Dirac.IsCliffordFamily.involutions
declarations.doc: `γ^0, i γ^1, i γ^2, i γ^3`: four involutions that anticommute.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def involutions (γ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ)
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ

declarations.name: Fermion.Dirac.IsCliffordFamily.involutions_anticomm
declarations.statement:
lemma involutions_anticomm (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    involutions γ μ * involutions γ ν + involutions γ ν * involutions γ μ =
      (Sum.elim (fun _ => (1 : ℂ)) (fun _ => I) μ * Sum.elim (fun _ => (1 : ℂ)) (fun _ => I) ν) •
        (γ μ * γ ν + γ ν * γ μ)

declarations.name: Fermion.Dirac.IsCliffordFamily.ne_two
declarations.doc:
**There are no `2 × 2` Clifford families**: they would give four anticommuting `2 × 2`
involutions.
declarations.statement: lemma ne_two : n ≠ 2

declarations.name: Fermion.Dirac.IsCliffordFamily.four_le
declarations.doc: **A nonempty Clifford family has size at least four.**
declarations.statement: lemma four_le (hn : n ≠ 0) : 4 ≤ n

declarations.name: Fermion.Dirac.isCliffordFamily_gamma
declarations.doc: The Dirac gamma matrices, written as `4 × 4` matrices, are a Clifford family.
declarations.statement: lemma isCliffordFamily_gamma : IsCliffordFamily fun μ => endEquivMatrix (gamma μ)

declarations.name: Fermion.Dirac.isLeast_size_isCliffordFamily
declarations.doc:
**The gamma matrices need four dimensions (Dirac, 1928).** The smallest size of a nonempty
Clifford family is four.
declarations.statement:
lemma isLeast_size_isCliffordFamily :
    IsLeast {n : ℕ | n ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ γ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ,
      IsCliffordFamily γ} 4

modules.title: Invariants of two Weyl indices
modules.doc:
The invariants of two Weyl indices are the metric `ε` or zero, and `ε` lies in `SL(2, ℂ)`.

## i. Overview

The Weyl metric `Fermion.metricRaw = !![0, 1; -1, 0]` has determinant one, so it is itself an
element of `SL(2, ℂ)`, written `Lorentz.SL2C.epsilon`. In that form it is the invariant symplectic
form, `gᵀ ε g = ε`. Contracting spinor indices needs the single-index version of that invariance. A
factor of `(g⁻¹)ᵀ`, or of `(g⁻¹)ᴴ`, moved across `ε` becomes a factor of `g`, or of its entrywise
conjugate, on the other slot. Those are `metricRaw_comm` and `metricRaw_comm_star` at `g⁻¹`, read
entrywise. Alongside this, `LeftHandedWeyl.metricVal_rep` states the invariance of `εᵃᵃ` as the
plain equation on the tensor product, rather than through the intertwining property of
`LeftHandedWeyl.metric`.

Conversely, `ε` is the only invariant: the invariants of the tensor square of a Weyl
representation are the line through `ε`.

On the matrix of components `SL(2, ℂ)` acts by `X ↦ M X Mᵀ`, up to reparametrising the group (C).
The argument runs on matrices, for a linear map `F` with `F (M Y Mᵀ) = ρ M (F Y)` and `F X`
invariant, and shows that `F X` is a multiple of `F ε` (D). Each of the four tensor squares
reduces to it, with `F` the inverse of the matrix of components (E).

The other tensor products of two Weyl representations are handled through a uniform matrix of
components (F). The four `V ⊗ V*` have the unit `δ` as their only invariant, and are in
`PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.Fermions.Weyl.Unit`. A left-handed and a right-handed index have no
invariants at all, which is `complexLorentzTensor.invariants_upL_upR_eq_bot` in
`PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.Bispinors.ComplexifiedAction`. A product of an undotted and a dotted
one-index Weyl family is an equivariant map out of the tensors with a dual left- and a dual
right-handed index (G). The tensor-level form of the uniqueness of the metric is with the metric
tensors, in `PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.Tensors.ComplexTensor.Metrics.Basic`.

The results are named after the statement. On a tensor square `X ⊗ X` it is
`X.invariants_tprod_eq_span_metricVal`. The other forms of these
statements, for invariant elements, for the invariants in the range of an intertwining map and for
intertwining maps out of the trivial representation, follow from them by the lemmas of
`PhyslibAlpha.Mathematics.RepresentationTheory.Invariants`.

## ii. Key results

- `Fermion.LeftHandedWeyl.metricVal_rep` : `εᵃᵃ` is invariant under `SL(2, ℂ)`.
- `Lorentz.SL2C.epsilon` : the Weyl metric as an element of `SL(2, ℂ)`.
- `Lorentz.SL2C.transpose_mul_epsilon_mul` : `ε` is the invariant symplectic form.
- `Lorentz.SL2C.sum_epsilon_mul_inv_transpose`,
  `Lorentz.SL2C.sum_epsilon_mul_inv_conjTranspose` : the single-index forms.
- `Fermion.map_eq_smul_map_metricRaw_of_invariant` : on matrices, an invariant image of `X` is a
  multiple of the image of `ε`.
- `Fermion.LeftHandedWeyl.invariants_tprod_eq_span_metricVal` and its three siblings : the
  invariants of the tensor square are the line through the metric.
- `Fermion.tensorToMatrix_map` : on the matrix of components of `V ⊗ W` a pair of linear maps acts
  by `X ↦ A X Bᵀ`.
- `Lorentz.isEquivariant_downLDownR_mul` : an undotted family times a dotted one is an
  equivariant map out of `ℂT[.downL, .downR]`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Invariance of the left metric
- B. The symplectic form as an element of `SL(2, ℂ)`
- C. Reparametrising the group
- D. Matrices with an invariant image
  - D.1. The diagonal part
  - D.2. The symmetric off-diagonal part
  - D.3. The antisymmetric part
- E. The metrics are the unique invariants
- F. Components of a tensor product of two Weyl representations
  - F.1. The matrix of components
  - F.2. Three elements of `SL(2, ℂ)`
- G. One-index Weyl families and their products

## iv. References

The Weyl metrics and `Fermion.metricRaw` are in `Physlib.Relativity.Fermions.Weyl.Metric`, and
sections C to F are written to move there, with `tensorToMatrix` beside the matrix equivalences
of `Physlib.Relativity.Fermions.Weyl.Two` and the elements of F.2 in `Physlib.Relativity.SL2C`.
Section E settles the `TODO` in that file on the uniqueness of the metrics. Section G uses the
equivariant maps of `PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.Tensors.Equivariant` and stays here.
Compare `SULieAlgebra.intertwiningMap_eq_smul_adjointℂContr`.

sections.text: ## A. Invariance of the left metric

## B. The symplectic form as an element of `SL(2, ℂ)`

`ε = metricRaw` has determinant one, so it lies in `SL(2,ℂ)`, and `gᵀ ε g = ε` for every `g`
there. The single-index identities move a factor of `(g⁻¹)ᵀ` or `(g⁻¹)ᴴ` across `ε`, where it
becomes a factor of `g` or of its conjugate on the other slot: they are `metricRaw_comm` and
`metricRaw_comm_star` at `g⁻¹`, read entrywise.

## C. Reparametrising the group

On two undotted indices `SL(2,ℂ)` acts on the matrix of components by `X ↦ M X Mᵀ`, and `ε` is
fixed by it. On the other three Weyl representations the group acts through `(M⁻¹)ᵀ`, the
conjugate of `M`, or `(M⁻¹)ᴴ`, and each of these runs over all of `SL(2,ℂ)` as `M` does.

## D. Matrices with an invariant image

The argument runs on the matrix of components, through a linear map `F` with
`F (M Y Mᵀ) = ρ M (F Y)`, and with `F Y` invariant. Here `ρ` is any family of linear maps, so
that it can be a representation composed with one of the reparametrisations of C. The boosts
`diag (2, 2⁻¹)` and `diag (2⁻¹, 2)` combine to give the diagonal part of `Y`, so `F` kills it
(D.1). The element `!![1, -1; 1, 0]` sends the symmetric off-diagonal matrix `O` to minus itself
plus a diagonal matrix, so `F O` is its own negative and vanishes (D.2). What is left of `Y` is
its antisymmetric part, a multiple of `ε` (D.3).
### D.1. The diagonal part
### D.2. The symmetric off-diagonal part
### D.3. The antisymmetric part

## E. The metrics are the unique invariants

On the matrix of components `SL(2,ℂ)` acts by `X ↦ N X Nᵀ`, where `N` is `M`, `(M⁻¹)ᵀ`, the
conjugate of `M`, or `(M⁻¹)ᴴ`, and by section C section D applies to each, with `F` the inverse of
the matrix of components. So the invariants of each tensor square are the line through its
metric.

## F. Components of a tensor product of two Weyl representations

The other twelve tensor products of two Weyl representations are handled uniformly through
their matrix of components, `tensorToMatrix`, on which `SL(2,ℂ)` acts by `X ↦ K₁ X K₂ᵀ` with
`Kᵢ` the matrices of the two factors (F.1). The arguments of
`PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.Fermions.Weyl.Unit` only test this action against three elements of
`SL(2,ℂ)`, the boosts `boostTwo` and `boostHalf` along `z`, and `epsilon` (F.2).
### F.1. The matrix of components
### F.2. Three elements of `SL(2, ℂ)`

## G. One-index Weyl families and their products

A two-element family of elements of an algebra `B` can carry one dual Weyl index, undotted or
dotted. Both laws are contragredient, and the dotted law carries the extra complex conjugation. A
fermion field of the Standard Model with every index but its spinor index frozen is such a family.
When the Lorentz action is multiplicative, an undotted family times a dotted one is an equivariant
map out of `ℂT[.downL, .downR]`, in either order, the shape of a Dirac mass term `ψ̄ ψ`. That such
a map carries no invariant is `Lorentz.reducesInvariantsTo_bot_leftRight`, in
`PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.Bispinors.ComplexifiedAction`.

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.sum_epsilon_mul_inv_transpose

Single-index form. A factor of `(g⁻¹)ᵀ` moved across `ε` becomes a factor of `g` on the

    ∑ k : Fin 2, epsilon.1 l k * (g.1⁻¹)ᴴ a k
      = ∑ b : Fin 2, star (g.1 b l) * epsilon.1 b a
