declarations.name: Lorentz.isEquivariant_downLDownR_mul
declarations.doc:
A family `X` with a dual undotted spinor index, moved by the contragredient of the
left-handed Weyl representation, times a family `Y` with a dual dotted spinor index, moved by
its conjugate, is an equivariant map out of `ℂT[.downL, .downR]`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_downLDownR_mul {X Y : Fin 2 → B}
    (hX : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (a : Fin 2), repLorentz Λ (X a) = ∑ β, (Λ⁻¹).1 a β • X β)
    (hY : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (a : Fin 2), repLorentz Λ (Y a) = ∑ β, star ((Λ⁻¹).1 a β) • Y β) :
    complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant ![.downL, .downR] repLorentz
      (liftComponents ((fun p => X p.1 * Y p.2) ∘ pairIdx))

declarations.name: Lorentz.isEquivariant_downLDownR_mul_swap
declarations.doc:
A dotted family times an undotted one is an equivariant map out of `ℂT[.downL, .downR]`, the
two spinor slots exchanged.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_downLDownR_mul_swap {X Y : Fin 2 → B}
    (hX : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (a : Fin 2), repLorentz Λ (X a) = ∑ β, star ((Λ⁻¹).1 a β) • X β)
    (hY : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (a : Fin 2), repLorentz Λ (Y a) = ∑ β, (Λ⁻¹).1 a β • Y β) :
    complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant ![.downL, .downR] repLorentz
      (liftComponents ((fun p => X p.2 * Y p.1) ∘ pairIdx))

modules.title: The metric pairings of four Weyl indices
modules.doc:
The invariants of four left-handed Weyl indices are spanned by two products of Weyl metrics.

## i. Overview

A coefficient function `C : (Fin n → Fin 2) → ℂ` of `n` left-handed Weyl indices carries the action
of `M ∈ SL(2, ℂ)` on each index, `SlotAction.act M C`. With four indices the products of two Weyl
metrics `ε_{ab} = metricRaw`, pairing the slots `ε_{a₀a₁} ε_{a₂a₃}`, `ε_{a₀a₂} ε_{a₁a₃}` and
`ε_{a₀a₃} ε_{a₁a₂}`, are invariant. They obey the Schouten identity
`ε₀₁ ε₂₃ - ε₀₂ ε₁₃ + ε₀₃ ε₁₂ = 0` (A), and the first two span all invariants (C).

The argument is infinitesimal. The unipotent elements `1 + z E` and `1 + z F` of `SL(2, ℂ)`, with
`E = !![0, 1; 0, 0]` and `F = !![0, 0; 1, 0]`, move a fixed coefficient function along a line, so
it is killed by the infinitesimal actions of `E` and `F`, one slot at a time (B). These
unipotent elements generate `SL(2, ℂ)`, every element being a product of four of them, which
`PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.Bispinors.ComplexifiedAction` uses. For four indices those two conditions
are linear equations on the sixteen coefficients. They force every coefficient with more raised
than lowered indices, or fewer, to vanish, and leave the six balanced ones in a two-dimensional
space. The two coefficients at `1100` and `1010` fix all the others
(`eq_sum_pairingBasis_of_infinitesimalAct_eq_zero`). The right-handed Weyl representation has the
same invariants, the group acting on it through a reparametrisation of itself (C.3). The components
of a tensor with four Weyl indices of one chirality are such a coefficient function, so the
invariant tensors are the span of the two products of metrics (D).

## ii. Key results

- `Fermion.metricPairing` : a product of two Weyl metrics on four indices.
- `Fermion.exists_eq_lowerUnipotent_mul_upperUnipotent` : every element of `SL(2, ℂ)` is a product
  of unipotent elements.
- `Fermion.metricPairing_schouten` : the Schouten identity.
- `Fermion.eq_sum_pairingBasis_of_infinitesimalAct_eq_zero` : a coefficient function killed by `E`
  and `F` is a combination of `ε₀₂ ε₁₃` and `ε₀₁ ε₂₃`.
- `Fermion.infinitesimalAct_eq_zero_of_invariant` : an invariant coefficient function is killed by
  `E` and `F`.
- `Fermion.mem_span_pairingBasis_iff` : the invariants of four left-handed Weyl indices are the span
  of `ε₀₂ ε₁₃` and `ε₀₁ ε₂₃`.
- `Fermion.linearIndependent_pairingBasis` : the two are linearly independent.
- `Fermion.mem_span_pairingBasis_iff_map_star` : the same for right-handed indices.
- `complexLorentzTensor.invariants_upL_pow_four_eq_span_range_leftMetricPairing`,
  `complexLorentzTensor.invariants_upR_pow_four_eq_span_range_rightMetricPairing` : the invariant
  tensors with four Weyl indices of one chirality.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Products of Weyl metrics
- B. The unipotent elements
- C. Four Weyl indices
  - C.1. The infinitesimal equations
  - C.2. The invariants
  - C.3. The other Weyl representations
- D. Tensors with four Weyl indices of one chirality

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Products of Weyl metrics
## B. The unipotent elements

## C. Four Weyl indices

### C.1. The infinitesimal equations

### C.2. The invariants

The pairings are invariant because `M ε Mᵀ = (det M) ε`, applied to each pair of slots.

### C.3. The other Weyl representations

On right-handed indices `M` acts through its conjugate, which runs over all of `SL(2, ℂ)` as `M`
does (`Fermion.map_star_coe_map_starRingEnd`), so their invariants are the same span.

## D. Tensors with four Weyl indices of one chirality

The components of a tensor with four left-handed Weyl indices are a coefficient function of four
Weyl indices, on which `g` acts by `act g.1`, and those of a tensor with four right-handed ones a
coefficient function on which `g` acts by `act (g.1.map star)`. The classifications of C are
thereby classifications of the invariant tensors, through
`TensorSpecies.invariants_tensorRep_eq_map_componentEquiv`. The dual colours are reached from
these by `TensorSpecies.invariants_tensorRep_update_eq_map_toDualMapAtIndex`.

declarations.name: Fermion.metricPairing
declarations.doc:
The product `ε_{a_i a_j} ε_{a_k a_l}` of two Weyl metrics on four Weyl indices, pairing the
slots `i, j` and `k, l`.
declarations.statement: def metricPairing (i j k l : Fin 4) (a : Fin 4 → Fin 2) : ℂ

declarations.name: Fermion.exists_eq_vecCons
declarations.doc: Every index vector of four slots is a vector literal.
declarations.statement: lemma exists_eq_vecCons {α : Type*} (a : Fin 4 → α) : ∃ w x y z, a = ![w, x, y, z]

declarations.name: Fermion.metricPairing_schouten
declarations.doc:
The Schouten identity `ε₀₁ ε₂₃ - ε₀₂ ε₁₃ + ε₀₃ ε₁₂ = 0`. Two-component spinors admit no
totally antisymmetric tensor of rank three.
declarations.statement:
lemma metricPairing_schouten :
    metricPairing 0 1 2 3 - metricPairing 0 2 1 3 + metricPairing 0 3 1 2 = 0

declarations.name: Fermion.pairingBasis
declarations.doc: The two pairings spanning the invariants of four Weyl indices, `ε₀₂ ε₁₃` and `ε₀₁ ε₂₃`.
declarations.statement: def pairingBasis : Fin 2 → (Fin 4 → Fin 2) → ℂ

declarations.name: Fermion.pairingPoint
declarations.doc: Two index vectors, `1100` and `1010`, on which `pairingBasis` is the unit matrix.
declarations.statement: def pairingPoint : Fin 2 → Fin 4 → Fin 2

declarations.name: Fermion.pairingBasis_pairingPoint
declarations.doc: The two basis pairings evaluated at the two test points form the unit matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma pairingBasis_pairingPoint (i j : Fin 2) :
    pairingBasis i (pairingPoint j) = if i = j then 1 else 0

declarations.name: Fermion.linearIndependent_pairingBasis
declarations.doc: The two pairings are linearly independent.
declarations.statement: lemma linearIndependent_pairingBasis : LinearIndependent ℂ pairingBasis

declarations.name: Fermion.upperUnipotent
declarations.doc: The unipotent element `!![1, z; 0, 1] = 1 + z E` of `SL(2, ℂ)`.
declarations.statement: def upperUnipotent (z : ℂ) : SL(2,ℂ)

declarations.name: Fermion.lowerUnipotent
declarations.doc: The unipotent element `!![1, 0; z, 1] = 1 + z F` of `SL(2, ℂ)`.
declarations.statement: def lowerUnipotent (z : ℂ) : SL(2,ℂ)

declarations.name: Fermion.exists_eq_lowerUnipotent_mul_upperUnipotent
declarations.doc:
Every element of `SL(2, ℂ)` is a product of four unipotent elements, alternately lower and
upper. With `M = !![p, q; r, s]` and `a` chosen so that `r' = a p + r ≠ 0`, the matrix
`lowerUnipotent a * M` is `upperUnipotent ((p - 1) / r') * lowerUnipotent r' *
upperUnipotent ((a q + s - 1) / r')`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_eq_lowerUnipotent_mul_upperUnipotent (M : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    ∃ a x r y : ℂ,
      M = lowerUnipotent a * upperUnipotent x * lowerUnipotent r * upperUnipotent y

declarations.name: Fermion.one_add_smul_zero_apply
declarations.doc: At `t = 0` the line `t ↦ 1 + c t G` is the identity.
declarations.statement:
lemma one_add_smul_zero_apply (G : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) (c : ℂ) (p q : Fin 2) :
    (1 + (c * ((0 : ℝ) : ℂ)) • G) p q = if p = q then 1 else 0

declarations.name: Fermion.hasDerivAt_one_add_smul
declarations.doc: The line `t ↦ 1 + c t G` has derivative `c G`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_one_add_smul (G : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) (c : ℂ) (p q : Fin 2) :
    HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => (1 + (c * (t : ℂ)) • G) p q) ((c • G) p q) 0

declarations.name: Fermion.infinitesimalAct_eq_zero_of_invariant
declarations.doc:
An invariant coefficient function of `n` Weyl indices is killed by the infinitesimal actions
of `E` and `F`, the derivatives of the unipotent lines.

declarations.name: Fermion.infinitesimalAct_four
declarations.doc: The infinitesimal action at four Weyl indices, written out slot by slot.
declarations.statement:
lemma infinitesimalAct_four (N : Fin 2 → Fin 2 → ℂ) (C : (Fin 4 → Fin 2) → ℂ) (w x y z : Fin 2) :
    infinitesimalAct N C ![w, x, y, z] = ∑ q, (N w q * C ![q, x, y, z] + N x q * C ![w, q, y, z]
      + N y q * C ![w, x, q, z] + N z q * C ![w, x, y, q])

declarations.name: Fermion.eq_sum_pairingBasis_of_infinitesimalAct_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
A coefficient function of four Weyl indices killed by `E` and `F` is a combination of
`ε₀₂ ε₁₃` and `ε₀₁ ε₂₃`, with its values at `1100` and `1010` as coefficients. The equations
of `E` at `0111`, of `F` at `1000` and their neighbours kill the unbalanced coefficients, and
those of `E` at the four index vectors with a single raised slot relate the six balanced ones.

declarations.name: Fermion.sum_metricRaw_mul
declarations.doc: The Weyl metric against two rows of a matrix gives the determinant times the metric.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_metricRaw_mul (M : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) (p q : Fin 2) :
    ∑ x, ∑ z, metricRaw x z * (M p x * M q z) = M.det * metricRaw p q

declarations.name: Fermion.sum_pi_four
declarations.doc: A sum over index vectors of four slots is a fourfold sum.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_pi_four {β : Type*} [AddCommMonoid β] (F : (Fin 4 → Fin 2) → β) :
    ∑ d, F d = ∑ w, ∑ x, ∑ y, ∑ z, F ![w, x, y, z]

modules.title: Weyl fermions as tensors
modules.doc:
Left- and right-handed Weyl fermions are the complex Lorentz tensors with one undotted or one
dotted index.

## i. Overview

A left-handed Weyl fermion is a complex Lorentz tensor with a single index of colour `.upL`, and a
right-handed one a tensor with a single index of colour `.upR`. In both cases `fromSingleT` is the
linear equivalence between the two. It makes `Fermion.LeftHandedWeyl` and
`Fermion.RightHandedWeyl` tensorial types, so that tensor products of them with other tensorial
types are tensorial through `TensorSpecies.Tensorial.prod`. The equivalence carries the action of
`SL(2, ℂ)` on spinors to the action on tensors, and the basis spinor `e_a` to the basis tensor with
the single component `a`, for left-handed (A) and right-handed (B) fermions alike.

## ii. Key results

- `Fermion.LeftHandedWeyl.tensorial` : left-handed Weyl fermions are the tensors with one index
  `.upL`.
- `Fermion.RightHandedWeyl.tensorial` : right-handed Weyl fermions are the tensors with one index
  `.upR`.
- `Fermion.LeftHandedWeyl.toTensor_basis`, `Fermion.RightHandedWeyl.toTensor_basis` : the basis
  spinor `e_a` is the basis tensor with component `a`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Left-handed Weyl fermions
- B. Right-handed Weyl fermions

## iv. References

The tensorial class is in `Physlib.Relativity.Tensors.Tensorial`. The tensorial instance of complex
four-vectors is in `PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.Tensors.ComplexTensor.Vector.Tensorial`.

modules.title: The units are the unique invariants
modules.doc:
Up to scale, the unit `δ` is the only invariant of a Weyl representation tensored with its dual.

## i. Overview

On `V ⊗ V*`, for `V` one of the four Weyl representations, `SL(2, ℂ)` acts on the matrix of
components by conjugation, `X ↦ N X N⁻¹`. The two boosts along `z` combine to give the
off-diagonal part of `X`, so an invariant has none, and conjugation by `ε` swaps the two diagonal
entries (A). An invariant of `V ⊗ V*` therefore has a multiple of the identity matrix as
components, which is the unit `δ` (B). For each of the four pairs this says that the invariants of
`V ⊗ V*` are the line through `δ` (C).

## ii. Key results

- `Fermion.DualLeftHandedWeyl.invariants_tprod_eq_span_unitVal` and its three siblings : the
  invariants of `V ⊗ V*` are the line through the unit.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Matrices
- B. Tensor products
- C. The four pairs

## iv. References

The units are in `Physlib.Relativity.Fermions.Weyl.Unit`, where these results are written to move.
The matrix of components `tensorToMatrix`, the elements `boostTwo`, `boostHalf` and `epsilon`,
and the tactic `weyl_act` are in `PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.Fermions.Weyl.Metric`, alongside the
analogous results for the metrics.

sections.text: ## A. Matrices
## B. Tensor products

## C. The four pairs

For each pair `V ⊗ V*` the statement is in the namespace that holds its unit, as in
`DualLeftHandedWeyl.unitVal : LeftHandedWeyl ⊗ DualLeftHandedWeyl`.

declarations.name: Fermion.map_eq_smul_map_one_of_conj
declarations.doc:
A linear map on matrices which is unchanged by the boosts `X ↦ D X D⁻¹`, on every matrix
with the same image as `X`, and by `X ↦ ε X ε⁻¹` at `X`, sends `X` to a multiple of the image
of the identity.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_eq_smul_map_one_of_conj (F : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    {X : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ}
    (hD : ∀ Z, F Z = F X → F !![Z 0 0, 4 * Z 0 1; Z 1 0 / 4, Z 1 1] = F Z)
    (hD' : ∀ Z, F Z = F X → F !![Z 0 0, Z 0 1 / 4; 4 * Z 1 0, Z 1 1] = F Z)
    (hε : F !![X 1 1, -X 1 0; -X 0 1, X 0 0] = F X) :
    F X = ((X 0 0 + X 1 1) / 2) • F 1

declarations.name: Fermion.exists_eq_smul_one_of_conj
declarations.doc:
When three elements of `SL(2,ℂ)` act on the components of `V ⊗ W` as two boosts and `ε`,
every invariant of `V ⊗ W` is a multiple of the element with the identity as components.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_eq_smul_one_of_conj {V W : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    [AddCommGroup W] [Module ℂ W] (b : Module.Basis (Fin 2) ℂ V) (c : Module.Basis (Fin 2) ℂ W)
    {ρV : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) V} {ρW : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) W} {v : V ⊗[ℂ] W}
    (hv : v ∈ (ρV.tprod ρW).invariants)
    (hD : ∃ g, ∀ X, LinearMap.toMatrix b b (ρV g) * X * (LinearMap.toMatrix c c (ρW g))ᵀ =
      !![X 0 0, 4 * X 0 1; X 1 0 / 4, X 1 1])
    (hD' : ∃ g, ∀ X, LinearMap.toMatrix b b (ρV g) * X * (LinearMap.toMatrix c c (ρW g))ᵀ =
      !![X 0 0, X 0 1 / 4; 4 * X 1 0, X 1 1])
    (hε : ∃ g, ∀ X, LinearMap.toMatrix b b (ρV g) * X * (LinearMap.toMatrix c c (ρW g))ᵀ =
      !![X 1 1, -X 1 0; -X 0 1, X 0 0]) :
    ∃ z : ℂ, v = z • (tensorToMatrix b c).symm 1

modules.title: Schwarzschild's incompressible fluid sphere and its junction with the exterior solution
modules.doc:
Junction of Schwarzschild's incompressible fluid sphere with the exterior Schwarzschild metric.

## i. Overview

In his second 1916 paper, Schwarzschild solved Einstein's equations for a static sphere of
incompressible fluid of constant density `ρ₀`. The interior space is a portion of a
three-sphere of curvature radius `Rc`, with `Rc ^ 2 = 3 / (κ ρ₀)` (`κ = 8 π G`, `c = 1`),
and the surface of the fluid sits at the polar angle `χ_a` with `sin χ_a = Ra / Rc`, where
`Ra` is the areal radius of the surface. In the areal radius `r = Rc sin χ` the interior metric
coefficients are

- `g_tt = ((3 cos χ_a - cos χ) / 2) ^ 2 = (3 / 2 cos χ_a - 1 / 2 √(1 - r ^ 2 / Rc ^ 2)) ^ 2`,
- `g_rr = 1 / (1 - r ^ 2 / Rc ^ 2)`,

while outside the sphere the metric is the exterior Schwarzschild solution with
`g_tt = 1 - α / r`, `g_rr = 1 / (1 - α / r)` and `α = Ra ^ 3 / Rc ^ 2`. The pressure is
`ρ₀ + p = ρ₀ 2 cos χ_a / (3 cos χ_a - cos χ)`.

This file takes the two metrics and the pressure as given (the field equations are not
verified here) and proves the elementary properties of the junction at `r = Ra`: continuity
of `g_tt` and `g_rr`, differentiability of the glued `g_tt`, non-differentiability of the glued
`g_rr` in the curvature coordinate `r`, the vanishing of the pressure at the surface, and the
Schwarzschild bound `cos χ_a > 1 / 3` (equivalently `Ra > 9 / 8 α`) for the central pressure to
be positive.

## ii. Key results

- `IncompressibleSphere` contains the input data: `Rc`, `Ra`, `ρ₀` with `0 < Ra < Rc` and
  `0 < ρ₀`.
- `rs_div_Ra`: Schwarzschild's relation (40), `α / Ra = sin χ_a ^ 2`.
- `pressure_chia`: the pressure vanishes at the surface.
- `pressure_zero_pos_iff`: the central pressure is positive if and only if `cos χ_a > 1 / 3`.
- `one_third_lt_cosChia_iff_rs`: `cos χ_a > 1 / 3` if and only if `9 / 8 α < Ra`.
- `gttIn_Ra`, `grrIn_Ra`: the interior and exterior formulas agree at `r = Ra`.
- `gttGlue_hasDerivAt`: the glued `g_tt` is differentiable at `Ra` with derivative `Ra / Rc ^ 2`.
- `grrGlue_not_differentiableAt`: the glued `g_rr` is continuous but not differentiable at
  `Ra` (one-sided derivatives `2 Ra / (Rc ^ 2 cos χ_a ^ 4)` and `- Ra / (Rc ^ 2 cos χ_a ^ 4)`).

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The input data
- B. The Schwarzschild radius and the angle of the surface
- C. The pressure
  - C.1. Pressure at the surface and at the centre
  - C.2. The bound `cos χ_a > 1 / 3`
- D. The metric coefficients
  - D.1. The interior metric in the angle `χ`
  - D.2. The values at the surface agree
- E. Derivatives of the metric coefficients at the surface
  - E.1. Two auxiliary derivatives
  - E.2. Derivatives of `g_tt`
  - E.3. Derivatives of `g_rr`
- F. The glued metric coefficients
- G. Consequences for the junction
- H. A numerical instance

## iv. References

- K. Schwarzschild, "Uber das Gravitationsfeld einer Kugel aus inkompressibler Flussigkeit nach
  der Einsteinschen Theorie", Sitzungsberichte der Koniglich Preussischen Akademie der
  Wissenschaften (1916), 424-434. English translation by S. Antoci, arXiv:physics/9912033.
  Equations (28), (29), (30), (35), (36), (39), (40) and the discussion on pages 8-9 of the
  translation (pressure diverging at `cos χ_a = 1 / 3`, limit `9 / 8 α`).
- A. Lichnerowicz, "Theories relativistes de la gravitation et de l'electromagnetisme",
  Masson (1955), chapter III, sections 27-29 (junction conditions).

sections.text:
## A. The input data

The sphere is specified by the curvature radius `Rc` of the interior space, the areal radius
`Ra` of its surface and the constant density `ρ₀`. The sphere is a proper part of the spherical
space (`Ra < Rc`, so that `χ_a < π / 2`).
## B. The Schwarzschild radius and the angle of the surface
## C. The pressure
### C.1. Pressure at the surface and at the centre

### C.2. The bound `cos χ_a > 1 / 3`

Schwarzschild, page 9 of the translation: the pressure at the centre stays finite as long as
`Ra > 9 / 8 α`.

## D. The metric coefficients

The interior metric (35) is written in the areal radius `r = Rc sin χ`; the relation with the
form in `χ` is a lemma (`gttIn_Rc_mul_sin`, `grrIn_Rc_mul_sin`), not a definition. The metric
coefficients are taken up to the sign of the signature.
### D.1. The interior metric in the angle `χ`
### D.2. The values at the surface agree
## E. Derivatives of the metric coefficients at the surface
### E.1. Two auxiliary derivatives
### E.2. Derivatives of `g_tt`
### E.3. Derivatives of `g_rr`

## F. The glued metric coefficients

The glued coefficients use the interior formula for `r ≤ Ra` and the exterior formula
beyond. The glued `g_tt` is differentiable at `Ra`; the glued `g_rr` is continuous but not
differentiable at `Ra`, since its one-sided derivatives differ.

## G. Consequences for the junction

In a Gaussian coordinate `l` along the radius, `dr / dl = 1 / √g_rr` and
`d g_tt / dl = g_tt' / √g_rr`. Both quantities take the same value at `Ra` from the two
formulas (Lichnerowicz, chapter III, section 28, evaluated at the surface). The coordinate `l`
itself is not constructed here.

## H. A numerical instance

The sphere with `Rc = 1`, `Ra = 3 / 5` and `ρ₀ = 1`: `cos χ_a = 4 / 5`, `α = 27 / 125`,
`9 / 8 α < Ra`, central pressure `1 / 7`.

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere
declarations.doc:
Schwarzschild's incompressible fluid sphere: the curvature radius `Rc` of the interior
spherical space (`Rc ^ 2 = 3 / (κ ρ₀)`, Schwarzschild (37)), the areal radius `Ra` of the
surface (Schwarzschild's `P_o`, (39)) and the constant density `ρ₀`, with `0 < Ra < Rc` and
`0 < ρ₀`.
declarations.statement:
structure IncompressibleSphere where
  /-- The curvature radius of the interior spherical space. -/
  Rc : ℝ
  /-- The areal radius of the surface of the fluid. -/
  Ra : ℝ
  /-- The constant density of the fluid. -/
  ρ₀ : ℝ
  /-- The curvature radius is positive. -/
  Rc_pos : 0 < Rc
  /-- The radius of the surface is positive. -/
  Ra_pos : 0 < Ra
  /-- The sphere is a proper part of the spherical space. -/
  Ra_lt_Rc : Ra < Rc
  /-- The density is positive. -/
  ρ₀_pos : 0 < ρ₀

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.rs
declarations.doc:
The Schwarzschild radius `α = (κ ρ₀ / 3) P_o ^ 3 = Ra ^ 3 / Rc ^ 2` of the sphere,
Schwarzschild (40).
declarations.statement: def rs : ℝ

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.chia
declarations.doc: The polar angle `χ_a` of the surface, `sin χ_a = Ra / Rc`, Schwarzschild (28).
declarations.statement: def chia : ℝ

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.cosChia
declarations.doc: The cosine of the angle of the surface, written as `√(1 - Ra ^ 2 / Rc ^ 2)`.
declarations.statement: def cosChia : ℝ

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.one_sub_sq_div_sq_pos
declarations.statement: lemma one_sub_sq_div_sq_pos : 0 < 1 - S.Ra ^ 2 / S.Rc ^ 2

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.cosChia_sq
declarations.statement: lemma cosChia_sq : S.cosChia ^ 2 = 1 - S.Ra ^ 2 / S.Rc ^ 2

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.cosChia_eq_cos_chia
declarations.doc: `cosChia` is the cosine of `chia`.
declarations.statement: lemma cosChia_eq_cos_chia : S.cosChia = Real.cos S.chia

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.cosChia_pos
declarations.statement: lemma cosChia_pos : 0 < S.cosChia

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.cosChia_lt_one
declarations.statement: lemma cosChia_lt_one : S.cosChia < 1

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.rs_div_Ra
declarations.doc: Schwarzschild (40): `α / P_o = sin χ_a ^ 2`.
declarations.statement: lemma rs_div_Ra : S.rs / S.Ra = Real.sin S.chia ^ 2

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.rs_lt_Ra
declarations.doc: The surface of the sphere lies outside its Schwarzschild radius.
declarations.statement: lemma rs_lt_Ra : S.rs < S.Ra

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.pressure
declarations.doc:
The pressure of the fluid at the polar angle `χ`, Schwarzschild (30):
`ρ₀ + p = ρ₀ 2 cos χ_a / (3 cos χ_a - cos χ)`.
declarations.statement: def pressure (χ : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.pressure_chia
declarations.doc: The pressure vanishes at the surface of the fluid.
declarations.statement: lemma pressure_chia : S.pressure S.chia = 0

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.pressure_zero
declarations.doc: The pressure at the centre, away from the critical value `cos χ_a = 1 / 3`.
declarations.statement:
lemma pressure_zero (h : 3 * S.cosChia ≠ 1) :
    S.pressure 0 = S.ρ₀ * (1 - S.cosChia) / (3 * S.cosChia - 1)

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.pressure_zero_pos
declarations.statement: lemma pressure_zero_pos (hsub : 1 / 3 < S.cosChia) : 0 < S.pressure 0

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.pressure_zero_pos_iff
declarations.doc:
The central pressure is positive if and only if `cos χ_a > 1 / 3`. For `cos χ_a < 1 / 3`
the formula (30) is negative at the centre; at `cos χ_a = 1 / 3` the division by zero of
Lean gives `pressure 0 = - ρ₀`. The divergence of the pressure at the critical value is not
a statement of this file.
declarations.statement: lemma pressure_zero_pos_iff : 0 < S.pressure 0 ↔ 1 / 3 < S.cosChia

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.one_third_lt_cosChia_iff_sq
declarations.statement: lemma one_third_lt_cosChia_iff_sq : 1 / 3 < S.cosChia ↔ S.Ra ^ 2 < 8 / 9 * S.Rc ^ 2

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.one_third_lt_cosChia_iff_Ra_lt
declarations.doc: `cos χ_a > 1 / 3` if and only if `Ra < √(8 / 9) Rc`.
declarations.statement: lemma one_third_lt_cosChia_iff_Ra_lt : 1 / 3 < S.cosChia ↔ S.Ra < √(8 / 9) * S.Rc

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.one_third_lt_cosChia_iff_rs
declarations.doc: `cos χ_a > 1 / 3` if and only if `9 / 8 α < Ra` (Schwarzschild, page 9).
declarations.statement: lemma one_third_lt_cosChia_iff_rs : 1 / 3 < S.cosChia ↔ 9 / 8 * S.rs < S.Ra

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.Ra_div_Rc_of_cosChia_eq
declarations.doc:
At the critical value `cos χ_a = 1 / 3` the ratio `Ra / Rc = sin χ_a` (Schwarzschild's
fall velocity, (42)) equals `√(8 / 9)`.
declarations.statement: lemma Ra_div_Rc_of_cosChia_eq (hc : S.cosChia = 1 / 3) : S.Ra / S.Rc = √(8 / 9)

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.gttIn
declarations.doc:
The interior coefficient `g_tt` in the areal radius `r`, Schwarzschild (35):
`(3 / 2 cos χ_a - 1 / 2 √(1 - r ^ 2 / Rc ^ 2)) ^ 2`.
declarations.statement: def gttIn (r : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.grrIn
declarations.doc:
The interior coefficient `g_rr` in the areal radius `r`, Schwarzschild (35):
`1 / (1 - r ^ 2 / Rc ^ 2)`.
declarations.statement: def grrIn (r : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.gttOut
declarations.doc: The exterior coefficient `g_tt = 1 - α / r`, Schwarzschild (36).
declarations.statement: def gttOut (r : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.grrOut
declarations.doc: The exterior coefficient `g_rr = 1 / (1 - α / r)`, Schwarzschild (36).
declarations.statement: def grrOut (r : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.one_sub_sin_sq
declarations.statement:
lemma one_sub_sin_sq (χ : ℝ) :
    1 - (S.Rc * Real.sin χ) ^ 2 / S.Rc ^ 2 = Real.cos χ ^ 2

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.gttIn_Rc_mul_sin
declarations.doc: Schwarzschild (35): in the angle `χ`, `g_tt = ((3 cos χ_a - cos χ) / 2) ^ 2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma gttIn_Rc_mul_sin {χ : ℝ} (h0 : 0 ≤ χ) (hπ : χ ≤ π / 2) :
    S.gttIn (S.Rc * Real.sin χ) = ((3 * S.cosChia - Real.cos χ) / 2) ^ 2

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.grrIn_Rc_mul_sin
declarations.doc: Schwarzschild (35): in the angle `χ`, the coefficient of `dχ ^ 2` is `Rc ^ 2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma grrIn_Rc_mul_sin {χ : ℝ} (hc : Real.cos χ ≠ 0) :
    S.grrIn (S.Rc * Real.sin χ) * (S.Rc * Real.cos χ) ^ 2 = S.Rc ^ 2

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.gttIn_Ra
declarations.doc: The interior and exterior formulas for `g_tt` take the same value at `r = Ra`.
declarations.statement: lemma gttIn_Ra : S.gttIn S.Ra = S.gttOut S.Ra

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.grrIn_Ra
declarations.doc: The interior and exterior formulas for `g_rr` take the same value at `r = Ra`.
declarations.statement: lemma grrIn_Ra : S.grrIn S.Ra = S.grrOut S.Ra

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.eq_rs_of_gttIn_Ra
declarations.doc:
The exterior form of `g_tt` at the surface determines the Schwarzschild radius: if
`g_tt (Ra) = 1 - a / Ra` then `a = α = Ra ^ 3 / Rc ^ 2`, which is Schwarzschild (40).
declarations.statement: lemma eq_rs_of_gttIn_Ra {a : ℝ} (h : S.gttIn S.Ra = 1 - a / S.Ra) : a = S.rs

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.gttIn_zero_of_cosChia_eq
declarations.doc: At the critical value `cos χ_a = 1 / 3`, `g_tt` vanishes at the centre.
declarations.statement: lemma gttIn_zero_of_cosChia_eq (hcrit : S.cosChia = 1 / 3) : S.gttIn 0 = 0

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.hasDerivAt_one_sub_sq_div
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_one_sub_sq_div (Rc r : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun x : ℝ => 1 - x ^ 2 / Rc ^ 2) (-(2 * r) / Rc ^ 2) r

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.hasDerivAt_sqrt_one_sub_sq_div
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_sqrt_one_sub_sq_div {Rc r : ℝ} (hu : 0 < 1 - r ^ 2 / Rc ^ 2) :
    HasDerivAt (fun x : ℝ => √(1 - x ^ 2 / Rc ^ 2))
      (-r / (Rc ^ 2 * √(1 - r ^ 2 / Rc ^ 2))) r

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.gttIn_hasDerivAt
declarations.doc: The interior `g_tt` is differentiable at `Ra` with derivative `Ra / Rc ^ 2`.
declarations.statement: lemma gttIn_hasDerivAt : HasDerivAt S.gttIn (S.Ra / S.Rc ^ 2) S.Ra

declarations.statement: lemma deriv_gttOut_Ra : deriv S.gttOut S.Ra = S.Ra / S.Rc ^ 2

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.deriv_gttIn_Ra_eq_deriv_gttOut_Ra

declarations.statement: lemma deriv_gttIn_Ra_eq_deriv_gttOut_Ra : deriv S.gttIn S.Ra = deriv S.gttOut S.Ra

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.grrIn_hasDerivAt
declarations.doc:
The interior `g_rr` is differentiable at `Ra` with derivative
`2 Ra / (Rc ^ 2 cos χ_a ^ 4)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma grrIn_hasDerivAt :
    HasDerivAt S.grrIn (2 * S.Ra / (S.Rc ^ 2 * S.cosChia ^ 4)) S.Ra

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.deriv_grrIn_Ra
declarations.doc: The derivative of the interior `g_rr` at `Ra`.
declarations.statement: lemma deriv_grrIn_Ra : deriv S.grrIn S.Ra = 2 * S.Ra / (S.Rc ^ 2 * S.cosChia ^ 4)

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.grrOut_hasDerivAt
declarations.doc:
The exterior `g_rr` is differentiable at `Ra` with derivative
`- Ra / (Rc ^ 2 cos χ_a ^ 4)`.

    HasDerivAt S.grrOut (-(S.Ra / (S.Rc ^ 2 * S.cosChia ^ 4))) S.Ra

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.deriv_grrOut_Ra
declarations.doc: The derivative of the exterior `g_rr` at `Ra`.
declarations.statement: lemma deriv_grrOut_Ra : deriv S.grrOut S.Ra = -(S.Ra / (S.Rc ^ 2 * S.cosChia ^ 4))

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.deriv_grrIn_Ra_ne_deriv_grrOut_Ra

The derivatives of the two formulas for `g_rr` differ at `r = Ra`, in the curvature

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.gttGlue
declarations.doc: The glued `g_tt`: interior formula for `r ≤ Ra`, exterior formula beyond.
declarations.statement: def gttGlue (r : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.grrGlue
declarations.doc: The glued `g_rr`: interior formula for `r ≤ Ra`, exterior formula beyond.
declarations.statement: def grrGlue (r : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: GeneralRelativity.IncompressibleSphere.gttGlue_continuousAt

modules.title: Class IsLorentzDeriv
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A family of operators indexed by the four spacetime directions is a Lorentz derivative
when the representation of `SL(2,ℂ)` intertwines it through the columns of the Lorentz
matrix, as the jet derivatives on a jet algebra do. The iterated operator along a multiset
of directions then transforms by one column of the Lorentz matrix per slot
(`rep_iteratedD_ofFn`), which is the law `IsLorentzDerivTransforms` and its covariant form
`IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms` record for a family of derivative symbols.

## ii. Key results

- `IsLorentzDerivTransforms` : a family of derivative symbols `F : s ↦ [∂_s ψ^φ]`, indexed by the
  dual of a value space `V` carrying a representation of `SL(2,ℂ)`, transforms as the derivative
  symbols of a Lorentz-covariant field: each ordered symbol mixes into all tuples of directions by
  the per-slot columns of the Lorentz matrix, while the value index transforms by the contragredient
  action `rep.dual` on the dual of `V`
- `IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms` : a family of *covariant*-derivative symbols, indexed by ordered
  tuples of directions (covariant derivatives do not commute) and by the dual of a Lorentz
  representation `V`, transforms as the covariant derivatives of a Lorentz-covariant field: each
  derivative slot mixes by the columns of the Lorentz matrix, while the value index transforms by
  the contragredient action `rep.dual` on the dual of `V`, the ordered-tuple analogue of
  `IsLorentzDerivTransforms`
- `rep_iteratedD_ofFn` : the Lorentz transformation of iterated derivatives: for a Lorentz
  derivative the ordered derivative symbol `D_{l 0} ⋯ D_{l (n-1)} x` mixes into all tuples of
  directions, with one Lorentz matrix factor per slot

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Lorentz-covariant families of derivative symbols

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Lorentz-covariant families of derivative symbols

declarations.name: Representation.trivial_dual_apply
declarations.doc: The dual of the trivial representation acts trivially.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.Representation.trivial_dual_apply {k G V : Type*} [CommSemiring k]
    [Group G] [AddCommMonoid V] [Module k V] (g : G) (φ : Module.Dual k V) :
    (Representation.trivial k G V).dual g φ = φ

declarations.name: Lorentz.iteratedD
declarations.doc:
The iterated operator `D_s = D_{ν₁} ⋯ D_{νₙ}` of a pairwise-commuting family of
endomorphisms along a multiset `s` of indices. Commutativity is what makes the
operator well-defined on a multiset, i.e. independent of any ordering of `s`.
declarations.statement:
def iteratedD {ι : Type*} (D : ι → A →ₗ[ℂ] A)
    (hD : ∀ i j, (D i).comp (D j) = (D j).comp (D i)) (s : Multiset ι) : A →ₗ[ℂ] A

declarations.name: Lorentz.iteratedD_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedD_zero {ι : Type*} (D : ι → A →ₗ[ℂ] A)
    (hD : ∀ i j, (D i).comp (D j) = (D j).comp (D i)) :
    iteratedD D hD (0 : Multiset ι) = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: Lorentz.iteratedD_cons
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedD_cons {ι : Type*} (D : ι → A →ₗ[ℂ] A)
    (hD : ∀ i j, (D i).comp (D j) = (D j).comp (D i)) (κ : ι) (s : Multiset ι) :
    iteratedD D hD (κ ::ₘ s) = (D κ).comp (iteratedD D hD s)

declarations.name: Lorentz.iteratedD_singleton
declarations.doc: The iterated operator of a singleton is the operator itself.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedD_singleton {ι : Type*} (D : ι → A →ₗ[ℂ] A)
    (hD : ∀ i j, (D i).comp (D j) = (D j).comp (D i)) (κ : ι) :
    iteratedD D hD {κ} = D κ

declarations.name: Lorentz.iteratedD_add
declarations.doc:
The iterated operator is additive in the multiset of directions. Applying along
`s + t` is applying along `t` and then along `s`.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedD_add {ι : Type*} (D : ι → A →ₗ[ℂ] A)
    (hD : ∀ i j, (D i).comp (D j) = (D j).comp (D i)) (s t : Multiset ι) :
    iteratedD D hD (s + t) = (iteratedD D hD s).comp (iteratedD D hD t)

declarations.name: Lorentz.iteratedD_cons'
declarations.doc:
The companion of `iteratedD_cons`, peeling the new operator on the inside. For a
commuting family the extra operator may equally be applied first.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedD_cons' {ι : Type*} (D : ι → A →ₗ[ℂ] A)
    (hD : ∀ i j, (D i).comp (D j) = (D j).comp (D i)) (κ : ι) (s : Multiset ι) :
    iteratedD D hD (κ ::ₘ s) = (iteratedD D hD s).comp (D κ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.iteratedD_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedD_mul (D : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → A →ₗ[ℂ] A)
    (D_comm : ∀ μ ν, (D μ).comp (D ν) = (D ν).comp (D μ))
    (D_mul : ∀ (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (b₁ b₂ : A),
      D μ (b₁ * b₂) = D μ b₁ * b₂ + b₁ * D μ b₂)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (b₁ b₂ : A) :
    Lorentz.iteratedD D D_comm s (b₁ * b₂) =
      (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        Lorentz.iteratedD D D_comm p.1 b₁ * Lorentz.iteratedD D D_comm p.2 b₂).sum

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsLorentzDeriv
declarations.doc:
A family of operators indexed by the spacetime directions is a Lorentz derivative
when the representation of `SL(2,ℂ)` intertwines it through the columns of the Lorentz
matrix. The class needs only the module structure, so it applies uniformly to any
representation space.
declarations.statement:
class IsLorentzDeriv {M : Type} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module ℂ M]
    (rep : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) M) (D : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M →ₗ[ℂ] M) where
  rep_deriv {Λ μ x} : rep Λ (D μ x) =
    ∑ a, (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 a μ : ℝ) : ℂ) • D a (rep Λ x)

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsLorentzDerivTransforms
declarations.doc:
A family of derivative symbols `F : s ↦ [∂_s ψ^φ]`, indexed by the dual of a value
space `V` carrying a representation of `SL(2,ℂ)`, transforms as the derivative
symbols of a Lorentz-covariant field. Each ordered symbol mixes into all tuples of
directions by the per-slot columns of the Lorentz matrix, while the value index
transforms by the contragredient action `rep.dual` on the dual of `V`. This is the
general form of the Lorentz law `GaugeBoson.LorentzTransformsAsGaugeField`, for a field
valued in an arbitrary Lorentz representation, such as the trivial representation for
scalars, the Weyl representations for fermions, and their conjugates for the barred
fields. At `n = 0`
it reduces to the homogeneous law `Λ • F₀^φ = F₀^{Λ^{-⊤} φ}`.
declarations.statement:
def IsLorentzDerivTransforms {k V : Type*} [CommRing k] [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
    [Module k A]
    (repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) A) (rep : Representation k SL(2,ℂ) V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual k V →ₗ[k] A) : Prop

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms
declarations.doc:
A family of covariant-derivative symbols, indexed by ordered tuples of
directions (covariant derivatives do not commute) and by the dual of a Lorentz
representation `V`, transforms as the covariant derivatives of a
Lorentz-covariant field. Each derivative slot mixes by the columns of the Lorentz
matrix, while the value index transforms by the contragredient action `rep.dual` on
the dual of `V`. This is the ordered-tuple analogue of `IsLorentzDerivTransforms`.
declarations.statement:
def IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms {k V : Type*} [CommRing k] [AddCommGroup V]
    [Module k V] [Module k A] (repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) A)
    (rep : Representation k SL(2,ℂ) V)
    (F : {n : ℕ} → (Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) → Module.Dual k V →ₗ[k] A) : Prop

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms.neg_one_apply
declarations.doc:
At the centre the derivative slots do not mix. The element `-1` of `SL(2,ℂ)` covers
the identity Lorentz transformation, so the sum over tuples collapses to the single term
`p = l` and only the value index moves.

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsLorentzDeriv.rep_iteratedD_ofFn
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz transformation of iterated derivatives. For a Lorentz derivative the
ordered derivative symbol `D_{l 0} ⋯ D_{l (n-1)} x` mixes into all tuples of
directions, with one Lorentz matrix factor per slot.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_iteratedD_ofFn [IsLorentzDeriv rep D]
    (D_comm : ∀ μ ν, (D μ).comp (D ν) = (D ν).comp (D μ))
    (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (x : A) :
    rep Λ (iteratedD D D_comm (List.ofFn l) x) =
      ∑ p : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3),
        (∏ i, (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 (p i) (l i) : ℝ) : ℂ)) •
          iteratedD D D_comm (List.ofFn p) (rep Λ x)

modules.title: The defining relation of the Lorentz group on its entries
modules.doc:
The relation `Λ η Λᵀ = η` over `ℂ`, read on a single entry and with integer metric entries.

## i. Overview

`Physlib.Relativity.LorentzGroup.Basic` states the defining relation of the Lorentz group as
the matrix equation `Λ η Λᵀ = η` over `ℝ`. A classification of invariant tensors contracts
that relation one metric pairing at a time, over `ℂ` and against entries which a decision
procedure has to evaluate. `sum_minkowskiMatrixZ_mul` is the relation in exactly that form:
the entry `(a, b)`, the coefficients cast into `ℂ`, and the metric entries taken from
`minkowskiMatrixZ` rather than `minkowskiMatrix`.

## ii. Key results

- `LorentzGroup.sum_minkowskiMatrixZ_mul` : the defining relation on the entry `(a, b)`, over
  `ℂ` and with integer metric entries.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The defining relation on an entry

## iv. References

The defining relation and its matrix forms are in `Physlib.Relativity.LorentzGroup.Basic`.

sections.text: ## A. The defining relation on an entry

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.sum_minkowskiMatrixZ_mul
declarations.doc:
The defining relation `Λ η Λᵀ = η` over `ℂ`, read on the entry `(a, b)` and with the
integer Minkowski matrix in place of `minkowskiMatrix`. This is the form the invariant
classifications contract against, one metric pairing per pair of slots.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_minkowskiMatrixZ_mul (Λ : LorentzGroup d) (a b : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    ∑ x : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d, ∑ y : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d, ((minkowskiMatrixZ x y : ℤ) : ℂ)
        * (((Λ.1 a x : ℝ) : ℂ) * ((Λ.1 b y : ℝ) : ℂ))
      = ((minkowskiMatrixZ a b : ℤ) : ℂ)

modules.title: Entries of an axis boost
modules.doc:
The Hermiticity of a coordinate-axis boost in `SL(2, ℂ)`, read on its entries.

## i. Overview

A boost along a coordinate axis, `boostAxis i t ht`, is a Hermitian element of `SL(2, ℂ)`:
`Physlib.Relativity.LorentzGroup.Boosts.Axis` states this as the matrix equation
`(boostAxis i t ht).1ᴴ = (boostAxis i t ht).1`. Contracting an axis boost against a family
of tensor components needs that equation one entry at a time, which is what
`star_boostAxis_apply` provides: conjugating an entry transposes it.

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.SL2C.star_boostAxis_apply` : conjugating an entry of an axis boost transposes it.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Hermiticity on the entries

## iv. References

The matrix form of the axis boosts is fixed in `Physlib.Relativity.LorentzGroup.Boosts.Axis`.

sections.text: ## A. Hermiticity on the entries

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.star_boostAxis_apply
declarations.doc: Hermiticity read on the entries: conjugating an entry of an axis boost transposes it.
declarations.statement:
lemma star_boostAxis_apply (i : Fin 3) (t : ℝ) (ht : t ≠ 0) (β α : Fin 2) :
    star ((boostAxis i t ht).1 β α) = (boostAxis i t ht).1 α β

modules.title: Fermionic parity
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The homomorphism `SL(2, ℂ) → LorentzGroup 3` is two-to-one, and the nontrivial element of its
kernel is `-1`. Physically it is the rotation by `2π`: it acts as the identity on every tensor,
and as `-1` on every spinor, so it measures the parity of the number of fermionic indices
carried by a quantity. We call it the *fermionic parity*.

Because it lies in the Lorentz group's double cover and projects to the identity, any quantity
required to be invariant under `SL(2, ℂ)` is fixed by it. A quantity carrying an odd number of
spinor indices is negated by it, and therefore vanishes: this is the selection rule that forbids
terms with an odd number of fermions.

## ii. Key results

- `LorentzGroup.fermionicParity` : the nontrivial element of the kernel of the covering
  `SL(2, ℂ) → LorentzGroup 3`.
- `LorentzGroup.toSelfAdjointMap_fermionicParity` : it acts trivially on self-adjoint matrices.
- `LorentzGroup.toLorentzGroup_fermionicParity` : it projects to the identity Lorentz
  transformation.
- `LorentzGroup.fermionicParity_sq` : it squares to one.
- `LorentzGroup.fermionicParity_ne_one` : it is not itself the identity.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Fermionic parity
- B. The action on vectors and on spinors

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Fermionic parity

## B. The action on vectors and on spinors

Fermionic parity is invisible on Lorentz vectors and acts by `-1` on Weyl spinors: this is what
makes it measure the parity of the number of spinor indices.

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.fermionicParity
declarations.doc:
Fermionic parity: the nontrivial element `-1` of the kernel of the two-to-one homomorphism
`SL(2, ℂ) → LorentzGroup 3`, that is the rotation by `2π`. It acts trivially on tensors and by
`-1` on spinors.
declarations.statement: def fermionicParity : SL(2, ℂ)

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.toSelfAdjointMap_fermionicParity
declarations.doc:
Fermionic parity acts trivially on self-adjoint matrices: conjugation by `-1` is the
identity.
declarations.statement:
lemma toSelfAdjointMap_fermionicParity :
    Lorentz.SL2C.toSelfAdjointMap fermionicParity = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.toLorentzGroup_fermionicParity
declarations.doc:
Fermionic parity projects to the identity Lorentz transformation: it is invisible on
tensors.
declarations.statement:
lemma toLorentzGroup_fermionicParity :
    Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup fermionicParity = 1

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.fermionicParity_sq
declarations.statement: lemma fermionicParity_sq : fermionicParity ^ 2 = 1

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.fermionicParity_ne_one
declarations.doc:
Fermionic parity is not the identity of `SL(2, ℂ)`: the covering is genuinely
two-to-one.
declarations.statement: lemma fermionicParity_ne_one : fermionicParity ≠ 1

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.complexCoVector_SL2CRep_fermionicParity
declarations.doc:
Fermionic parity acts trivially on complex covariant Lorentz vectors, since it projects to
the identity Lorentz transformation.
declarations.statement:
lemma complexCoVector_SL2CRep_fermionicParity :
    Lorentz.ComplexCoVector.SL2CRep fermionicParity = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.rightHandedWeyl_rep_fermionicParity
declarations.doc: Fermionic parity acts by `-1` on right-handed Weyl spinors.
declarations.statement:
lemma rightHandedWeyl_rep_fermionicParity :
    Fermion.RightHandedWeyl.rep fermionicParity = -LinearMap.id

modules.title: The eigenspaces of the centre of `SL(2,ℂ)`
modules.doc:
The subspaces on which the central element `-1` of `SL(2,ℂ)` acts by a scalar, and the Lorentz
invariants of a half-integer spin.

## i. Overview

The classifications of the invariant tensors contract the components with a coefficient tensor.
This file settles, in one step and for every pattern at once, the patterns that carry no
invariant for the crudest of reasons: they are of half-integer spin, and a half-integer spin has
no invariant because the centre of `SL(2,ℂ)` already tells integer spin from half-integer spin
apart.

The element `-1` of `SL(2,ℂ)` covers the identity Lorentz transformation
(`SL2C.toLorentzGroup_neg_one`), so a representation of `SL(2,ℂ)` that factors through the
Lorentz group — a tensor of four-vector indices — sends it to the identity, while each Weyl
index contributes a sign. A subspace with an odd number of Weyl indices therefore lies in the
`-1` eigenspace of `repLorentz (-1)`, and a vector both fixed by the group and negated by `-1`
is zero. `centreEigenspace` names the eigenspace, `mul_le_centreEigenspace` multiplies the two
signs in a product of subspaces, and `mem_of_invariant_of_mem_sup_centreEigenspace_neg_one` is
the classification modulo a Lorentz-stable subspace `S`, the form the Standard Model files use.

The subspaces that arise there are spans of symbol families, so section B reads the sign of
such a span off the sign of the value space: the covariant-derivative slots of a family
obeying `IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms` are inert at the centre, and only the value index moves.

The argument uses the central element alone: it needs neither a grading nor a light-cone
basis. On the complex Lorentz tensors `-1` acts on each Weyl index by `-1` and on each
four-vector index by `1`, so on the tensors with colours `c` by `(-1)` to the number of Weyl
colours of `c`, and with an odd number of Weyl indices there are no invariant tensors but zero
(E).

## ii. Key results

- `centreEigenspace` : the subspace on which the centre of `SL(2,ℂ)` acts by the scalar `ε`: an
  integer spin sits at `ε = 1` and a half-integer spin at `ε = -1`
- `mul_le_centreEigenspace` : the sign of a product is the product of the signs
- `mem_of_invariant_of_mem_sup_centreEigenspace_neg_one` : a subspace of half-integer spin carries
  no Lorentz invariant beyond a Lorentz-stable submodule `S`: an invariant of the join with `S`
  already lies in `S`
- `complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep_neg_one` : `-1` acts on the tensors by `(-1)` to the number of
  Weyl colours
- `complexLorentzTensor.invariants_eq_bot_of_odd_weyl` : tensors with an odd number of Weyl
  indices have no invariants but zero

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The sign a subspace carries at the centre
- B. The sign of a symbol family
- C. Signs multiply
- D. The classification modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule
- E. The centre on the complex Lorentz tensors

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The sign a subspace carries at the centre

The centre of `SL(2,ℂ)` is `±1` and squares to the identity, so `repLorentz (-1)` is an
involution and the only signs on offer are `±1`. A tensor of four-vector indices carries `1`,
a Weyl index carries `-1`, and nothing else is needed of the pattern.

## B. The sign of a symbol family

A family of symbols transforming as the covariant derivatives of a field valued in `V` carries
at the centre the sign that `V` does. The derivative slots mix by the Lorentz matrix, which is
the identity at the centre, so they contribute nothing; the value index moves by `rep.dual`,
which carries the sign of `rep` by section A. Both signs that occur are recorded, `ε = 1` for
the Lorentz-scalar value spaces and `ε = -1` for the Weyl ones.

## C. Signs multiply

The Lorentz action on the field algebra is by algebra maps, so the sign a product carries is
the product of the signs of its factors. This is the whole of the bookkeeping: two Weyl
indices cancel and an odd number does not.

## D. The classification modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule

A vector of a subspace of sign `-1` that the group fixes is negated by `-1` and fixed by it at
once, so it is zero. Modulo a stable subspace `S` this is the case `μ = -1` of
`reducesInvariantsTo_bot_of_apply_eq_smul`: the invariance leaves `-2` times the vector inside
`S`, and dividing by `-2` is allowed over `ℂ`; no quotient representation is needed.

## E. The centre on the complex Lorentz tensors

The element `-1` covers the identity Lorentz transformation, so it acts on the four-vector colours
by `1`, and on each Weyl colour by `-1`. On the tensors with colours `c` it therefore acts by the
product of these signs, `(-1)` to the number of Weyl colours of `c`
(`TensorSpecies.tensorRep_eq_prod_smul`). With an odd number of Weyl colours this is `-1`, and an
invariant tensor both fixed and negated by `-1` is zero.

declarations.name: Lorentz.Invariants.centreEigenspace
declarations.doc:
The subspace on which the centre of `SL(2,ℂ)` acts by the scalar `ε`: an integer spin
sits at `ε = 1` and a half-integer spin at `ε = -1`.
declarations.statement: def centreEigenspace (repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) V) (ε : ℂ) : Submodule ℂ V

declarations.name: Lorentz.Invariants.mem_centreEigenspace
declarations.doc: Membership of `centreEigenspace` unfolded: the centre scales the vector by `ε`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_centreEigenspace {repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) V} {ε : ℂ} {x : V} :
    x ∈ centreEigenspace repLorentz ε ↔ repLorentz (-1) x = ε • x

declarations.name: Lorentz.Invariants.dual_neg_one_eq_smul_id
declarations.doc:
Dualising a representation preserves the sign at the centre: `-1` is its own inverse, so
the contragredient action of the centre is the transpose of a scalar.
declarations.statement:
lemma dual_neg_one_eq_smul_id {rep : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) V} {ε : ℂ}
    (hrep : rep (-1) = ε • LinearMap.id) : rep.dual (-1) = ε • LinearMap.id

declarations.name: Lorentz.Invariants.range_le_centreEigenspace
declarations.doc: **The span of one symbol family carries the sign of its value space.**

declarations.name: Lorentz.Invariants.range_le_centreEigenspace_neg_one
declarations.doc:
The half-integer case of `range_le_centreEigenspace`, in the form the Weyl value spaces
state their sign.

declarations.name: Lorentz.Invariants.mul_le_centreEigenspace
declarations.doc: The sign of a product is the product of the signs.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_le_centreEigenspace {repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) A}
    (hmul : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x y : A), repLorentz Λ (x * y) = repLorentz Λ x * repLorentz Λ y)
    {W₁ W₂ : Submodule ℂ A} {ε₁ ε₂ : ℂ} (h₁ : W₁ ≤ centreEigenspace repLorentz ε₁)
    (h₂ : W₂ ≤ centreEigenspace repLorentz ε₂) :
    W₁ * W₂ ≤ centreEigenspace repLorentz (ε₁ * ε₂)

declarations.name: Lorentz.Invariants.mem_of_invariant_of_mem_sup_centreEigenspace_neg_one
declarations.doc:
A subspace of half-integer spin carries no Lorentz invariant beyond a Lorentz-stable
submodule `S`: an invariant of the join with `S` already lies in `S`. The centre acts on the
subspace by `-1 ≠ 1`, so it reduces to `⊥`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_invariant_of_mem_sup_centreEigenspace_neg_one
    {repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) A} {W : Submodule ℂ A}
    (hW : W ≤ centreEigenspace repLorentz (-1)) (S : Submodule ℂ A)
    (hS : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) {x : A} (hx : x ∈ W ⊔ S)
    (hinv : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: Lorentz.centreSign
declarations.doc:
The sign by which `-1` acts on a colour: `1` on the four-vector colours and `-1` on the Weyl
colours.
declarations.statement: def centreSign (k : complexLorentzTensor.Color) : ℂ

declarations.name: Lorentz.rep_neg_one
declarations.doc: The element `-1` acts on the representation of each colour by its sign.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_neg_one (k : complexLorentzTensor.Color) :
    complexLorentzTensor.rep k (-1) = centreSign k • LinearMap.id

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep_neg_one
declarations.doc:
The element `-1` acts on the tensors with colours `c` by `(-1)` to the number of Weyl colours
of `c`.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep_neg_one {n : ℕ}
    (c : Fin n → complexLorentzTensor.Color) :
    complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep c (-1) =
      (-1 : ℂ) ^ (Finset.univ.filter fun i => ¬ (c i = .up ∨ c i = .down)).card •
        LinearMap.id

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.invariants_eq_bot_of_odd_weyl
declarations.doc:
The tensors with an odd number of Weyl indices have no invariants but zero. The element `-1`
negates them, and an invariant tensor is fixed by it.

modules.title: Reynolds elements for complex Lorentz tensors
modules.doc:
The action of `SL(2, ℂ)` on complex Lorentz tensors is continuous, so the tensors have a Reynolds
element.

## i. Overview

A family of vectors in a representation `repLorentz` of `SL(2,ℂ)` on `B`, carrying Lorentz
indices of colours `c`, is packaged as a linear map `f : ℂT(c) →ₗ[ℂ] B`, equivariant in the sense
`complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant c repLorentz f`. The invariants in the range of such a map
come from invariant tensors whenever the tensors have a Reynolds element,
`TensorSpecies.HasReynolds`.

In its basis the matrix of `g` on a colour is `g`, `(g⁻¹)ᵀ`, the entrywise conjugate of `g`,
`(g⁻¹)ᴴ`, the Lorentz matrix of `g`, or the transpose of the inverse of that (A). So its entries
depend continuously on `g` (B). The tensors with any list of colours are finite-dimensional, and
the continuous action of `SL(2,ℂ)` on them has a Reynolds element by
`Representation.exists_isReynolds_of_specialLinearGroup`, `complexLorentzTensor.hasReynolds` (C).

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.continuous_toMatrix_rep` : the matrix entries of every colour depend continuously on
  the element of `SL(2,ℂ)`.
- `complexLorentzTensor.hasReynolds` : the tensors with any list of colours have a Reynolds
  element.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The matrices of the colours
- B. Continuity of the matrices
- C. Reynolds elements

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The matrices of the colours
## B. Continuity of the matrices
## C. Reynolds elements

declarations.name: Lorentz.toMatrix_rep_upL
declarations.doc: The matrix of `g` on the left-handed Weyl colour is `g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrix_rep_upL (g : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    LinearMap.toMatrix (complexLorentzTensor.basis .upL) (complexLorentzTensor.basis .upL)
      (complexLorentzTensor.rep .upL g) = g.1

declarations.name: Lorentz.toMatrix_rep_downL
declarations.doc: The matrix of `g` on the dual left-handed Weyl colour is `(g⁻¹)ᵀ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrix_rep_downL (g : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    LinearMap.toMatrix (complexLorentzTensor.basis .downL) (complexLorentzTensor.basis .downL)
      (complexLorentzTensor.rep .downL g) = (g.1⁻¹)ᵀ

declarations.name: Lorentz.toMatrix_rep_upR
declarations.doc: The matrix of `g` on the right-handed Weyl colour is the entrywise conjugate of `g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrix_rep_upR (g : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    LinearMap.toMatrix (complexLorentzTensor.basis .upR) (complexLorentzTensor.basis .upR)
      (complexLorentzTensor.rep .upR g) = g.1.map star

declarations.name: Lorentz.toMatrix_rep_downR
declarations.doc: The matrix of `g` on the dual right-handed Weyl colour is `(g⁻¹)ᴴ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrix_rep_downR (g : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    LinearMap.toMatrix (complexLorentzTensor.basis .downR) (complexLorentzTensor.basis .downR)
      (complexLorentzTensor.rep .downR g) = (g.1⁻¹)ᴴ

declarations.name: Lorentz.toMatrix_rep_up_apply
declarations.doc: The matrix of `g` on the contravariant vector colour is the Lorentz matrix of `g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrix_rep_up_apply (g : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    LinearMap.toMatrix (complexLorentzTensor.basis .up) (complexLorentzTensor.basis .up)
      (complexLorentzTensor.rep .up g) μ ν
      = (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup g).1 μ ν : ℝ) : ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.toMatrix_rep_down_apply
declarations.doc:
The matrix of `g` on the covariant vector colour is the transpose of the inverse of the
Lorentz matrix of `g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrix_rep_down_apply (g : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    LinearMap.toMatrix (complexLorentzTensor.basis .down) (complexLorentzTensor.basis .down)
      (complexLorentzTensor.rep .down g) μ ν
      = (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup g)⁻¹.1 ν μ : ℝ) : ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.continuous_toLorentzGroup_apply
declarations.doc:
The entries of the Lorentz matrix of `g` depend continuously on `g`, through the trace
formula `L(g)_{i j} = ½ tr (σ'_i g σ'_j g†)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_toLorentzGroup_apply (i j : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    Continuous fun g : SL(2,ℂ) => (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup g).1 i j : ℝ) : ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.continuous_toMatrix_rep
declarations.doc: The entries of the matrix of `g` on every colour depend continuously on `g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_toMatrix_rep (k : complexLorentzTensor.Color) (x y : basisIdx k) :
    Continuous fun g : SL(2,ℂ) => LinearMap.toMatrix (complexLorentzTensor.basis k)
      (complexLorentzTensor.basis k) (complexLorentzTensor.rep k g) x y

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.hasReynolds
declarations.doc:
The complex Lorentz tensors with any list of colours have a Reynolds element. They are
finite-dimensional, and `SL(2,ℂ)` acts on them continuously.
declarations.statement:
lemma complexLorentzTensor.hasReynolds {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → complexLorentzTensor.Color) :
    complexLorentzTensor.HasReynolds c

modules.title: The Lorentz mixing of derivative slots
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A Lorentz transformation mixes each derivative slot of a symbol through a column `Λ_{b a}`
of the Lorentz matrix. On families indexed by multisets of directions this is the operator
`lorentzMix`: peel one direction `a`, put it back as every direction `b` weighted by
`Λ_{b a}`, and mix what is left; peeling commutes, so the operator descends to multisets,
and `lorentzMix_ofFn` is its tuple form. The correction terms of a covariant derivative are
Leibniz convolutions `derivConv` over the multiset antidiagonal, and `lorentzMix` is a
morphism for the convolution. The Lorentz law of any covariant tower built one slot at a
time from a covariant correction is then one induction, `repLorentz_tower`. Nothing here
depends on a gauge group.

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.lorentzMix`, `Lorentz.lorentzMix_ofFn` : the mixing operator and its tuple form.
- `Lorentz.derivConv`, `Lorentz.lorentzMix_derivConv` : the Leibniz convolution, and the
  mixing operator as a morphism for it.
- `Lorentz.repLorentz_tower` : the Lorentz law of an abstract covariant tower.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Lorentz mixing of derivative slots
- B. The Leibniz convolution
- C. The Lorentz law of a covariant tower

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The Lorentz mixing of derivative slots
## B. The Leibniz convolution

## C. The Lorentz law of a covariant tower

A covariant tower is built one slot at a time: the tower along `l 0 :: l'` is the tower
along `l'` with one more plain derivative, plus a correction `C (l 0)` applied to the tower
along `l'`. The induction is run once, for an abstract tower with a Lorentz covariant
correction that is linear in the family it corrects and lets a twist of the value index
through.

declarations.name: Lorentz.lorentzMixStep
declarations.doc:
One peeling step of the Lorentz mixing: the direction `a` is removed from the multiset
index of the family and put back as every direction `b`, weighted by `Λ_{b a}`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def lorentzMixStep (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (a : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (G : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M) : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M

declarations.doc: Peeling two directions commutes, so the mixing is well defined on a multiset.
declarations.statement: instance (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) : LeftCommutative (lorentzMixStep (M := M) Λ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.lorentzMix
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz mixing of a multiset-indexed family along a multiset `s` of directions:
every direction of `s` is peeled and replaced by all directions, weighted by the
corresponding column of the Lorentz matrix.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def lorentzMix (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (G : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M

declarations.name: Lorentz.lorentzMix_zero
declarations.statement: lemma lorentzMix_zero : lorentzMix Λ G 0 = G

declarations.name: Lorentz.lorentzMix_cons_apply
declarations.doc: Mixing along `a ::ₘ s` peels `a` after mixing along `s`.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzMix_cons_apply (a : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    lorentzMix Λ G (a ::ₘ s) t = ∑ b, L[Λ] b a • lorentzMix Λ G s (b ::ₘ t)

declarations.name: Lorentz.lorentzMix_apply_add
declarations.doc:
Evaluating a mixed family away from the empty multiset is mixing the translated
family at the empty multiset.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzMix_apply_add (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    ∀ (G : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M) (t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)),
      lorentzMix Λ G s t = lorentzMix Λ (fun r => G (r + t)) s 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.lorentzMix_cons_zero
declarations.doc: Peeling at the empty multiset: the peeled direction is pushed into the family.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzMix_cons_zero (a : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    lorentzMix Λ G (a ::ₘ s) 0 = ∑ b, L[Λ] b a • lorentzMix Λ (fun t => G (b ::ₘ t)) s 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.lorentzMix_map
declarations.doc: The mixing operator commutes with any linear map applied to the values.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzMix_map (Φ : M →ₗ[ℂ] N) (s t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    Φ (lorentzMix Λ G s t) = lorentzMix Λ (fun r => Φ (G r)) s t

declarations.name: Lorentz.lorentzMix_smul_fam
declarations.doc: The mixing operator is homogeneous in the family.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzMix_smul_fam (c : ℂ) (s t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    lorentzMix Λ (fun r => c • G r) s t = c • lorentzMix Λ G s t

declarations.name: Lorentz.lorentzMix_add_fam
declarations.doc: The mixing operator is additive in the family.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzMix_add_fam (G₁ G₂ : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M)
    (s t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    lorentzMix Λ (fun r => G₁ r + G₂ r) s t = lorentzMix Λ G₁ s t + lorentzMix Λ G₂ s t

declarations.name: Lorentz.lorentzMix_sum_fam
declarations.doc: The mixing operator commutes with finite sums of families.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzMix_sum_fam {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (H : ι → Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M)
    (s t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    lorentzMix Λ (fun r => ∑ i, H i r) s t = ∑ i, lorentzMix Λ (H i) s t

declarations.name: Lorentz.lorentzMix_ofFn
declarations.doc:
The mixing operator agrees with the tuple form of the Lorentz law: along an ordered
tuple of directions it is the sum over all tuples with one Lorentz matrix factor per
slot.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzMix_ofFn {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    lorentzMix Λ G (List.ofFn l) t =
      ∑ p : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3),
        (∏ i, L[Λ] (p i) (l i)) • G ((List.ofFn p : List (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) + t)

declarations.name: Lorentz.derivConv
declarations.doc:
The Leibniz convolution of two families of derivative symbols: the sum over the
splittings of the multiset of the products of the two symbols.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivConv (f g : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) : B

declarations.name: Lorentz.derivConv_cons
declarations.doc: One derivative peeled off a convolution lands on one factor or the other.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivConv_cons (f g : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B) (a : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    derivConv f g (a ::ₘ s) =
      derivConv f (fun r => g (a ::ₘ r)) s + derivConv (fun r => f (a ::ₘ r)) g s

declarations.name: Lorentz.derivConv_sum_right
declarations.doc: The convolution is linear in its right-hand family.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivConv_sum_right {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (f : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B)
    (c : ι → ℂ) (g : ι → Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    derivConv f (fun r => ∑ i, c i • g i r) s = ∑ i, c i • derivConv f (g i) s

declarations.name: Lorentz.derivConv_sum_left
declarations.doc: The convolution is linear in its left-hand family.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivConv_sum_left {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (g : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B)
    (c : ι → ℂ) (f : ι → Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    derivConv (fun r => ∑ i, c i • f i r) g s = ∑ i, c i • derivConv (f i) g s

declarations.name: Lorentz.lorentzMix_derivConv
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz mixing operator is a morphism for the Leibniz convolution: mixing the two
factors separately and convolving is the same as convolving and then mixing.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzMix_derivConv (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    ∀ (f g : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B),
      derivConv (fun x => lorentzMix Λ f x 0) (fun y => lorentzMix Λ g y 0) s =
        lorentzMix Λ (derivConv f g) s 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.repLorentz_derivConv
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz law of a Leibniz convolution: the mixing operator is a morphism for the
convolution, so a convolution of two families with Lorentz laws has one too.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_derivConv {repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) B}
    (hmul : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (b₁ b₂ : B),
      repLorentz Λ (b₁ * b₂) = repLorentz Λ b₁ * repLorentz Λ b₂)
    (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (f f' g g' : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B)
    (hf : ∀ x, repLorentz Λ (f x) = lorentzMix Λ f' x 0)
    (hg : ∀ y, repLorentz Λ (g y) = lorentzMix Λ g' y 0) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    repLorentz Λ (derivConv f g s) = lorentzMix Λ (derivConv f' g') s 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.repLorentz_tower
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz law of a covariant tower `T` built by the step `hstep` from a correction
`C`, transforming into a tower `T'` built by the same step: the seed of `T` transforms
into the seed of `T'` with the value index twisted by `τ` (`hzero`), and the correction is
Lorentz covariant (`hC`), linear in the family it corrects (`hClin`) and lets the twist
through (`hCτ`). Then the covariant slots mix by their own columns of the Lorentz matrix,
the plain slots by `lorentzMix`, and the value index by `τ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_tower {K : Type} [Field K] {W : Type} [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W]
    [Module K B] [SMulCommClass K ℂ B] (Λ : SL(2,ℂ))
    (T T' : (n : ℕ) → (Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) → Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → W →ₗ[K] B)
    (C : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → W →ₗ[K] B) →
      Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → W →ₗ[K] B)
    (τ : W →ₗ[K] W)
    (hstep : ∀ (n : ℕ) (l : Fin (n + 1) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)),
      T (n + 1) l s = T n (fun i => l i.succ) (l 0 ::ₘ s) + C (l 0) (T n fun i => l i.succ) s)
    (hstep' : ∀ (n : ℕ) (l : Fin (n + 1) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)),
      T' (n + 1) l s = T' n (fun i => l i.succ) (l 0 ::ₘ s) + C (l 0) (T' n fun i => l i.succ) s)
    (hzero : ∀ (l : Fin 0 → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : W),
      repLorentz Λ (T 0 l s φ) = lorentzMix Λ (fun t => T' 0 l t (τ φ)) s 0)
    (hC : ∀ (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (G G' : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → W →ₗ[K] B),
      (∀ y χ, repLorentz Λ (G y χ) = lorentzMix Λ (fun t => G' t χ) y 0) →
      ∀ (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : W), repLorentz Λ (C ρ G s φ) =
        ∑ a, L[Λ] a ρ • lorentzMix Λ (fun t => C a G' t φ) s 0)
    (hClin : ∀ (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] (c : ι → ℂ)
      (G : ι → Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → W →ₗ[K] B) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : W), C ρ (fun t => ∑ i, c i • G i t) s φ = ∑ i, c i • C ρ (G i) s φ)
    (hCτ : ∀ (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (G : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → W →ₗ[K] B)
      (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : W),
      C ρ (fun t => G t ∘ₗ τ) s φ = C ρ G s (τ φ)) :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : W),
      repLorentz Λ (T n l s φ) =
        ∑ p : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3),
          (∏ i, L[Λ] (p i) (l i)) • lorentzMix Λ (fun t => T' n p t (τ φ)) s 0

modules.title: The Minkowski matrix over the integers
modules.doc:
The Minkowski matrix with integer entries, so that the kernel can evaluate it.

## i. Overview

The entries of `minkowskiMatrix` are integers, but it is a matrix over `ℝ`, and the kernel
cannot evaluate arithmetic in `ℝ`. Statements which a decision procedure has to evaluate are
therefore stated with `minkowskiMatrixZ`, the same diagonal matrix `diag(1, -1, …, -1)` taken
over `ℤ`. The bridge back is `minkowskiMatrixZ.cast_apply`, which casts an entry to the
corresponding entry of `minkowskiMatrix`; the remaining lemmas are the entry values and the
symmetry, matching the `minkowskiMatrix` API.

## ii. Key results

- `minkowskiMatrixZ` : the Minkowski matrix over `ℤ`.
- `minkowskiMatrixZ.cast_apply` : its cast to `ℝ` is `minkowskiMatrix`, entry by entry.
- `minkowskiMatrixZ.inl_0_inl_0`, `minkowskiMatrixZ.inr_i_inr_i`,
  `minkowskiMatrixZ.off_diag_zero` : the entries.
- `minkowskiMatrixZ.comm` : it is symmetric.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Minkowski matrix over the integers

## iv. References

The real Minkowski matrix and its API are in `Physlib.Relativity.MinkowskiMatrix`.

sections.text: ## A. The Minkowski matrix over the integers

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrixZ
declarations.doc:
The Minkowski matrix over the integers, `diag(1, -1, -1, ...)` in `ℤ`. Its cast to `ℝ` is
`minkowskiMatrix`, by `minkowskiMatrixZ.cast_apply`.
declarations.statement: def minkowskiMatrixZ {d : ℕ} : Matrix (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) ℤ

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrixZ.as_diagonal
declarations.doc: The integer Minkowski matrix as a diagonal matrix.
declarations.statement: lemma as_diagonal : @minkowskiMatrixZ d = diagonal (Sum.elim 1 (-1))

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrixZ.inl_0_inl_0
declarations.doc: The time-time component of the integer Minkowski matrix is `1`.
declarations.statement: lemma inl_0_inl_0 : @minkowskiMatrixZ d (Sum.inl 0) (Sum.inl 0) = 1

declarations.name: minkowskiMatrixZ.inr_i_inr_i
declarations.doc: The space diagonal components of the integer Minkowski matrix are `-1`.
declarations.statement: lemma inr_i_inr_i (i : Fin d) : @minkowskiMatrixZ d (Sum.inr i) (Sum.inr i) = -1
