lemma cast_apply (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    ((minkowskiMatrixZ μ ν : ℤ) : ℝ) = minkowskiMatrix μ ν

modules.title: Three anticommuting matrices are the most `2 × 2` can hold
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A family `τ` of `2 × 2` complex matrices is anticommuting when `τ_a τ_b + τ_b τ_a = 2 δ_ab 1`:
each `τ_a` squares to `1` and two different ones anticommute. Conjugating `τ_a` by another
member reverses its sign, so every member is traceless, and the trace pairs the members with
each other and with `1` orthonormally. Together with `1` they are linearly independent in the
four dimensional space of `2 × 2` matrices, so such a family has at most three members. The
Pauli matrices `σ1, σ2, σ3` attain the bound: they are a maximal anticommuting family, one for
each axis of space.

## ii. Key results

- `IsAnticommuting` : the relation `τ_a τ_b + τ_b τ_a = 2 δ_ab 1`.
- `IsAnticommuting.trace_mul`, `IsAnticommuting.trace_eq_zero` : the trace pairing.
- `IsAnticommuting.linearIndependent` : the members together with `1` are independent.
- `IsAnticommuting.card_le_three` : an anticommuting family has at most three members.
- `isAnticommuting_pauliMatrix` : the Pauli matrices are anticommuting.
- `isGreatest_card_isAnticommuting` : the largest anticommuting family has three members.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Anticommuting families
- B. At most three members
- C. The Pauli matrices attain the bound

## iv. References

* W. Pauli, *Zur Quantenmechanik des magnetischen Elektrons*, Z. Phys. 43 (1927) 601–623.

sections.text: ## A. Anticommuting families
## B. At most three members
## C. The Pauli matrices attain the bound

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.IsAnticommuting
declarations.doc: A family of `2 × 2` matrices with `τ_a τ_b + τ_b τ_a = 2 δ_ab 1`.
declarations.statement: def IsAnticommuting {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (τ : ι → Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) : Prop

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.IsAnticommuting.mul_self
declarations.statement: lemma mul_self (a : ι) : τ a * τ a = 1

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.IsAnticommuting.mul_comm_of_ne
declarations.statement: lemma mul_comm_of_ne {a b : ι} (h : a ≠ b) : τ b * τ a = -(τ a * τ b)

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.IsAnticommuting.trace_mul
declarations.doc: The trace pairs the members orthogonally: `tr (τ_a τ_b) = 2 δ_ab`.
declarations.statement: lemma trace_mul (a b : ι) : (τ a * τ b).trace = if a = b then 2 else 0

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.IsAnticommuting.trace_eq_zero
declarations.doc: In a family with at least two members, every member is traceless.
declarations.statement: lemma trace_eq_zero {a b : ι} (hab : b ≠ a) : (τ a).trace = 0

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.IsAnticommuting.linearIndependent
declarations.doc:
In a family with at least two members, the members together with `1` are linearly
independent.
declarations.statement:
lemma linearIndependent [Fintype ι] [Nontrivial ι] :
    LinearIndependent ℂ (fun o : Option ι => o.elim (1 : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) τ)

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.IsAnticommuting.card_le_three
declarations.doc: **An anticommuting family of `2 × 2` matrices has at most three members.**
declarations.statement: lemma card_le_three [Fintype ι] : Fintype.card ι ≤ 3

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.isAnticommuting_pauliMatrix
declarations.doc: The Pauli matrices `σ1, σ2, σ3` are an anticommuting family.
declarations.statement: lemma isAnticommuting_pauliMatrix : IsAnticommuting fun i : Fin 3 => pauliMatrix (Sum.inr i)

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.isGreatest_card_isAnticommuting
declarations.doc:
**The Pauli matrices are a maximal anticommuting family.** The largest anticommuting family
of `2 × 2` matrices has three members.
declarations.statement:
lemma isGreatest_card_isAnticommuting :
    IsGreatest {n : ℕ | ∃ τ : Fin n → Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ, IsAnticommuting τ} 3

modules.title: The covariant Pauli matrices as plain matrices
modules.doc:
The Pauli matrices with the vector index lowered, and their completeness relation.

## i. Overview

`Physlib.Relativity.PauliMatrices.SelfAdjoint` carries the Pauli matrices as self-adjoint
matrices and as the basis `pauliBasis'` of the self-adjoint `2 × 2` matrices. Contracting
them against tensor components needs them as plain matrices, which is `pauliLower μ`, the
matrix underlying `pauliSelfAdjoint' μ`; `pauliBasis'_coe` identifies it with the basis vector
and `pauliLower_eq_smul` with `η_{μμ} σ^μ`. The Fierz completeness relation
`sum_pauliLower_mul_pauliLower` then says that these four matrices span the `2 × 2` matrices,
with the trace pairing as the duality and normalisation `2`; it is the relation which turns a
sum over a Lorentz index into a pair of Kronecker deltas on the spinor indices.

## ii. Key results

- `PauliMatrix.pauliLower` : the covariant Pauli matrices as plain matrices.
- `PauliMatrix.pauliBasis'_coe` : they underlie the basis `pauliBasis'`.
- `PauliMatrix.pauliLower_eq_smul` : lowering the index multiplies by the metric entry.
- `PauliMatrix.sum_pauliLower_mul_pauliLower` : the Fierz completeness relation.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The covariant Pauli matrices as plain matrices

## iv. References

The self-adjoint Pauli matrices and the basis `pauliBasis'` are in
`Physlib.Relativity.PauliMatrices.SelfAdjoint`.

sections.text: ## A. The covariant Pauli matrices as plain matrices

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.pauliLower
declarations.doc:
The Pauli matrices with the vector index lowered by the Minkowski metric,
`σ_μ = η_{μμ} σ^μ`, as plain matrices: the underlying matrices of `pauliSelfAdjoint'`.
declarations.statement: def pauliLower (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.pauliBasis'_coe
declarations.doc: The covariant Pauli matrices are the underlying matrices of the basis `pauliBasis'`.
declarations.statement: lemma pauliBasis'_coe (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : (pauliBasis' μ).1 = pauliLower μ

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.pauliLower_eq_smul
declarations.doc: Lowering the vector index multiplies by the diagonal entry of the metric.
declarations.statement:
lemma pauliLower_eq_smul (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    pauliLower μ = ((minkowskiMatrixZ μ μ : ℤ) : ℂ) • pauliMatrix μ

declarations.name: PauliMatrix.sum_pauliLower_mul_pauliLower
declarations.doc:
The Fierz completeness relation: the covariant Pauli matrices span the `2 × 2` matrices,
with the trace pairing as the duality and normalisation `2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_pauliLower_mul_pauliLower (α α' β β' : Fin 2) :
    ∑ ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, pauliLower ρ β' β * pauliLower ρ α α'
      = 2 * ((if α = β then 1 else 0) * (if α' = β' then 1 else 0))

modules.title: The Poincaré group
modules.doc:
The Poincaré group acts on spacetime by Lorentz transformations and translations.

## i. Overview

An element of the Poincaré group is a pair of a translation `a` and a Lorentz transformation `Λ`.
It acts on a point `x` by `x ↦ Λ x + a`. The group is built from the existing `LorentzGroup d`
and the vector group of `SpaceTime d`. The file also defines the action on functions of
spacetime by `(g • u) x = u (g⁻¹ x)`. A group element is orthochronous when its Lorentz part is.
The action on functions sends the support of a function to the image of the support.

## ii. Key results

- `PoincareGroup` : the group of translations and Lorentz transformations.
- `PoincareGroup.IsOrthochronous` : the Lorentz part preserves the direction of time.
- `PoincareGroup.act` : the action on functions of spacetime.
- `PoincareGroup.tsupport_act` : the support of `g • u` is the image of the support of `u`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The group
- B. The action on spacetime
- C. Orthochronous elements
- D. Point reflections
- E. The action on functions

## iv. References

None.

## A. The group

- `PoincareGroup` : the group of translations and Lorentz transformations.

## B. The action on spacetime

- `PoincareGroup.toHomeomorph` : each element is a homeomorphism of spacetime.

## C. Orthochronous elements

- `PoincareGroup.IsOrthochronous` : the Lorentz part preserves the direction of time.

## D. Point reflections

- `PoincareGroup.pointReflection` : the point reflection `x ↦ p - x`.
- `PoincareGroup.not_isOrthochronous_pointReflection` : it is not orthochronous.

## E. The action on functions

- `PoincareGroup.act` : the action `(g • u) x = u (g⁻¹ x)` on functions of spacetime.

declarations.name: PoincareGroup
declarations.doc: The Poincaré group of `SpaceTime d`. An element `⟨a, Λ⟩` acts by `x ↦ Λ x + a`.
declarations.statement:
structure PoincareGroup (d : ℕ) where
  /-- The translation part. -/
  translation : SpaceTime d
  /-- The Lorentz part. -/
  lorentz : LorentzGroup d
instance : Group (PoincareGroup d)

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.translation_mul
declarations.doc: The translation part of a product.
declarations.statement:
lemma translation_mul (g h : PoincareGroup d) :
    (g * h).translation = g.translation + g.lorentz • h.translation

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.lorentz_mul
declarations.doc: The Lorentz part of a product.
declarations.statement: lemma lorentz_mul (g h : PoincareGroup d) : (g * h).lorentz = g.lorentz * h.lorentz

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.translation_inv
declarations.doc: The translation part of an inverse.
declarations.statement:
lemma translation_inv (g : PoincareGroup d) :
    g⁻¹.translation = -(g.lorentz⁻¹ • g.translation)

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.lorentz_inv
declarations.doc: The Lorentz part of an inverse.
declarations.statement: lemma lorentz_inv (g : PoincareGroup d) : g⁻¹.lorentz = g.lorentz⁻¹

declarations.doc: The Poincaré group acts on spacetime by `x ↦ Λ x + a`.
declarations.statement: instance : MulAction (PoincareGroup d) (SpaceTime d)

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.smul_def
declarations.doc: The action on a point.
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_def (g : PoincareGroup d) (x : SpaceTime d) :
    g • x = g.lorentz • x + g.translation

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.toHomeomorph
declarations.doc: Each element is a homeomorphism of spacetime.
declarations.statement: def toHomeomorph (g : PoincareGroup d) : SpaceTime d ≃ₜ SpaceTime d

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.toHomeomorph_apply
declarations.doc: The homeomorphism acts as the point action.
declarations.statement: lemma toHomeomorph_apply (g : PoincareGroup d) (x : SpaceTime d) : g.toHomeomorph x = g • x

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.toHomeomorph_symm_apply
declarations.doc: The inverse homeomorphism acts as the inverse point action.
declarations.statement:
lemma toHomeomorph_symm_apply (g : PoincareGroup d) (x : SpaceTime d) :
    g.toHomeomorph.symm x = g⁻¹ • x

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.isCompact_smul
declarations.doc: The image of a compact set under a Poincaré transformation is compact.
declarations.statement:
lemma isCompact_smul (g : PoincareGroup d) {K : Set (SpaceTime d)} (hK : IsCompact K) :
    IsCompact (g • K)

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.IsOrthochronous
declarations.doc: A Poincaré element is orthochronous when its Lorentz part preserves the direction of time.
declarations.statement: def IsOrthochronous (g : PoincareGroup d) : Prop

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.isOrthochronous_one
declarations.doc: The identity is orthochronous.
declarations.statement: lemma isOrthochronous_one : IsOrthochronous (1 : PoincareGroup d)

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.IsOrthochronous.mul
declarations.doc: Products of orthochronous elements are orthochronous.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsOrthochronous.mul {g h : PoincareGroup d} (hg : IsOrthochronous g)
    (hh : IsOrthochronous h) : IsOrthochronous (g * h)

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.IsOrthochronous.inv
declarations.doc: Inverses of orthochronous elements are orthochronous.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsOrthochronous.inv {g : PoincareGroup d} (hg : IsOrthochronous g) :
    IsOrthochronous g⁻¹

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.pointReflection
declarations.doc: The point reflection `x ↦ p - x` as a Poincaré transformation.
declarations.statement: def pointReflection (p : SpaceTime d) : PoincareGroup d

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.pointReflection_smul
declarations.doc: The point reflection sends `x` to `p - x`.
declarations.statement: lemma pointReflection_smul (p x : SpaceTime d) : pointReflection p • x = p - x

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.not_isOrthochronous_pointReflection
declarations.doc: The point reflection is not orthochronous.
declarations.statement:
lemma not_isOrthochronous_pointReflection (p : SpaceTime d) :
    ¬ (pointReflection p).IsOrthochronous

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.act
declarations.doc: The action on functions of spacetime: `(g • u) x = u (g⁻¹ x)`.
declarations.statement: def act (g : PoincareGroup d) (u : SpaceTime d → V) : SpaceTime d → V

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.act_apply
declarations.doc: The value of the transformed function.
declarations.statement:
lemma act_apply (g : PoincareGroup d) (u : SpaceTime d → V) (x : SpaceTime d) :
    act g u x = u (g⁻¹ • x)

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.act_one
declarations.doc: The identity acts trivially.
declarations.statement: lemma act_one (u : SpaceTime d → V) : act (1 : PoincareGroup d) u = u

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.act_mul
declarations.doc: The action is a left action.
declarations.statement:
lemma act_mul (g h : PoincareGroup d) (u : SpaceTime d → V) :
    act (g * h) u = act g (act h u)

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.act_inv_act
declarations.doc: The action of an element and its inverse cancel.
declarations.statement: lemma act_inv_act (g : PoincareGroup d) (u : SpaceTime d → V) : act g⁻¹ (act g u) = u

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.act_add
declarations.doc: The action commutes with addition.
declarations.statement:
lemma act_add [AddCommGroup V] (g : PoincareGroup d) (u v : SpaceTime d → V) :
    act g (u + v) = act g u + act g v

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.act_smul
declarations.doc: The action commutes with scalar multiplication.
declarations.statement:
lemma act_smul {R : Type*} [SMul R V] (g : PoincareGroup d) (c : R) (u : SpaceTime d → V) :
    act g (c • u) = c • act g u

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.tsupport_act
declarations.doc: The support of the transformed function is the image of the support.
declarations.statement:
lemma tsupport_act [Zero V] (g : PoincareGroup d) (u : SpaceTime d → V) :
    tsupport (act g u) = g • tsupport u

modules.title: The causal structure is Poincaré invariant
modules.doc:
Orthochronous Poincaré transformations preserve causal futures and pasts.

## i. Overview

An event `q` causally follows `p` when the difference lies in the closed future light cone.
A Lorentz transformation preserves the Minkowski product. An orthochronous one also preserves the
direction of time, so it maps the future light cone to itself. A translation does not change
differences. So an orthochronous Poincaré transformation maps the causal future of a set to the
causal future of the image. A transformation that reverses time exchanges causal future and past.

## ii. Key results

- `causallyFollows_zero_smul` : orthochronous Lorentz maps preserve the future light cone.
- `causallyFollows_smul_iff` : orthochronous Poincaré maps preserve causal order.
- `causalFuture_smul` : the causal future of the image is the image of the causal future.
- `causalFuture_smul_of_not` : a time-reversing map sends the causal future to the causal past.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The future light cone
- B. The causal order
- C. Causal futures and pasts of sets

## iv. References

None.

## A. The future light cone

- `causallyFollows_zero_smul` : orthochronous Lorentz maps preserve the future light cone.

## B. The causal order

- `causallyFollows_smul_iff` : orthochronous Poincaré maps preserve causal order.

## C. Causal futures and pasts of sets

- `causalFuture_smul` : the causal future of the image is the image of the causal future.

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.timeComponent_eq_minkowski
declarations.doc: The time component is the Minkowski product with the unit time vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma timeComponent_eq_minkowski (p : SpaceTime d) :
    p.timeComponent = ⟪p, Lorentz.Vector.basis (Sum.inl 0)⟫ₘ

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.causallyFollows_zero_smul
declarations.doc: An orthochronous Lorentz transformation maps the closed future light cone into itself.
declarations.statement:
lemma causallyFollows_zero_smul {Λ : LorentzGroup d} (hΛ : LorentzGroup.IsOrthochronous Λ)
    {u : SpaceTime d} (hu : causallyFollows 0 u) : causallyFollows 0 (Λ • u)

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.smul_sub_smul
declarations.doc: The vectors between two transformed events are the Lorentz image of the original vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_sub_smul (g : PoincareGroup d) (p q : SpaceTime d) :
    g • q - g • p = g.lorentz • (q - p)

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.causallyFollows_zero_smul_iff
declarations.doc: An orthochronous Lorentz transformation preserves the closed future light cone.
declarations.statement:
lemma causallyFollows_zero_smul_iff {Λ : LorentzGroup d} (hΛ : LorentzGroup.IsOrthochronous Λ)
    (u : SpaceTime d) : causallyFollows 0 (Λ • u) ↔ causallyFollows 0 u

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.causallyFollows_smul_iff
declarations.doc: An orthochronous Poincaré transformation preserves the causal order.
declarations.statement:

modules.title: The Poincaré action on test functions and distributions
modules.doc:
The Poincaré group acts on test functions by pullback and on distributions by transposition.

## i. Overview

A Poincaré element `g` acts on a test function by `(g • φ) x = φ (g⁻¹ x)`. The action is
continuous on the space of test functions because pullback by a Lorentz transformation and by a
translation are. A distribution `T` is transformed by `(g • T) φ = T (g⁻¹ • φ)`. Then the
delta distribution at `p` goes to the delta distribution at `g p`. A distribution that vanishes
outside a set goes to a distribution that vanishes outside the image of the set.

## ii. Key results

- `PoincareGroup.actTestFunction` : the action on test functions.
- `PoincareGroup.actDist` : the action on distributions.
- `PoincareGroup.isVanishingOn_actDist` : the support of a transformed distribution.
- `PoincareGroup.actDist_delta` : the action sends a delta distribution to a delta distribution.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Test functions
- B. Distributions

## iv. References

None.

## A. Test functions

- `PoincareGroup.actTestFunction` : the action on test functions.

## B. Distributions

- `PoincareGroup.actDist` : the action on distributions.

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.lorentzCLE
declarations.doc: A Lorentz transformation as a continuous linear equivalence of spacetime.
declarations.statement: def lorentzCLE (Λ : LorentzGroup d) : SpaceTime d ≃L[ℝ] SpaceTime d

declarations.statement:
lemma abs_det_lorentzCLE (Λ : LorentzGroup d) :
    |LinearMap.det (lorentzCLE Λ : SpaceTime d →ₗ[ℝ] SpaceTime d)| = 1

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.actTestFunction
declarations.doc: The action of the Poincaré group on test functions.
declarations.statement:
def actTestFunction (g : PoincareGroup d) :
    𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), F) →L[ℝ] 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), F)

declarations.doc: The value of a transformed test function.
declarations.statement:
lemma actTestFunction_apply (g : PoincareGroup d) (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), F))
    (x : SpaceTime d) : actTestFunction g φ x = φ (g⁻¹ • x)

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.actTestFunction_translation_inv
declarations.doc: The inverse of a pure translation acts on test functions as the translate `x ↦ φ (x + p)`.
declarations.statement:

    actTestFunction (⟨p, 1⟩ : PoincareGroup d)⁻¹ φ = TestFunction.precompTranslationCLM p φ

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.actTestFunction_one
declarations.doc: The identity acts trivially on test functions.
declarations.statement:
lemma actTestFunction_one (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), F)) :
    actTestFunction (1 : PoincareGroup d) φ = φ

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.actTestFunction_mul
declarations.doc: The action on test functions is a left action.
declarations.statement:
lemma actTestFunction_mul (g h : PoincareGroup d) (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), F)) :
    actTestFunction (g * h) φ = actTestFunction g (actTestFunction h φ)

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.tsupport_actTestFunction

declarations.statement:
lemma tsupport_actTestFunction (g : PoincareGroup d) (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), F)) :
    tsupport (actTestFunction g φ) = g • tsupport φ

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.actDist
declarations.doc: The action of the Poincaré group on distributions: `(g • T) φ = T (g⁻¹ • φ)`.
declarations.statement: def actDist (g : PoincareGroup d) : DistributionField d V →L[ℝ] DistributionField d V

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.actDist_apply
declarations.doc: The value of a transformed distribution.
declarations.statement:
lemma actDist_apply (g : PoincareGroup d) (T : DistributionField d V)
    (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) : actDist g T φ = T (actTestFunction g⁻¹ φ)

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.actDist_one
declarations.doc: The identity acts trivially on distributions.
declarations.statement: lemma actDist_one (T : DistributionField d V) : actDist (1 : PoincareGroup d) T = T

declarations.doc: The action on distributions is a left action.
declarations.statement:
lemma actDist_mul (g h : PoincareGroup d) (T : DistributionField d V) :
    actDist (g * h) T = actDist g (actDist h T)

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.isVanishingOn_actDist
declarations.doc: A transformed distribution vanishes outside the image of the set.

declarations.name: PoincareGroup.actDist_delta
declarations.doc: The action sends a delta distribution to a delta distribution.
declarations.statement:
lemma actDist_delta (g : PoincareGroup d) (p : SpaceTime d) :
    actDist g (Distribution.delta p : DistributionField d ℝ) = Distribution.delta (g • p)

modules.title: The Poincaré action on smooth fields
modules.doc:
The Poincaré group acts on smooth fields and on compactly supported smooth fields.

## i. Overview

The action `(g • u) x = u (g⁻¹ x)` sends smooth functions to smooth functions. It is linear and
it sends the support to the image of the support. So it preserves compact support. The file
restricts the action to the submodule of smooth fields and to the submodule of test fields.

## ii. Key results

- `PoincareGroup.actSmooth` : the action as a linear map on smooth fields.
- `PoincareGroup.actTest` : the action as a linear map on test fields.
- `PoincareGroup.tsupport_actSmooth` : the support of a transformed field.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Smooth fields
- B. Test fields

## iv. References

None.

## A. Smooth fields

- `PoincareGroup.actSmooth` : the action as a linear map on smooth fields.

## B. Test fields

- `PoincareGroup.actTest` : the action as a linear map on test fields.

modules.title: The cyclic rotation and the half turns
modules.doc:
The rotation cycling the spatial axes, and the rotations by `π` about a coordinate axis.

## i. Overview

`Physlib.Relativity.SL2C.AxisRotations` carries the rotations taking the `z`-axis to a chosen
coordinate axis. Two further distinguished rotations are added here, both of which act on the
Lorentz index by a permutation or a sign and so can be used to relabel the axes in a
classification.

The cyclic rotation `rotationCycle` is the rotation by `2π/3` about the diagonal spatial axis.
Its Lorentz matrix is the permutation matrix of `cycDir`, the permutation fixing time and
sending `x → y → z → x`. Since `cycDir` has order three, an index family not fixed by it has
three distinct rotations, which is `cycDir_orbit_distinct`: that is what lets one axis of a
three-axis statement be proved and the other two obtained by relabelling.

The half turn `halfTurn k` is the rotation by `π` about the axis `k`, taken as the lift
`-i σ_k`. Its Lorentz matrix is diagonal: it fixes time and the axis and negates the two
transverse directions, with the signs recorded by `halfTurnSign`.

The spatial-axis convention is `0 = x`, `1 = y`, `2 = z`.

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.cycDir` : the cyclic permutation of Lorentz direction labels.
- `Lorentz.cycDir_cycDir_cycDir`, `Lorentz.cycDir_orbit_distinct` : it has order three, and an
  index family it does not fix has three distinct rotations.
- `Lorentz.SL2C.rotationCycle` : the cyclic rotation in `SL(2, ℂ)`.
- `Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup_rotationCycle_apply` : its Lorentz matrix is the permutation
  matrix of `cycDir`.
- `Lorentz.halfTurnSign`, `Lorentz.SL2C.halfTurn` : the half turn about a coordinate axis.
- `Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup_halfTurn_apply` : its diagonal Lorentz matrix.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The cyclic coordinate rotation
- B. Half turns about the coordinate axes

## iv. References

The rotations from the `z`-axis to a coordinate axis are in
`Physlib.Relativity.SL2C.AxisRotations`.

sections.text: ## A. The cyclic coordinate rotation

## B. Half turns about the coordinate axes

The half turn about the axis `k` is the rotation by `π` about it. It has two lifts to
`SL(2,ℂ)`, `-i σ_k` and `i σ_k`, which differ by the central element `-1` and have the same
Lorentz matrix. The chosen lift `halfTurn k` is `-i σ_k`, the value at `θ = π` of
`cos (θ / 2) - i sin (θ / 2) σ_k`, the convention `rotationCycle` also follows. Its Lorentz
matrix is diagonal: it fixes time and the axis and negates the two transverse directions, with
the signs recorded by `halfTurnSign`.

declarations.name: Lorentz.cycDir
declarations.doc:
The cyclic permutation of Lorentz direction labels: time is fixed and the spatial
directions rotate as `x → y → z → x`.
declarations.statement: def cycDir : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3

declarations.name: Lorentz.cycDir_inl
declarations.doc: The cyclic permutation fixes the time direction.
declarations.statement: lemma cycDir_inl : cycDir (Sum.inl 0) = Sum.inl 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.cycDir_inr
declarations.doc: The cyclic permutation advances a spatial direction by one.
declarations.statement: lemma cycDir_inr (m : Fin 3) : cycDir (Sum.inr m) = Sum.inr (m + 1)

declarations.name: Lorentz.cycDir_comp_two
declarations.doc: Composing the cyclic permutation with a two-slot index vector rotates both entries.
declarations.statement:
lemma cycDir_comp_two (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (fun j => cycDir (![μ, ν] j)) = ![cycDir μ, cycDir ν]

declarations.name: Lorentz.cycDir_comp_one
declarations.doc: Composing the cyclic permutation with a one-slot index vector rotates its entry.
declarations.statement:
lemma cycDir_comp_one (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (fun j => cycDir (![μ] j)) = ![cycDir μ]

declarations.name: Lorentz.cycDir_comp_nil
declarations.doc: Composing the cyclic permutation with the empty index vector is the empty vector.
declarations.statement: lemma cycDir_comp_nil : (fun j : Fin 0 => cycDir (![] j)) = ![]

declarations.name: Lorentz.cycDir_cycDir_cycDir
declarations.doc: The cyclic permutation of Lorentz direction labels has order three.
declarations.statement: lemma cycDir_cycDir_cycDir (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : cycDir (cycDir (cycDir μ)) = μ

declarations.name: Lorentz.cycDir_injective
declarations.doc:
The cyclic permutation of Lorentz direction labels is injective: applying it twice
more returns the original label.
declarations.statement: lemma cycDir_injective : Function.Injective cycDir

declarations.name: Lorentz.cycDir_orbit_distinct
declarations.doc: An index not fixed by the rotation has three distinct rotations.
declarations.statement:
lemma cycDir_orbit_distinct {ι : Type*} (d : ι → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (hd : (fun s => cycDir (d s)) ≠ d) :
    (fun s => cycDir (cycDir (d s))) ≠ d
      ∧ (fun s => cycDir (cycDir (d s))) ≠ (fun s => cycDir (d s))

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.rotationCycle
declarations.doc:
The cyclic rotation `x → y → z → x` in `SL(2,ℂ)`, realized as the rotation by
`2π/3` about the diagonal spatial axis.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def rotationCycle : SL(2,ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup_rotationCycle_apply
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz matrix of `rotationCycle`: it is the permutation matrix associated with
`cycDir`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toLorentzGroup_rotationCycle_apply (a b : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (toLorentzGroup rotationCycle).1 a b = if a = cycDir b then 1 else 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.halfTurnSign
declarations.doc:
The sign the half turn about the axis `k` gives a direction: `1` on time and on the axis,
`-1` on the two transverse directions.
declarations.statement: def halfTurnSign (k : Fin 3) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : ℤ

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.halfTurn
declarations.doc:
The half turn about the axis `k`, the rotation by `π` about it, as the element `-i σ_k` of
`SL(2,ℂ)`. The other lift `i σ_k` is `-halfTurn k`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def halfTurn : Fin 3 → SL(2,ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.halfTurn_zero_apply
declarations.doc: The matrix entries of the half turn about the `x`-axis, `-i σ_x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma halfTurn_zero_apply (j k : Fin 2) :
    (halfTurn 0).1 j k = (!![0, -Complex.I; -Complex.I, 0]) j k

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.halfTurn_one_apply
declarations.doc: The matrix entries of the half turn about the `y`-axis, `-i σ_y`.
declarations.statement:
lemma halfTurn_one_apply (j k : Fin 2) :
    (halfTurn 1).1 j k = (!![0, -1; 1, 0] : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) j k

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.halfTurn_two_apply
declarations.doc: The matrix entries of the half turn about the `z`-axis, `-i σ_z`.
declarations.statement:
lemma halfTurn_two_apply (j k : Fin 2) :
    (halfTurn 2).1 j k = (!![-Complex.I, 0; 0, Complex.I]) j k

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup_halfTurn_apply
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz matrix of the half turn about the axis `k` is diagonal, with the signs
`halfTurnSign k`: it fixes time and the axis and negates the two transverse directions.
declarations.statement:
lemma toLorentzGroup_halfTurn_apply (k : Fin 3) (a b : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (toLorentzGroup (halfTurn k)).1 a b = if a = b then (halfTurnSign k a : ℝ) else 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup_halfTurn_symm
declarations.doc: The Lorentz matrix of the half turn is diagonal, hence symmetric.
declarations.statement:
lemma toLorentzGroup_halfTurn_symm (k : Fin 3) (a b : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (toLorentzGroup (halfTurn k)).1 a b = (toLorentzGroup (halfTurn k)).1 b a

modules.title: Conjugation and the kernel of the covering map
modules.doc:
Entrywise conjugation on `SL(2, ℂ)`, and the covering map on `-1`, on entries and on adjoints.

## i. Overview

Three things about the covering map `SL(2, ℂ) →* LorentzGroup 3` are collected here, all
needed to carry a Lorentz index through a spinor computation.

Entrywise complex conjugation is a monoid endomorphism `conjHom` of `SL(2, ℂ)`, an involution,
and conjugating the group argument undoes the conjugation of the entries: the inverse
conjugate transpose at `conjHom g` is the inverse transpose at `g`. This is what lets a
right-handed slot be treated as a conjugated left-handed one.

The covering map sandwiches, `A ↦ M A Mᴴ`, so the two signs of `-1` cancel and
`toLorentzGroup (-1) = 1`: the map is two-to-one. It also intertwines conjugate transposition
with matrix transposition, `L(M†) = L(M)ᵀ`.

Finally `sum_pauliLower_mul_sl2c` is the defining intertwining identity read entrywise:
sandwiching `σ_μ` between `g` and `gᴴ` mixes the covariant Pauli matrices by the column `μ` of
the Lorentz matrix of `g`.

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.SL2C.conjHom` : entrywise conjugation as a monoid endomorphism.
- `Lorentz.SL2C.conjHom_involutive`, `Lorentz.SL2C.conjHom_inv_conjTranspose` : its
  involutivity, and its effect on the inverse conjugate transpose.
- `Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup_neg_one` : the centre covers the identity.
- `Lorentz.SL2C.sum_pauliLower_mul_sl2c` : the intertwining identity on entries.
- `Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup_conjTranspose` : `L(M†) = L(M)ᵀ`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Entrywise conjugation
- B. The kernel of the covering map
- C. The intertwining identity on entries
- D. The covering map and adjoints

## iv. References

The covering map and its properties are in `Physlib.Relativity.SL2C.Basic`.

sections.text: ## A. Entrywise conjugation
## B. The kernel of the covering map
## C. The intertwining identity on entries
## D. The covering map and adjoints

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.conjHom
declarations.doc:
Entrywise complex conjugation as a monoid endomorphism of `SL(2,ℂ)`: Mathlib's
`SpecialLinearGroup.map` along `starRingEnd ℂ`.
declarations.statement: abbrev conjHom : SL(2,ℂ) →* SL(2,ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.conjHom_coe
declarations.statement: lemma conjHom_coe (g : SL(2,ℂ)) : (conjHom g).1 = g.1.map star

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.conjHom_involutive
declarations.doc: Conjugation is an involution, hence surjective.
declarations.statement: lemma conjHom_involutive : Function.Involutive conjHom

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.conjHom_inv_conjTranspose
declarations.doc:
Conjugating the group argument undoes the conjugation of the entries: the inverse
conjugate transpose at `conjHom g` is the inverse transpose at `g`.
declarations.statement: lemma conjHom_inv_conjTranspose (g : SL(2,ℂ)) : (((conjHom g).1)⁻¹)ᴴ = (g.1⁻¹)ᵀ

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup_neg_one
declarations.doc:
**The centre of `SL(2, ℂ)` covers the identity Lorentz transformation.** The covering
map sandwiches, `A ↦ M A Mᴴ`, so the two signs of `-1` cancel. Together with
`_root_.map_one` this says that the covering map is two-to-one.
declarations.statement: lemma toLorentzGroup_neg_one : toLorentzGroup (-1) = 1

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.sum_pauliLower_mul_sl2c
declarations.doc:
The intertwining identity `toSelfAdjointMap_basis` read entrywise: sandwiching the
covariant Pauli matrix `σ_μ` between `g` and `gᴴ` mixes the covariant Pauli matrices by the
column `μ` of the Lorentz matrix of `g`, the summed Lorentz index first.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_pauliLower_mul_sl2c (g : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (β β' : Fin 2) :
    ∑ p : Fin 2 × Fin 2, PauliMatrix.pauliLower μ p.1 p.2 * (g.1 β p.1 * star (g.1 β' p.2))
      = ∑ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, (((toLorentzGroup g).1 ν μ : ℝ) : ℂ)
        * PauliMatrix.pauliLower ν β β'

declarations.name: Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup_conjTranspose
declarations.doc:
The covering map intertwines conjugate transposition with matrix
transposition: `L(M†) = L(M)ᵀ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toLorentzGroup_conjTranspose {M N : SL(2,ℂ)} (hN : N.1 = M.1ᴴ) :
    (toLorentzGroup N).1 = (toLorentzGroup M).1ᵀ

modules.title: The metrics are the unique invariant tensors with two indices of one colour
modules.doc:
Up to scale, the metric of a colour is the only invariant tensor with two indices of that colour.

## i. Overview

A tensor with two indices of colour `k` is `fromPairT` of an element of the tensor square of the
representation of that colour. The invariants of that tensor square are the line through the
metric, for the four-vectors, the covectors and each of the four Weyl representations, so the
invariant tensors of `ℂT[k, k]` are the line through `metricTensor k` (A). For an equivariant map
`f` out of `ℂT[k, k]`, every Lorentz invariant of the range of `f` is a multiple of
`f (metricTensor k)`, modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule, the shape of a mass term (B).

The colours `fun _ : Fin 2 => .up` of two four-vector indices are a reindexing of `![.up, .up]`,
so the invariant tensors with these colours are the line through the reindexed metric
`RankTwo.metric`, whose components are the Minkowski metric (C).

## ii. Key results

- `complexLorentzTensor.invariants_pair_eq_span_metricTensor` : the invariant tensors with two
  indices of one colour are the line through the metric.
- `Lorentz.invariantReductionToMetricTensor` : the invariants of the range of an equivariant map
  reduce to the image of the metric.
- `complexLorentzTensor.invariants_up_pow_two_eq_span_metric` : the same for the colours

modules.title: The metrics are the unique invariants
modules.doc:
Up to scale, the Minkowski metric is the only invariant of two complex Lorentz vector indices.

## i. Overview

On `ComplexVector ⊗ ComplexVector` the group `SL(2, ℂ)` acts on the matrix of components by
`Y ↦ Λ Y Λᵀ`, with `Λ` the complexified Lorentz matrix. The complexified Minkowski matrix `η`
squares to the identity and gives `Λ⁻¹ = η Λᵀ η` (A), so the other orderings of upper and lower
indices reduce to this action after multiplying by `η`.

Let `F` be a linear map out of the matrices which intertwines `Y ↦ Λ Y Λᵀ` with an action on `B`,
and let `F X` be invariant (B). The three half turns act by diagonal sign matrices, and averaging
over them keeps only the diagonal, so `F X` is the image of the diagonal of `X` (B.1). For a
diagonal `D` the boost along the axis `i` changes only the time and `i` entries of the diagonal,
by a multiple of `d_t + d_i`, so `(d_t + d_i) • F P_i = 0`, where `P_i` projects onto the plane
of time and the axis `i` (B.2). The cyclic rotation of the axes carries `P_i` to `P_{i+1}`, so
the three `F P_i` vanish together (B.3). If they vanish, `F D` and `F η` are both multiples of
the image of the time projection, and otherwise `D` is a multiple of `η`. Either way `F X` is a
multiple of `F η` (B.4).

The result follows for any tensor product whose matrix of components carries this action (C).
On two contravariant indices the invariants of the tensor product are the line through the metric
(D). The same holds for two covariant indices, through the matrix of components conjugated by `η`
(E).

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.map_eq_smul_map_minkowskiMatrix_of_invariant` : on matrices with the action
  `Y ↦ Λ Y Λᵀ`, an invariant in the image of an equivariant map is a multiple of the image of `η`.
- `Lorentz.ComplexVector.invariants_tprod_eq_span_metricVal` : the invariants of
  `ComplexVector ⊗ ComplexVector` are the line through the metric.
- `Lorentz.ComplexCoVector.invariants_tprod_eq_span_metricVal` : the same for
  `ComplexCoVector ⊗ ComplexCoVector`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The complexified Minkowski matrix
- B. Invariants in the image of an equivariant map on matrices
  - B.1. The diagonal part
  - B.2. Boosts
  - B.3. Cycling the axes
  - B.4. Invariants are multiples of the image of the metric
- C. Tensor products with a matrix of components
- D. Two contravariant indices
- E. Two covariant indices

## iv. References

The metrics are in `Physlib.Relativity.Tensors.ComplexTensor.Metrics.Pre`, where these results are
written to move, and sections D and E settle the `TODO` in that file on the uniqueness of the
metrics. The matrices of components are in `Physlib.Relativity.Tensors.ComplexTensor.Matrix.Pre`,
the half turns and the cyclic rotation in `PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.SL2C.AxisRotations`, and the
axis boosts in `Physlib.Relativity.LorentzGroup.Boosts.Axis`. The analogous results for two Weyl
indices are in `PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.Fermions.Weyl.Metric`.

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.minkowskiMatrix_map_mul_self
declarations.doc: The complexified Minkowski matrix squares to the identity.
declarations.statement:
lemma minkowskiMatrix_map_mul_self :
    (@minkowskiMatrix d).map ofRealHom * (@minkowskiMatrix d).map ofRealHom = 1

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.minkowskiMatrix_map_mul_minkowskiMatrix_map_mul
declarations.doc: Multiplying twice by the complexified Minkowski matrix is the identity.
declarations.statement:
lemma minkowskiMatrix_map_mul_minkowskiMatrix_map_mul
    (X : Matrix (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) ℂ) :
    (@minkowskiMatrix d).map ofRealHom * ((@minkowskiMatrix d).map ofRealHom * X) = X

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.transpose_minkowskiMatrix_map
declarations.doc: The complexified Minkowski matrix is symmetric.
declarations.statement:
lemma transpose_minkowskiMatrix_map :
    ((@minkowskiMatrix d).map ofRealHom)ᵀ = (@minkowskiMatrix d).map ofRealHom

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.inv_toComplex
declarations.doc: The inverse of a complexified Lorentz matrix is `η Λᵀ η`.
declarations.statement:
lemma inv_toComplex (Λ : LorentzGroup d) : (toComplex Λ)⁻¹ =
    minkowskiMatrix.map ofRealHom * (toComplex Λ)ᵀ * minkowskiMatrix.map ofRealHom

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.minkowskiMatrix_map_mul_inv_toComplex
declarations.doc: Moving `Λ⁻¹` across `η` turns it into `Λᵀ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma minkowskiMatrix_map_mul_inv_toComplex (Λ : LorentzGroup d) :
    minkowskiMatrix.map ofRealHom * (toComplex Λ)⁻¹ =
      (toComplex Λ)ᵀ * minkowskiMatrix.map ofRealHom

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.inv_toComplex_transpose_mul_minkowskiMatrix_map
declarations.doc: Moving `Λ⁻¹ᵀ` across `η` turns it into `Λ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma inv_toComplex_transpose_mul_minkowskiMatrix_map (Λ : LorentzGroup d) :
    (toComplex Λ)⁻¹ᵀ * minkowskiMatrix.map ofRealHom =
      minkowskiMatrix.map ofRealHom * toComplex Λ

declarations.name: LorentzGroup.inv_toComplex_transpose_mul_conj_minkowskiMatrix_map
declarations.doc:
Conjugating by `η` turns the action `X ↦ Λ⁻¹ᵀ X Λ⁻¹` on two covariant indices into the
action `Y ↦ Λ Y Λᵀ` on two contravariant indices.
declarations.statement:
lemma inv_toComplex_transpose_mul_conj_minkowskiMatrix_map (Λ : LorentzGroup d)
    (Y : Matrix (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) ℂ) :
    (toComplex Λ)⁻¹ᵀ * (minkowskiMatrix.map ofRealHom * Y * minkowskiMatrix.map ofRealHom) *
      (toComplex Λ)⁻¹ = minkowskiMatrix.map ofRealHom * (toComplex Λ * Y * (toComplex Λ)ᵀ) *
      minkowskiMatrix.map ofRealHom

declarations.name: Lorentz.toComplex_toLorentzGroup_halfTurn
declarations.doc:
The complexified Lorentz matrix of the half turn about the axis `k` is the diagonal matrix of
the signs `halfTurnSign k`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toComplex_toLorentzGroup_halfTurn (k : Fin 3) :
    LorentzGroup.toComplex (SL2C.toLorentzGroup (SL2C.halfTurn k)) =
      diagonal fun μ => (halfTurnSign k μ : ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.add_sum_halfTurnSign_conj
declarations.doc: Adding a matrix to its conjugates by the three half turns keeps four times its diagonal.
declarations.statement:
lemma add_sum_halfTurnSign_conj (Y : Matrix (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) ℂ) :
    Y + ∑ k, diagonal (fun μ => (halfTurnSign k μ : ℂ)) * Y *
      (diagonal fun μ => (halfTurnSign k μ : ℂ))ᵀ = (4 : ℂ) • diagonal fun μ => Y μ μ

declarations.name: Lorentz.map_eq_map_diagonal_of_invariant
declarations.doc: When `F Y` is invariant, it is the image of the diagonal of `Y`.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_eq_map_diagonal_of_invariant
    (hF : ∀ g Y, F (LorentzGroup.toComplex (SL2C.toLorentzGroup g) * Y *
      (LorentzGroup.toComplex (SL2C.toLorentzGroup g))ᵀ) = ρ g (F Y))
    {Y : Matrix (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) ℂ} (hY : ∀ g, ρ g (F Y) = F Y) :
    F Y = F (diagonal fun μ => Y μ μ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.timeAxisProj
declarations.doc:
The projection onto the plane of time and the axis `i`, the diagonal matrix with `1` in the
time and `i` slots and `0` in the other two.
declarations.statement: def timeAxisProj (i : Fin 3) : Matrix (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) ℂ

declarations.name: Lorentz.diagonal_boost_conj_sub
declarations.doc:
The boost along the axis `i` with parameter `2` changes the diagonal of a diagonal matrix
`diagonal d` only in the time and `i` slots, by `(225 / 64) (d_t + d_i)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma diagonal_boost_conj_sub (i : Fin 3) (d : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 → ℂ) :
    (diagonal fun μ => (LorentzGroup.toComplex (SL2C.toLorentzGroup
      (SL2C.boostAxis i 2 two_ne_zero)) * diagonal d * (LorentzGroup.toComplex
      (SL2C.toLorentzGroup (SL2C.boostAxis i 2 two_ne_zero)))ᵀ) μ μ) - diagonal d =
      ((225 / 64 : ℂ) * (d (Sum.inl 0) + d (Sum.inr i))) • timeAxisProj i

declarations.name: Lorentz.add_smul_map_timeAxisProj_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
When `F (diagonal d)` is invariant, `d_t + d_i` kills the image of the projection onto the
plane of time and the axis `i`.
declarations.statement:
lemma add_smul_map_timeAxisProj_eq_zero
    (hF : ∀ g Y, F (LorentzGroup.toComplex (SL2C.toLorentzGroup g) * Y *
      (LorentzGroup.toComplex (SL2C.toLorentzGroup g))ᵀ) = ρ g (F Y))
    {d : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 → ℂ} (hd : ∀ g, ρ g (F (diagonal d)) = F (diagonal d)) (i : Fin 3) :
    (d (Sum.inl 0) + d (Sum.inr i)) • F (timeAxisProj i) = 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.rotationCycle_conj_timeAxisProj
declarations.doc:
The cyclic rotation of the axes carries the projection onto the plane of time and the axis
`i` to that of the axis `i + 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma rotationCycle_conj_timeAxisProj (i : Fin 3) :
    LorentzGroup.toComplex (SL2C.toLorentzGroup SL2C.rotationCycle) * timeAxisProj i *
      (LorentzGroup.toComplex (SL2C.toLorentzGroup SL2C.rotationCycle))ᵀ =
      timeAxisProj (i + 1)

declarations.name: Lorentz.map_timeAxisProj_eq_zero_of_eq_zero
declarations.doc: The images of the projections onto the three planes of time and an axis vanish together.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_timeAxisProj_eq_zero_of_eq_zero
    (hF : ∀ g Y, F (LorentzGroup.toComplex (SL2C.toLorentzGroup g) * Y *
      (LorentzGroup.toComplex (SL2C.toLorentzGroup g))ᵀ) = ρ g (F Y))
    {i : Fin 3} (h : F (timeAxisProj i) = 0) (j : Fin 3) : F (timeAxisProj j) = 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.diagonal_eq_sum_timeAxisProj
declarations.doc:
A diagonal matrix in terms of the time projection and the projections onto the planes of
time and an axis.
declarations.statement:
lemma diagonal_eq_sum_timeAxisProj (d : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 → ℂ) :
    diagonal d = (d (Sum.inl 0) - ∑ i, d (Sum.inr i)) • diagonal (Pi.single (Sum.inl 0) 1) +
      ∑ i, d (Sum.inr i) • timeAxisProj i

declarations.name: Lorentz.minkowskiMatrix_map_eq_sum_timeAxisProj
declarations.doc:
The complexified Minkowski matrix in terms of the time projection and the projections onto
the planes of time and an axis.
declarations.statement:
lemma minkowskiMatrix_map_eq_sum_timeAxisProj :
    minkowskiMatrix.map ofRealHom =
      (4 : ℂ) • diagonal (Pi.single (Sum.inl 0) 1) - ∑ i, timeAxisProj i

declarations.name: Lorentz.diagonal_eq_smul_minkowskiMatrix_map
declarations.doc: A diagonal matrix with `d_t + d_i = 0` for each axis `i` is `d_t η`.

declarations.name: Lorentz.map_diagonal_eq_smul_of_invariant
declarations.doc:
When `F (diagonal d)` is invariant, it is a multiple of `F η`. If the images of the
projections onto the planes of time and an axis vanish, both are multiples of the image of the
time projection, and otherwise `diagonal d` is a multiple of `η`.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_diagonal_eq_smul_of_invariant
    (hF : ∀ g Y, F (LorentzGroup.toComplex (SL2C.toLorentzGroup g) * Y *
      (LorentzGroup.toComplex (SL2C.toLorentzGroup g))ᵀ) = ρ g (F Y))
    {d : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 → ℂ} (hd : ∀ g, ρ g (F (diagonal d)) = F (diagonal d)) :
    ∃ c : ℂ, F (diagonal d) = c • F (minkowskiMatrix.map ofRealHom)

declarations.name: Lorentz.map_eq_smul_map_minkowskiMatrix_of_invariant
declarations.doc:
When `F X` is invariant, it is a multiple of the image `F η` of the complexified Minkowski
matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_eq_smul_map_minkowskiMatrix_of_invariant
    (hF : ∀ g Y, F (LorentzGroup.toComplex (SL2C.toLorentzGroup g) * Y *
      (LorentzGroup.toComplex (SL2C.toLorentzGroup g))ᵀ) = ρ g (F Y))
    {X : Matrix (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) ℂ} (hX : ∀ g, ρ g (F X) = F X) :
    ∃ c : ℂ, F X = c • F (minkowskiMatrix.map ofRealHom)

declarations.name: Lorentz.invariants_eq_span_map_minkowskiMatrix
declarations.doc:
Let `T` be a linear map from the matrices onto `V` which intertwines `Y ↦ Λ Y Λᵀ` with the
action on `V`. The invariants of `V` are the line through `T η`.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_eq_span_map_minkowskiMatrix {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V]
    [Module ℂ V] {σ : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) V}
    (T : Matrix (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) ℂ →ₗ[ℂ] V) (hT : Function.Surjective T)
    (hσ : ∀ g Y, T (LorentzGroup.toComplex (SL2C.toLorentzGroup g) * Y *
      (LorentzGroup.toComplex (SL2C.toLorentzGroup g))ᵀ) = σ g (T Y)) :
    σ.invariants = ℂ ∙ T (minkowskiMatrix.map ofRealHom)

declarations.doc: Up to scale, the metric `ηᵃᵃ` is the unique invariant of `ComplexVector ⊗ ComplexVector`.

modules.title: The units are the unique invariants
modules.doc:
Up to scale, the unit `δ` is the only invariant of a complex Lorentz vector index and a covector
index.

## i. Overview

On `ComplexVector ⊗ ComplexCoVector` the group `SL(2, ℂ)` acts on the matrix of components by
`X ↦ Λ X Λ⁻¹`, and on `ComplexCoVector ⊗ ComplexVector` by `X ↦ Λ⁻¹ᵀ X Λᵀ`, with `Λ` the
complexified Lorentz matrix. Since `Λ⁻¹ = η Λᵀ η`, multiplying the matrix of components by the
complexified Minkowski matrix `η` on the right, respectively on the left, turns either action into
the action `Y ↦ Λ Y Λᵀ` on two contravariant indices (A). The classification of invariants for that
action in `PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.Tensors.ComplexTensor.Metrics.Pre` then applies, and `η` goes to
`η η = 1`, the matrix of components of the unit. For each of the two orderings the invariants of
the tensor product are the line through the unit (B, C).

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.ComplexCoVector.invariants_tprod_eq_span_unitVal` : the invariants of
  `ComplexVector ⊗ ComplexCoVector` are the line through the unit.
- `Lorentz.ComplexVector.invariants_tprod_eq_span_unitVal` : the same for
  `ComplexCoVector ⊗ ComplexVector`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Reparametrising the mixed actions by the Minkowski matrix
- B. A contravariant then a covariant index
- C. A covariant then a contravariant index

## iv. References

The units are in `Physlib.Relativity.Tensors.ComplexTensor.Units.Pre`, where these results are
written to move. The analogous results for Weyl fermions are in
`PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.Fermions.Weyl.Unit`.
