modules.title: The dual of the complex covector representation
modules.doc:
How dual complex covectors transform, on the dual basis.

## i. Overview

A covector representation induces one on the dual space, and a classification of invariant
tensors has to know how the dual basis transforms. For the complex covectors
`Lorentz.ComplexCoVector` the answer is that dual covectors transform contravariantly: the dual
basis vector `e^μ` goes to the combination of dual basis vectors given by the column `μ` of the
complexified Lorentz matrix. This is the complex analogue of
`Lorentz.CoVector.sl2Rep_dual_dualBasis`, and is obtained from
`Representation.dual_apply_dualBasis` with the transposed inverse matrix read off from
`Lorentz.ComplexCoVector.basis_ρ_apply`.

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.ComplexCoVector.SL2CRep_dual_dualBasis` : dual complex covectors transform by the columns
  of the complexified Lorentz matrix.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The dual representation on the dual basis

## iv. References

The complex covector representation is in
`Physlib.Relativity.Tensors.ComplexTensor.Vector.Basic`.

sections.text: ## A. The dual representation on the dual basis

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexCoVector.SL2CRep_dual_dualBasis
declarations.doc:
The dual of the complex covector representation on the dual basis: dual covectors
transform contravariantly, by the columns of the (complexified) Lorentz matrix. The
complex analogue of `Lorentz.CoVector.sl2Rep_dual_dualBasis`.
declarations.statement:
lemma ComplexCoVector.SL2CRep_dual_dualBasis (Λ : SL(2,ℂ))
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    Lorentz.ComplexCoVector.SL2CRep.dual Λ (Lorentz.ComplexCoVector.basis.dualBasis μ) =
      ∑ j, (((Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 j μ : ℝ) : ℂ) •
        Lorentz.ComplexCoVector.basis.dualBasis j

modules.title: The contraction tensors of four four-vector indices
modules.doc:
The Lorentz invariants of four four-vector indices are spanned by the three pairings of the
metric and the Levi-Civita symbol.

## i. Overview

A rank-four tensor `T^{μνρσ}` has `4 ^ 4 = 256` components, and four invariant tensors can be
contracted with it:

* `η_{μν} η_{ρσ}`, `η_{μρ} η_{νσ}` and `η_{μσ} η_{νρ}`, the three pairings of the metric,
* `ε_{μνρσ}`, the Levi-Civita symbol.

These are the tensors `contractionTensor i`. There are no others: the invariant tensors are the
span of the four,
`complexLorentzTensor.invariants_up_pow_four_eq_span_range_contractionTensor` (I). For an
equivariant map `f : ℂT(fun _ : Fin 4 => .up) →ₗ[ℂ] B`, the invariants of
`LinearMap.range f ⊔ S`, for `S` a Lorentz-stable submodule, therefore reduce to the span of the
four images `f (contractionTensor i)`, `ComplexVector.reducesInvariantsTo_span_contractionTensor`.
The fourth tensor is a pseudoscalar, so it would drop out if reflections were allowed. For a
given `f` the four images may be dependent or zero. When `f` is antisymmetric under exchanging
its last two slots, two images already span: that of `η_{μρ} η_{νσ}` and that of `ε_{μνρσ}` (F).
When `f` is moreover symmetric under exchanging its first two slots, both of those vanish too (G).

The four tensors are invariant, by `Λ η Λᵀ = η` and `det Λ = 1` (D, E), and linearly
independent (H). That they span every invariant is seen through Weyl spinors (I). The Pauli
matrices change each four-vector index into a bispinor index, a left-handed and a right-handed
Weyl index, injectively and equivariantly (`complexLorentzTensor.pauliTensorMap`). On the Weyl
side the invariants are products of those of the four left-handed and of the four right-handed
indices, two pairings `ε ε` for each chirality, so they span a space of dimension at most four
(`complexLorentzTensor.invariants_upL_pow_four_upR_pow_four_eq_span_range_bispinorPairing`).
The four tensors are independent, so they span every invariant.

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.RankFour.contractionTensor` : the four invariant tensors.
- `Lorentz.RankFour.linearIndependent_contractionTensor` : they are linearly independent.
- `complexLorentzTensor.invariants_up_pow_four_eq_span_range_contractionTensor` : the invariant
  tensors are their span.
- `Lorentz.ComplexVector.reducesInvariantsTo_span_contractionTensor` : the invariants of the
  range of `f` reduce to the span of their images.
- `Lorentz.RankFour.span_range_contractionTensor_of_antisymm` : for a map antisymmetric in its
  last two slots, two of the four images span.
- `Lorentz.RankFour.apply_contractionTensor_one_of_symm_of_antisymm`,
  `Lorentz.RankFour.apply_contractionTensor_three_of_symm` : symmetry in the first two slots
  kills those two images.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Coefficient tensors
- B. The four invariant tensors
- C. The metric, the Levi-Civita symbol and the invariant tensors
- D. The four coefficient tensors are invariant
- E. The four tensors are Lorentz invariant
- F. Exchanging the last two slots
- G. Exchanging the first two slots
- H. The four tensors are independent
- I. The classification of the invariants

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Coefficient tensors

A direction is an element of `Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3`, time or one of the three axes; an index vector
`d : Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3` puts one in each slot, and a coefficient tensor `c` assigns a
number to each. The components of a tensor, relabelled this way, are its coefficient tensor,
`coeffEquiv 4`, on which `g` acts by

`(act Λ c) a = ∑_d c_d Λ_{a₀ d₀} ⋯ Λ_{a₃ d₃}`,

with `a` free and `d` summed (`coeffEquiv_smul`), and a tensor is invariant exactly when its
coefficient tensor is `IsInvariantCoeff` (`invariant_iff_isInvariantCoeff`). Everything in this
paragraph is stated for any number of slots in
`PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.Tensors.ComplexTensor.Vector.InvariantCoeff`, and used here at four.

## B. The four invariant tensors

## C. The metric, the Levi-Civita symbol and the invariant tensors

The metric is `minkowskiMatrixZ`, the integer form of `minkowskiMatrix`, and the symbol is
`leviCivitaSymbol`, read on an index vector through `finSumFinEquiv`. Both are integer valued.
The metric pairings use the slots `(0,1)(2,3)`, `(0,2)(1,3)` and `(0,3)(1,2)`;
`contractionCoeff` holds the four coefficient tensors and `contractionTensor` the four tensors
with those coefficients, in that order.

## D. The four coefficient tensors are invariant

`Λ η Λᵀ = η` defines the Lorentz group; entry by entry it is
`LorentzGroup.sum_minkowskiMatrixZ_mul`, and a pair of metrics is two copies of it, one per
pair of slots (`act_outerPair`). The inner and split pairings are the outer one with the slots
permuted (`act_outerPair_comp`). The symbol against
four rows of `M` gives `det M` times the symbol of those rows (`sum_leviCivitaSymbol_mul_prod`),
and `det Λ = 1` here: the only use of the determinant, and the reason there are four invariants
and not three, a reflection having `det = -1`. `sum_pi_four` is bookkeeping.
## E. The four tensors are Lorentz invariant

## F. Exchanging the last two slots

Exchanging the slots `2` and `3`, `permT (Equiv.swap 2 3)`, fixes `η_{μν} η_{ρσ}`, the metric
being symmetric, and exchanges `η_{μρ} η_{νσ}` with `η_{μσ} η_{νρ}`. So a linear map `f` out of
the tensors with `f ∘ₗ permT (Equiv.swap 2 3) = -f` sends the first tensor to zero and the
third to minus the second, and the four images span what the second and the Levi-Civita image
span. Neither equivariance of `f` nor any structure on `B` beyond a complex module is used; the
two remaining images may still be dependent or zero.

## G. Exchanging the first two slots

Exchanging the slots `0` and `1`, `permT (Equiv.swap 0 1)`, exchanges `η_{μρ} η_{νσ}` with
`η_{μσ} η_{νρ}` and negates `ε_{μνρσ}`. So a linear map `f` out of the tensors with
`f ∘ₗ permT (Equiv.swap 0 1) = f` sends `ε_{μνρσ}` to zero, and if `f` is also antisymmetric in
its last two slots it sends `η_{μρ} η_{νσ}` to zero as well: in both a symmetric pair of slots
is contracted against an antisymmetric one. As in F nothing beyond a complex module is used.

## H. The four tensors are independent

At `t t x x`, `t x t x`, `t x x t` and `t x y z` exactly one of the four coefficient tensors is
nonzero, so the four coefficient tensors, and with them the four tensors, are linearly
independent.

## I. The classification of the invariants

The Pauli matrices change each four-vector index into a bispinor index, a left-handed and a
right-handed Weyl index, which is an injective equivariant map
`complexLorentzTensor.pauliTensorMap 4` into the tensors with four left-handed and then four
right-handed Weyl indices. Its image of the invariant tensors lies in their invariants, the span of
the four products of pairings `ε ε ⊗ ε̄ ε̄`
(`complexLorentzTensor.invariants_upL_pow_four_upR_pow_four_eq_span_range_bispinorPairing`). So
the invariant tensors have dimension at most four, and the four linearly independent invariant
tensors `contractionTensor i` span them. With them comes the reduction of the invariants of
`LinearMap.range f ⊔ S` to the span of the four images `f (contractionTensor i)`.

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.contractionCoeff
declarations.doc: The four coefficient tensors, the three metric pairings, then the Levi-Civita symbol.
declarations.statement: def contractionCoeff : Fin 4 → (Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℤ

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.contractionTensor
declarations.doc:
The four invariant tensors with four contravariant indices, `η_{μν} η_{ρσ}`,
`η_{μρ} η_{νσ}`, `η_{μσ} η_{νρ}` and `ε_{μνρσ}`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def contractionTensor (i : Fin 4) : ℂT(fun _ : Fin 4 => Color.up)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.liftComponents_contractionTensor
declarations.doc:
`liftComponents T` sends each invariant tensor to the contraction of `T` with its
coefficients.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_contractionTensor (T : (Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B) (i : Fin 4) :
    liftComponents T (contractionTensor i)
      = ∑ d, ((contractionCoeff i d : ℤ) : ℂ) • T d

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.sum_pi_four
declarations.doc: A sum over index vectors is a fourfold sum over directions.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_pi_four {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] (F : (Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M) :
    ∑ d : Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, F d
      = ∑ x : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, ∑ y : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, ∑ z : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3,
        ∑ w : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, F ![x, y, z, w]

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.act_outerPair
declarations.doc:
The pairing of slots `(0,1)` and `(2,3)` is fixed, by two copies of
`LorentzGroup.sum_minkowskiMatrixZ_mul`.
declarations.statement:
lemma act_outerPair (Λ : LorentzGroup 3) (a : Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    act Λ.1 (fun d => ((minkowskiMatrixZ (d 0) (d 1) * minkowskiMatrixZ (d 2) (d 3) : ℤ) : ℂ)) a
      = ((minkowskiMatrixZ (a 0) (a 1) * minkowskiMatrixZ (a 2) (a 3) : ℤ) : ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.act_outerPair_comp
declarations.doc: The same for the slots permuted by `σ`, by renaming the summation variable.
declarations.statement:
lemma act_outerPair_comp (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin 4)) (Λ : LorentzGroup 3)
    (a : Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    act Λ.1 (fun d => ((minkowskiMatrixZ (d (σ 0)) (d (σ 1))
        * minkowskiMatrixZ (d (σ 2)) (d (σ 3)) : ℤ) : ℂ)) a
      = ((minkowskiMatrixZ (a (σ 0)) (a (σ 1))
        * minkowskiMatrixZ (a (σ 2)) (a (σ 3)) : ℤ) : ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.act_leviCivitaSymbol
declarations.doc:
The symbol is fixed by a Lorentz matrix of determinant `1`; in general it picks up `det Λ`,
by `sum_leviCivitaSymbol_mul_prod`.
declarations.statement:
lemma act_leviCivitaSymbol (Λ : LorentzGroup 3) (hΛ : Λ.1.det = 1) (a : Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    act Λ.1 (fun d => ((leviCivitaSymbol fun μ => d (finSumFinEquiv μ) : ℤ) : ℂ)) a
      = ((leviCivitaSymbol fun μ => a (finSumFinEquiv μ) : ℤ) : ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.isInvariantCoeff_contractionCoeff
declarations.doc: The four coefficient tensors are invariant.
declarations.statement:
lemma isInvariantCoeff_contractionCoeff (i : Fin 4) :
    IsInvariantCoeff fun d => ((contractionCoeff i d : ℤ) : ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.contractionTensor_invariant
declarations.doc: Each of the four tensors is Lorentz invariant, its coefficient tensor being invariant.
declarations.statement:
lemma contractionTensor_invariant (i : Fin 4) (g : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    g • contractionTensor i = contractionTensor i

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.isReindexing_swap_two_three
declarations.doc: Exchanging the last two of four contravariant slots is a reindexing.
declarations.statement:
lemma isReindexing_swap_two_three :
    Tensor.IsReindexing (fun _ : Fin 4 => Color.up) (fun _ => Color.up)
      ⇑(Equiv.swap (2 : Fin 4) 3)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.permT_swap_two_three_contractionTensor_zero
declarations.doc: `η_{μν} η_{ρσ}` is unchanged by exchanging its last two slots.
declarations.statement:
lemma permT_swap_two_three_contractionTensor_zero :
    Tensor.permT _ isReindexing_swap_two_three (contractionTensor 0) = contractionTensor 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.permT_swap_two_three_contractionTensor_one
declarations.doc: Exchanging the last two slots of `η_{μρ} η_{νσ}` gives `η_{μσ} η_{νρ}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma permT_swap_two_three_contractionTensor_one :
    Tensor.permT _ isReindexing_swap_two_three (contractionTensor 1) = contractionTensor 2

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.apply_contractionTensor_zero_of_antisymm
declarations.doc: A map antisymmetric in the last two slots sends `η_{μν} η_{ρσ}` to zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_contractionTensor_zero_of_antisymm
    (hf : f ∘ₗ Tensor.permT _ isReindexing_swap_two_three = -f) :
    f (contractionTensor 0) = 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.apply_contractionTensor_two_of_antisymm
declarations.doc:
A map antisymmetric in the last two slots sends `η_{μσ} η_{νρ}` to minus the image of
`η_{μρ} η_{νσ}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_contractionTensor_two_of_antisymm
    (hf : f ∘ₗ Tensor.permT _ isReindexing_swap_two_three = -f) :
    f (contractionTensor 2) = -f (contractionTensor 1)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.span_range_contractionTensor_of_antisymm
declarations.doc:
For a map antisymmetric in the last two slots, the images of the four invariant tensors
span the same as the images of `η_{μρ} η_{νσ}` and `ε_{μνρσ}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma span_range_contractionTensor_of_antisymm
    (hf : f ∘ₗ Tensor.permT _ isReindexing_swap_two_three = -f) :
    Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun i => f (contractionTensor i))
      = Submodule.span ℂ {f (contractionTensor 1), f (contractionTensor 3)}

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.isReindexing_swap_zero_one
declarations.doc: Exchanging the first two of four contravariant slots is a reindexing.
declarations.statement:
lemma isReindexing_swap_zero_one :
    Tensor.IsReindexing (fun _ : Fin 4 => Color.up) (fun _ => Color.up)
      ⇑(Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 4) 1)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.permT_swap_zero_one_contractionTensor_one
declarations.doc: Exchanging the first two slots of `η_{μρ} η_{νσ}` gives `η_{μσ} η_{νρ}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma permT_swap_zero_one_contractionTensor_one :
    Tensor.permT _ isReindexing_swap_zero_one (contractionTensor 1) = contractionTensor 2

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.permT_swap_zero_one_contractionTensor_three
declarations.doc: Exchanging the first two slots negates `ε_{μνρσ}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma permT_swap_zero_one_contractionTensor_three :
    Tensor.permT _ isReindexing_swap_zero_one (contractionTensor 3) = -contractionTensor 3

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.apply_contractionTensor_one_of_symm_of_antisymm
declarations.doc:
A map symmetric in the first two slots and antisymmetric in the last two sends
`η_{μρ} η_{νσ}` to zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_contractionTensor_one_of_symm_of_antisymm
    (hs : f ∘ₗ Tensor.permT _ isReindexing_swap_zero_one = f)
    (ha : f ∘ₗ Tensor.permT _ isReindexing_swap_two_three = -f) :
    f (contractionTensor 1) = 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.apply_contractionTensor_three_of_symm
declarations.doc: A map symmetric in the first two slots sends `ε_{μνρσ}` to zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_contractionTensor_three_of_symm
    (hs : f ∘ₗ Tensor.permT _ isReindexing_swap_zero_one = f) :
    f (contractionTensor 3) = 0

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.linearIndependent_contractionCoeff
declarations.doc: The four coefficient tensors are linearly independent.
declarations.statement:
lemma linearIndependent_contractionCoeff :
    LinearIndependent ℂ fun i d => ((contractionCoeff i d : ℤ) : ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.RankFour.linearIndependent_contractionTensor
declarations.doc: The four tensors are linearly independent.
declarations.statement: lemma linearIndependent_contractionTensor : LinearIndependent ℂ contractionTensor

declarations.name: complexLorentzTensor.invariants_up_pow_four_eq_span_range_contractionTensor
declarations.doc:
The invariant tensors with four four-vector indices are the span of the four
`contractionTensor i`.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.complexLorentzTensor.invariants_up_pow_four_eq_span_range_contractionTensor :
    (complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep (fun _ : Fin 4 => Color.up)).invariants =
      Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range contractionTensor)

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector.reducesInvariantsTo_span_contractionTensor
declarations.doc:
The invariants of the range of `f` reduce to the span of the images of the four invariant
tensors.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.Lorentz.ComplexVector.reducesInvariantsTo_span_contractionTensor
    (hf : complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant (fun _ : Fin 4 => .up) repLorentz f) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (fun g : SL(2,ℂ) => repLorentz g) (LinearMap.range f)
      (Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun i => f (contractionTensor i)))

modules.title: Invariant coefficient tensors of the complex vector representation
modules.doc:
Invariant coefficient tensors on spacetime indices, and equivariant maps out of the tensors with
`n` four-vector indices.

## i. Overview

The tensors `ℂT(fun _ : Fin n => .up)` with `n` contravariant indices are the `n`-th tensor power
of the complex vector representation `ComplexVector`. This file holds the machinery that the
classifications of their invariants use: the odd ranks in
`PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.Bispinors.ComplexifiedAction`, rank two in
`PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.Tensors.ComplexTensor.Metrics.Basic` and rank four in
`PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.Tensors.ComplexTensor.Vector.ContractionTensor`.

A real `4 × 4` matrix acts on coefficient tensors one factor per slot, `Invariants.act`, and an
invariant coefficient tensor is one fixed by the Lorentz matrix of every element of `SL(2, ℂ)`
(A). Section B collects sums over index vectors.

The components of a tensor, relabelled by `Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3` in each slot, are a coefficient tensor,
`coeffEquiv` (C), on which `SL(2,ℂ)` acts by `Invariants.act`. An invariant tensor therefore has
an invariant coefficient tensor, `Invariants.IsInvariantCoeff`, and a classification of the
invariant coefficient tensors is a classification of the invariant tensors (D).

A family `T` of vectors indexed by `n` directions is the map `liftComponents T`, sending each basis
tensor to the matching vector, and it is equivariant exactly when the vectors obey the
transformation law of the components of a tensor (E, `isEquivariant_liftComponents_up_iff`),

`repLorentz g (T l) = ∑_a (∏ i, Λ(g)_{a i, l i}) • T a`,

with `l` free and `a` summed, and the summed index first in each factor of the Lorentz matrix
`Λ(g)` of `g`. Permuting the slots by `permT σ` reads the coefficient tensor and the family at
permuted index vectors (`permT_coeffEquiv_symm`, `liftComponents_comp_permT`). Products of a family
with a Lorentz-inert element or with a Lorentz vector are again such families (F).

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.Invariants.IsInvariantCoeff` : invariant coefficient tensors.
- `Lorentz.coeffEquiv` : the components of a tensor with `n` four-vector indices, as a coefficient
  tensor.
- `Lorentz.invariant_iff_isInvariantCoeff` : a tensor is invariant exactly when its coefficient
  tensor is.
- `Lorentz.invariants_tensorRep_le_map` : the invariant tensors come from the invariant
  coefficient tensors.
- `Lorentz.isEquivariant_liftComponents_up_iff` : the map of a family is equivariant exactly when
  the family obeys the transformation law.
- `Lorentz.isEquivariant_liftComponents_up_mul_fixed`,
  `Lorentz.isEquivariant_liftComponents_up_mul_vector` : products of a family with a Lorentz-inert
  element or with a Lorentz vector.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Coefficient tensors on spacetime indices
- B. Sums over index vectors
- C. Coefficient tensors
- D. Invariant tensors from invariant coefficient tensors
- E. Maps from components
- F. Products of families in an algebra

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Coefficient tensors on spacetime indices
## B. Sums over index vectors
## C. Coefficient tensors
## D. Invariant tensors from invariant coefficient tensors
## E. Maps from components

## F. Products of families in an algebra

When the families take values in an algebra on which `SL(2,ℂ)` acts multiplicatively, a family
times a Lorentz-inert element keeps its rank, and a rank-two family times a Lorentz vector is a
rank-three family.

declarations.name: Lorentz.Invariants.act
declarations.doc:
The action of a real `4 × 4` matrix on coefficient tensors, one factor per slot:
`(act Λ c) a = ∑_d c_d Λ_{a₀ d₀} ⋯`, with `a` free and `d` summed.
declarations.statement:
def act (Λ : Matrix (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) ℝ)
    (c : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ) (a : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : ℂ

declarations.name: Lorentz.Invariants.IsInvariantCoeff
declarations.doc: A coefficient tensor fixed by `act` of the Lorentz matrix of every `g : SL(2,ℂ)`.
declarations.statement: def IsInvariantCoeff (c : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ) : Prop

declarations.name: Lorentz.sum_pi_fin_two
declarations.doc: A sum over families of two four-vector indices is a double sum.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_pi_fin_two {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] (f : (Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M) :
    ∑ d : Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, f d
      = ∑ x : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, ∑ y : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, f ![x, y]

declarations.name: Lorentz.sum_pi_fin_zero
declarations.doc: A sum over families of no four-vector indices is its single term.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_pi_fin_zero {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] (f : (Fin 0 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M) :
    ∑ d : Fin 0 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, f d = f ![]

declarations.name: Lorentz.sum_pi_fin_one
declarations.doc: A sum over families of one four-vector index is a single sum.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_pi_fin_one {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] (f : (Fin 1 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M) :
    ∑ d : Fin 1 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, f d = ∑ x : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, f ![x]

declarations.name: Lorentz.vecCons_fin_one_eta
declarations.doc: A family of one four-vector index is the tuple of its own entry.
declarations.statement: lemma vecCons_fin_one_eta (l : Fin 1 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : ![l 0] = l

declarations.name: Lorentz.sum_pi_fin_three
declarations.doc: A sum over families of three four-vector indices is a triple sum.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_pi_fin_three {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] (f : (Fin 3 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M) :
    ∑ d : Fin 3 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, f d
      = ∑ x : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, ∑ y : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, ∑ z : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, f ![x, y, z]

declarations.name: Lorentz.vectorIdx
declarations.doc:
The component indices of a tensor with `n` contravariant indices, which are labelled by
`Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3` in each slot.

declarations.name: Lorentz.vectorIdx_symm_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma vectorIdx_symm_apply (d : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (i : Fin n) :
    (vectorIdx n).symm d i = d i

declarations.name: Lorentz.coeffEquiv
declarations.doc:
The components of a tensor with `n` contravariant indices, as a coefficient tensor, the
component equivalence of the species for the labels `vectorIdx n`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def coeffEquiv (n : ℕ) :
    ℂT(fun _ : Fin n => Color.up) ≃ₗ[ℂ] ((Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.coeffEquiv_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma coeffEquiv_apply (t : ℂT(fun _ : Fin n => Color.up)) (d : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    coeffEquiv n t d = (Tensor.basis _).repr t ((vectorIdx n).symm d)

declarations.name: Lorentz.coeffEquiv_symm_apply
declarations.doc:
The tensor with coefficient tensor `c` is the combination of the basis tensors with those
coefficients.
declarations.statement:
lemma coeffEquiv_symm_apply (c : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ) :
    (coeffEquiv n).symm c = ∑ d, c d • Tensor.basis _ ((vectorIdx n).symm d)

declarations.name: Lorentz.permT_coeffEquiv_symm
declarations.doc:
Permuting the slots of a tensor by `σ` permutes its coefficient tensor: slot `i` of
`permT σ h t` holds slot `σ i` of `t`, so the new coefficient at `d` is the old one at
`d ∘ σ.symm`.
declarations.statement:
lemma permT_coeffEquiv_symm (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n))
    (h : IsReindexing (fun _ : Fin n => Color.up) (fun _ => Color.up) σ)
    (c : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ) :
    permT σ h ((coeffEquiv n).symm c) = (coeffEquiv n).symm fun d => c (d ∘ σ.symm)

declarations.name: Lorentz.coeffEquiv_smul
declarations.doc:
The action of `g` on tensors is the action `act` of its Lorentz matrix on coefficient
tensors.
declarations.statement:
lemma coeffEquiv_smul (g : SL(2,ℂ)) (t : ℂT(fun _ : Fin n => Color.up)) :
    coeffEquiv n (g • t) = act (SL2C.toLorentzGroup g).1 (coeffEquiv n t)

declarations.name: Lorentz.invariant_iff_isInvariantCoeff
declarations.doc:
A tensor is invariant exactly when its coefficient tensor is an invariant coefficient
tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariant_iff_isInvariantCoeff (t : ℂT(fun _ : Fin n => Color.up)) :
    (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), g • t = t) ↔ IsInvariantCoeff (coeffEquiv n t)

declarations.name: Lorentz.invariants_tensorRep_le_map
declarations.doc:
The invariant tensors lie in the image of any submodule `K` of coefficient tensors which
contains every invariant coefficient tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_tensorRep_le_map {n : ℕ} {K : Submodule ℂ ((Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ)}
    (hK : ∀ c, IsInvariantCoeff c → c ∈ K) :
    (complexLorentzTensor.tensorRep (fun _ : Fin n => Color.up)).invariants ≤
      K.map (coeffEquiv n).symm.toLinearMap

declarations.name: Lorentz.liftComponents_coeffEquiv_symm
declarations.doc: The map of a family contracts the coefficient tensor of its argument with the family.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_coeffEquiv_symm (T : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B)
    (c : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ) :
    liftComponents T ((coeffEquiv n).symm c)
      = ∑ d, c d • T d

declarations.name: Lorentz.liftComponents_comp_permT
declarations.doc:
Precomposing the map of a family with the slot permutation `permT σ` reads the family at the
permuted index vectors `d ∘ σ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_comp_permT (σ : Fin n → Fin n)
    (h : IsReindexing (fun _ : Fin n => Color.up) (fun _ => Color.up) σ)
    (T : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B) :
    liftComponents (S := complexLorentzTensor) (c := fun _ : Fin n => .up) T ∘ₗ permT σ h
      = liftComponents (S := complexLorentzTensor) (c := fun _ : Fin n => .up) fun d => T (d ∘ σ)

declarations.name: Lorentz.liftComponents_comp_permT_eq_neg
declarations.doc:
A family antisymmetric under reading its index vectors through `σ` gives a map
antisymmetric under `permT σ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_comp_permT_eq_neg (σ : Fin n → Fin n)
    (h : IsReindexing (fun _ : Fin n => Color.up) (fun _ => Color.up) σ)
    {T : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B} (hT : ∀ d, T (d ∘ σ) = -T d) :
    liftComponents (S := complexLorentzTensor) (c := fun _ : Fin n => .up) T ∘ₗ permT σ h
      = -liftComponents (S := complexLorentzTensor) (c := fun _ : Fin n => .up) T

declarations.name: Lorentz.liftComponents_comp_permT_eq_self
declarations.doc:
A family symmetric under reading its index vectors through `σ` gives a map invariant under
`permT σ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_comp_permT_eq_self (σ : Fin n → Fin n)
    (h : IsReindexing (fun _ : Fin n => Color.up) (fun _ => Color.up) σ)
    {T : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B} (hT : ∀ d, T (d ∘ σ) = T d) :
    liftComponents (S := complexLorentzTensor) (c := fun _ : Fin n => .up) T ∘ₗ permT σ h
      = liftComponents (S := complexLorentzTensor) (c := fun _ : Fin n => .up) T

declarations.name: Lorentz.isEquivariant_liftComponents_up_iff
declarations.doc:
The map of a family is equivariant exactly when the family obeys the transformation law of
the components of a tensor with `n` four-vector indices.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_liftComponents_up_iff {repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) B}
    (T : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B) :
    complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant (fun _ : Fin n => .up) repLorentz (liftComponents T) ↔
      ∀ (g : SL(2,ℂ)) l, repLorentz g (T l) = ∑ a : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3,
        (∏ i, (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup g).1 (a i) (l i) : ℝ) : ℂ)) • T a

declarations.name: Lorentz.isEquivariant_liftComponents_up_mul_fixed
declarations.doc:
Multiplying a Lorentz tensor family by a Lorentz-inert element gives a family of the
same rank, the element riding through the transformation law untouched.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_liftComponents_up_mul_fixed {n : ℕ}
    (hmul : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x y : B), repLorentz Λ (x * y) = repLorentz Λ x * repLorentz Λ y)
    {T : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B}
    (hT : complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant (fun _ : Fin n => .up) repLorentz (liftComponents T))
    {y : B} (hy : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g y = y) :
    complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant (fun _ : Fin n => .up) repLorentz
      (liftComponents fun d => T d * y)

declarations.name: Lorentz.isEquivariant_liftComponents_up_mul_vector
declarations.doc:
A rank-two family against a Lorentz vector is a rank-three family, the two covector
indices of the first factor and the single index of the second make three.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_liftComponents_up_mul_vector
    (hmul : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x y : B), repLorentz Λ (x * y) = repLorentz Λ x * repLorentz Λ y)
    {T : (Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B}
    (hT : complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant (fun _ : Fin 2 => .up) repLorentz (liftComponents T))
    {U : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B}
    (hU : ∀ (g : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3), repLorentz g (U μ)
      = ∑ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup g).1 ν μ : ℝ) : ℂ) • U ν) :
    complexLorentzTensor.IsEquivariant (fun _ : Fin 3 => .up) repLorentz
      (liftComponents fun d : Fin 3 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 => T ![d 0, d 1] * U (d 2))

modules.title: Complex four-vectors as tensors
modules.doc:
Complex four-vectors are the complex Lorentz tensors with one contravariant index.

## i. Overview

A complex four-vector is a complex Lorentz tensor with a single index of colour `.up`, and
`fromSingleT` is the linear equivalence between the two. It makes `Lorentz.ComplexVector` a
tensorial type, so that tensor products of it with other tensorial types are tensorial through
`TensorSpecies.Tensorial.prod`. The equivalence carries the action of `SL(2, ℂ)` on four-vectors to
the action on tensors, and the basis vector `e_μ` to the basis tensor with the single component
`μ` (A).

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.ComplexVector.tensorial` : complex four-vectors are the tensors with one index `.up`.
- `Lorentz.ComplexVector.toTensor_SL2CRep` : the equivalence intertwines the two actions.
- `Lorentz.ComplexVector.toTensor_basis` : the basis vector `e_μ` is the basis tensor with
  component `μ`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The tensorial instance

## iv. References

The tensorial class is in `Physlib.Relativity.Tensors.Tensorial`. The instance for real
four-vectors is in `Physlib.Relativity.Tensors.RealTensor.Vector.Tensorial`.

sections.text: ## A. The tensorial instance

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector.tensorial
declarations.doc:
Complex four-vectors are the complex Lorentz tensors with one index `.up`, through
`fromSingleT`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance tensorial : Tensorial complexLorentzTensor ![.up] ComplexVector

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector.toTensor_eq_fromSingleT
declarations.statement:
lemma toTensor_eq_fromSingleT (v : ComplexVector) :
    toTensor v = fromSingleT (S := complexLorentzTensor) (c := .up) v

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector.toTensor_SL2CRep
declarations.doc:
The equivalence with the one-index tensors carries the action of `SL(2, ℂ)` on four-vectors to
the action on tensors.
declarations.statement:
lemma toTensor_SL2CRep (g : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : ComplexVector) :
    toTensor (SL2CRep g v) = g • toTensor v

declarations.name: Lorentz.ComplexVector.toTensor_basis
declarations.doc: The basis vector `e_μ` is the basis tensor with the single component `μ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toTensor_basis (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    toTensor (basis μ) = Tensor.basis (S := complexLorentzTensor) ![.up]
      (ComponentIdx.single.symm μ)

modules.title: Equivariant maps out of the tensors of a species
modules.doc:
Families of vectors carrying tensor indices, and how their invariants come from invariant tensors.

## i. Overview

A family of vectors in a representation `ρ` of the group `G` of a tensor species `S`, carrying
indices of colors `c`, is packaged as a linear map `f : S.Tensor c →ₗ[k] B`, and
`S.IsEquivariant c ρ f` says that `f` intertwines the action of `G` on tensors with `ρ`. The action
on `S.Tensor c` is a representation `S.tensorRep c`, so the invariant tensors are the Mathlib
submodule `(S.tensorRep c).invariants` (A). Every classification of invariant tensors is stated as
`(S.tensorRep c).invariants = ℂ ∙ t₀`, `= Submodule.span ℂ s` or `= ⊥`.

Over `ℂ`, the invariants in the range of such a map come from invariant tensors (C): every
invariant of `LinearMap.range f ⊔ W`, for `W` a `G`-stable submodule, is `f t + y` with `t` an
invariant tensor and `y ∈ W`. This holds whenever the tensors have a Reynolds element,
`HasReynolds` (B): an element of the group algebra with coefficients summing to one which maps
every tensor to an invariant one. Applied to any preimage of an invariant `f t`, it gives an
invariant tensor with the same image. The Reynolds elements of a group are produced from the
continuity of its action, which `continuousMatrixCoeff_top_comp` reads off the matrix entries of
the colors. A classification of the invariant tensors thereby classifies the invariants in the
range of `f`, `IsEquivariant.invariantReductionToSpan`, and the invariants in the range of an
intertwining map out of the tensors, `HasReynolds.invariants_inf_range_eq_span`.

A family `T` of vectors indexed by the component indices of `S.Tensor c` is the map
`liftComponents T`, sending each basis tensor to the matching component, and it is equivariant
exactly when the components obey the transformation law of the components of a tensor in the
basis of the species, `isEquivariant_liftComponents_iff` (D). A family indexed by other labels is
first relabelled by an equivalence `e` with the component indices, as `liftComponents (T ∘ e)`.

A tensor with two indices is `fromPairT` of exactly one element of the tensor product of the two
representations, and `fromPairTEquiv` intertwines the two actions, so the invariant tensors with
two indices are the image of the invariants of that tensor product; likewise for three indices and
`fromTripleTEquiv` (E). A classification of the invariants of a tensor product of
representations is thereby one of the invariant tensors. A family with two indices `T x y`,
relabelled by `pairIdx`, gives an equivariant map when each index moves by the matrix of its
colour, `isEquivariant_liftComponents_pair`.

Reindexing and dualising an index carry the invariant tensors of one colour list onto those of
the other, so a classification is stated only for the canonical order of the colours, undualised.
A classification of the coefficient functions fixed by the matrices of the group, one factor per
index, is one of the invariant tensors, `invariants_tensorRep_eq_map_componentEquiv` (F).

The group of a species can be changed along a homomorphism for each colour, the same for a colour
and its dual, keeping the tensors, `restrict` (G).

## ii. Key results

- `TensorSpecies.IsEquivariant` : equivariant linear maps out of `S.Tensor c`.
- `TensorSpecies.tensorRep` : the action on tensors as a representation.
- `TensorSpecies.HasReynolds` : the tensors have a Reynolds element.
- `TensorSpecies.continuousMatrixCoeff_top_comp` : continuity of the action on the tensors from
  that of the colors.
- `TensorSpecies.IsEquivariant.exists_invariant_add_of_mem_sup` : invariants of the range come from
  invariant tensors.
- `TensorSpecies.IsEquivariant.reducesInvariantsTo_span`,
  `TensorSpecies.IsEquivariant.reducesInvariantsTo_bot` : the reductions given by the invariant
  tensors.
- `TensorSpecies.IsEquivariant.invariantReductionToSpan` : the reduction to one invariant tensor.
- `TensorSpecies.HasReynolds.invariants_inf_range_eq_map` : the invariants in the range of an
  intertwining map out of the tensors are the image of the invariant tensors.
- `TensorSpecies.liftComponents` : a family lifted to the linear map out of the tensors sending
  each basis tensor to the matching member of the family.
- `TensorSpecies.isEquivariant_liftComponents_iff` : the map of a family is equivariant exactly when
  the family obeys the transformation law of the components.
- `TensorSpecies.invariants_tensorRep_pair_eq_span`,
  `TensorSpecies.invariants_tensorRep_triple_eq_span` : invariant tensors with two or three
  indices from the invariants of the tensor product of the representations.
- `TensorSpecies.invariants_tensorRep_eq_map_permT`,
  `TensorSpecies.invariants_tensorRep_update_eq_map_toDualMapAtIndex` : the invariant tensors
  transported along a reindexing and along the dualisation of an index.
- `TensorSpecies.invariants_tensorRep_eq_map_componentEquiv` : the invariant tensors from the
  invariant coefficient functions.
- `TensorSpecies.restrict` : a species restricted along a homomorphism of groups for each colour.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Equivariant maps and the tensors as a representation
- B. Reynolds elements for the tensors
- C. Invariants in the range come from invariant tensors
- D. Maps from components
- E. Invariant tensors with two and three indices
- F. Transport of the invariant tensors
  - F.1. Reindexing
  - F.2. Components
  - F.3. Dualisation
- G. Restricting the group

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Equivariant maps and the tensors as a representation
## B. Reynolds elements for the tensors
## C. Invariants in the range come from invariant tensors
## D. Maps from components
## E. Invariant tensors with two and three indices

## F. Transport of the invariant tensors

A classification of the invariant tensors is stated once, for the colours in their canonical order
and undualised. A reindexing `permT σ h` (F.1) and the dualisation `toDualMapAtIndex i` of an index
(F.3) are linear equivalences commuting with the group, so they carry the invariant tensors of one
colour list onto those of the other. A tensor is also determined by its components, and the
components of `g • t` are the components of `t` moved by the products of the matrix entries of `g`,
one factor per index (F.2). A classification of the coefficient functions fixed by these
products is thereby one of the invariant tensors.
### F.1. Reindexing
### F.2. Components
### F.3. Dualisation

## G. Restricting the group

A homomorphism `φ c : H →* G` for each colour, agreeing on a colour and its dual, turns the species
`S` into one for the group `H`, `S.restrict φ hφ`: the colour `c` carries the representation of
`G` pulled back along `φ c`, and the contractions and units are those of `S`, which stay
equivariant because a colour and its dual are pulled back along the same homomorphism. The
tensors, their bases and their components are those of `S`, and `h` acts on the index `i` of a
tensor with colours `c` as `φ (c i) h` does in `S`.

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.IsEquivariant
declarations.doc:
A linear map `f` from the tensors of the species `S` with index colors `c` to a
representation `ρ` of the group of the species, which is equivariant, that is, it intertwines
the action of the group on tensors with `ρ`.
declarations.statement:
structure IsEquivariant (S : TensorSpecies k C G V basisIdx rep b) {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → C)
    {B : Type*} [AddCommMonoid B] [Module k B] (ρ : Representation k G B)
    (f : S.Tensor c →ₗ[k] B) : Prop where
  equivariant : ∀ (g : G) (t : S.Tensor c), f (g • t) = ρ g (f t)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.smul_basis_eq_sum
declarations.doc:
The action of `g` on a basis tensor. The coefficient of `e_ψ` in `g • e_φ` is the product over
the indices of the matrix entries of `g` in the color of that index.
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_basis_eq_sum {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → C) (g : G) (φ : ComponentIdx (S := S) c) :
    g • Tensor.basis (S := S) c φ
      = ∑ ψ : ComponentIdx (S := S) c,
        (∏ i, LinearMap.toMatrix (b (c i)) (b (c i)) (rep (c i) g) (ψ i) (φ i)) •
        Tensor.basis (S := S) c ψ

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.basis_repr_smul
declarations.doc:
The components of `g • t`, the matrix of products of the matrix entries of `g`, one factor
per index, applied to the components of `t`.
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_repr_smul {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → C) (g : G) (t : S.Tensor c)
    (φ : ComponentIdx (S := S) c) :
    (Tensor.basis c).repr (g • t) φ
      = ∑ ψ, (∏ i, LinearMap.toMatrix (b (c i)) (b (c i)) (rep (c i) g) (φ i) (ψ i)) *
        (Tensor.basis c).repr t ψ

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.tensorRep
declarations.doc: The action of the group on the tensors with index colors `c`, as a representation.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def tensorRep {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → C) : Representation k G (S.Tensor c)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.tensorRep_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorRep_apply {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} (g : G) (t : S.Tensor c) :
    S.tensorRep c g t = g • t

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.tensorRep_eq_prod_smul
declarations.doc:
When `g` acts on the representation of each colour `a` by a scalar `s a`, it acts on the
tensors with colours `c` by the product of the scalars of their colours.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorRep_eq_prod_smul {g : G} {s : C → k} (hs : ∀ (a : C) (v : V a), rep a g v = s a • v)
    {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → C) : S.tensorRep c g = (∏ i, s (c i)) • LinearMap.id

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.invariants_tensorRep_eq_span_singleton
declarations.doc:
The invariant tensors are the line through an invariant tensor `t₀` when every invariant
tensor is a multiple of it.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_tensorRep_eq_span_singleton {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C} {t₀ : S.Tensor c}
    (ht₀ : ∀ g : G, g • t₀ = t₀)
    (h : ∀ t : S.Tensor c, (∀ g : G, g • t = t) → ∃ a : k, t = a • t₀) :
    (S.tensorRep c).invariants = k ∙ t₀

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.invariants_tensorRep_eq_bot
declarations.doc: There are no invariant tensors but zero when every invariant tensor vanishes.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_tensorRep_eq_bot {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → C}
    (h : ∀ t : S.Tensor c, (∀ g : G, g • t = t) → t = 0) : (S.tensorRep c).invariants = ⊥

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.IsEquivariant.isStableUnder_range
declarations.doc: The range of an equivariant map is stable under the group.
declarations.statement: lemma isStableUnder_range : IsStableUnder (fun g : G => ρ g) (LinearMap.range f)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.IsEquivariant.rep_map_of_invariant
declarations.doc: The image of an invariant tensor under an equivariant map is invariant.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_map_of_invariant {t : S.Tensor c} (ht : ∀ g : G, g • t = t) (g : G) :
    ρ g (f t) = f t

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.IsEquivariant.sum
declarations.doc: A sum of equivariant maps is equivariant.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) {F : ι → S.Tensor c →ₗ[k] B}
    (hF : ∀ i ∈ s, S.IsEquivariant c ρ (F i)) : S.IsEquivariant c ρ (∑ i ∈ s, F i)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.IsEquivariant.comp
declarations.doc: Composing with a linear map that intertwines `ρ` with `ρ'` keeps a map equivariant.

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.IsEquivariant.sub
declarations.doc: A difference of equivariant maps is equivariant.
declarations.statement:
lemma sub {f' : S.Tensor c →ₗ[k] B} (hf' : S.IsEquivariant c ρ f') :
    S.IsEquivariant c ρ (f - f')

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.HasReynolds
declarations.doc:
The tensors of `S` with index colors `c` have a Reynolds element: an element of the group
algebra, with coefficients summing to one, which maps every tensor to an invariant tensor.
declarations.statement: def HasReynolds (S : TensorSpecies ℂ C G V basisIdx rep b) {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → C) : Prop

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.HasReynolds.of_comp
declarations.doc:
The tensors have a Reynolds element when they have one for the action restricted along a
surjective homomorphism `φ` onto the group of the species.
declarations.statement:
lemma HasReynolds.of_comp {H : Type*} [Group H] {φ : H →* G} (hφ : Function.Surjective φ)
    (h : ∃ r, Representation.IsReynolds ((S.tensorRep c).comp φ) ⊤ r) : S.HasReynolds c

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.continuousMatrixCoeff_top_comp
declarations.doc:
The action on the tensors, restricted along `φ : H →* G`, has continuous matrix coefficients
when the matrix entries of every color are continuous on `H`.
declarations.statement:
lemma continuousMatrixCoeff_top_comp {H : Type*} [Group H] [TopologicalSpace H] (φ : H →* G)
    (hφ : ∀ (k : C) (x y : basisIdx k),
      Continuous fun h => LinearMap.toMatrix (b k) (b k) (rep k (φ h)) x y) :
    Representation.ContinuousMatrixCoeff (⊤ : Subrepresentation ((S.tensorRep c).comp φ))

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.IsEquivariant.exists_invariant_eq_of_mem_range
declarations.doc:
An invariant in the range of `f` is the image of an invariant tensor, the Reynolds element
applied to any preimage.

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.IsEquivariant.exists_invariant_add_of_mem_sup
declarations.doc:
An invariant of `LinearMap.range f ⊔ W`, for `W` a stable submodule, is the image of an
invariant tensor plus an element of `W`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_invariant_add_of_mem_sup (hc : S.HasReynolds c) (W : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hW : ∀ g : G, ∀ y ∈ W, ρ g y ∈ W) {x : B} (hx : x ∈ LinearMap.range f ⊔ W)
    (hinv : ∀ g : G, ρ g x = x) :
    ∃ t : S.Tensor c, (∀ g : G, g • t = t) ∧ ∃ y ∈ W, x = f t + y

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.IsEquivariant.reducesInvariantsTo_map
declarations.doc:
When every invariant tensor of `S.Tensor c` lies in `I`, the invariants of the range of `f`
reduce to the image of `I`.

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.IsEquivariant.reducesInvariantsTo_span
declarations.doc:
When the invariant tensors are the span of `s`, the invariants of the range of `f` reduce to
the span of the image of `s`.

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.IsEquivariant.reducesInvariantsTo_bot
declarations.doc: When the only invariant tensor of `S.Tensor c` is zero, the range of `f` reduces to `⊥`.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_bot (hc : S.HasReynolds c) (h : (S.tensorRep c).invariants = ⊥) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (fun g : G => ρ g) (LinearMap.range f) ⊥

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.IsEquivariant.eq_zero_of_invariant
declarations.doc:
When the only invariant tensor of `S.Tensor c` is zero, so is every invariant in the range
of `f`.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_zero_of_invariant (hc : S.HasReynolds c) (h : (S.tensorRep c).invariants = ⊥)
    {x : B} (hx : x ∈ LinearMap.range f) (hinv : ∀ g : G, ρ g x = x) : x = 0

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.IsEquivariant.invariantReductionToSpan
declarations.doc:
When the invariant tensors of `S.Tensor c` are the line through `t₀`, the invariants of the
range of `f` reduce to the span of `f t₀`.

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.IsEquivariant.invariantReductionToSpanOfEq
declarations.doc:
The reduction of `invariantReductionToSpan`, stated for a submodule `V` equal to the range of
`f` and with the spanning vector given by any expression `v` for `f t₀`.

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.HasReynolds.invariants_inf_range_eq_map
declarations.doc:
With a Reynolds element, the invariants in the range of an intertwining map `f` out of the
tensors are the images of the invariant tensors.
declarations.statement:
lemma HasReynolds.invariants_inf_range_eq_map (hc : S.HasReynolds c)
    (f : (S.tensorRep c).IntertwiningMap ρ) :
    ρ.invariants ⊓ f.range.toSubmodule = (S.tensorRep c).invariants.map f.toLinearMap

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.HasReynolds.invariants_inf_range_eq_span
declarations.doc:
The invariants in the range of an intertwining map `f` out of the tensors are the line through
`f t₀` when the invariant tensors are the line through `t₀`.

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.HasReynolds.invariants_inf_range_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
The invariants in the range of an intertwining map `f` out of the tensors are zero when there
are no invariant tensors but zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma HasReynolds.invariants_inf_range_eq_bot (hc : S.HasReynolds c)
    (h : (S.tensorRep c).invariants = ⊥) (f : (S.tensorRep c).IntertwiningMap ρ) :
    ρ.invariants ⊓ f.range.toSubmodule = ⊥

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.liftComponents
declarations.doc:
A family `T` indexed by the component indices, lifted along the tensor basis to the linear map
out of `S.Tensor c` sending each basis tensor to the matching component `T φ`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def liftComponents (T : ComponentIdx (S := S) c → B) : S.Tensor c →ₗ[k] B

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.liftComponents_basis
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_basis (T : ComponentIdx (S := S) c → B) (φ : ComponentIdx (S := S) c) :
    liftComponents T (Tensor.basis c φ) = T φ

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.range_liftComponents
declarations.doc: The range of `liftComponents T` is the span of the components.
declarations.statement:
lemma range_liftComponents (T : ComponentIdx (S := S) c → B) :
    LinearMap.range (liftComponents T) = Submodule.span k (Set.range T)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.range_liftComponents_comp
declarations.doc:
The range of the map of a family relabelled by an equivalence `e` is the span of the
family.
declarations.statement:
lemma range_liftComponents_comp {ι : Type*} (e : ComponentIdx (S := S) c ≃ ι) (T : ι → B) :
    LinearMap.range (liftComponents (T ∘ e)) = Submodule.span k (Set.range T)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.liftComponents_mem
declarations.doc: The image of `liftComponents T` lies in every submodule containing the components.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_mem (T : ComponentIdx (S := S) c → B) {M : Submodule k B}
    (hT : ∀ φ, T φ ∈ M) (t : S.Tensor c) : liftComponents T t ∈ M

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.liftComponents_comp_mem_span
declarations.doc:
The image of the map of a family relabelled by an equivalence `e` lies in the span of the
family.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_comp_mem_span {ι : Type*} (e : ComponentIdx (S := S) c ≃ ι) (T : ι → B)
    (t : S.Tensor c) : liftComponents (T ∘ e) t ∈ Submodule.span k (Set.range T)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.liftComponents_comp_mem
declarations.doc:
The image of the map of a relabelled family lies in every submodule containing the
family.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_comp_mem {ι : Type*} (e : ComponentIdx (S := S) c ≃ ι) (T : ι → B)
    {M : Submodule k B} (hT : ∀ l, T l ∈ M) (t : S.Tensor c) : liftComponents (T ∘ e) t ∈ M

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.liftComponents_sum
declarations.doc: `liftComponents` of a sum of families is the sum of the maps.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_sum {α : Type*} (s : Finset α) (T : α → ComponentIdx (S := S) c → B) :
    liftComponents (fun φ => ∑ i ∈ s, T i φ) = ∑ i ∈ s, liftComponents (T i)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.liftComponents_sub
declarations.doc: `liftComponents` of a difference of families is the difference of the maps.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_sub (T T' : ComponentIdx (S := S) c → B) :
    liftComponents (fun φ => T φ - T' φ) = liftComponents T - liftComponents T'

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.comp_liftComponents
declarations.doc:
A linear map applied after `liftComponents T` is `liftComponents` of its values on the
components.
declarations.statement:
lemma comp_liftComponents {B' : Type*} [AddCommGroup B'] [Module k B'] (σ : B →ₗ[k] B')
    (T : ComponentIdx (S := S) c → B) :
    σ ∘ₗ liftComponents T = liftComponents fun φ => σ (T φ)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.map_liftComponents
declarations.doc:
A linear map applied to `liftComponents T t` is `liftComponents` of its values on the
components, applied to `t`.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_liftComponents {B' : Type*} [AddCommGroup B'] [Module k B'] (σ : B →ₗ[k] B')
    (T : ComponentIdx (S := S) c → B) (t : S.Tensor c) :
    σ (liftComponents T t) = liftComponents (fun φ => σ (T φ)) t

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.liftComponents_comp_sum
declarations.doc: `liftComponents` of a sum of relabelled families is the sum of the maps.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_comp_sum {ι α : Type*} (e : ComponentIdx (S := S) c ≃ ι) (s : Finset α)
    (T : α → ι → B) :
    liftComponents ((fun l => ∑ i ∈ s, T i l) ∘ e) = ∑ i ∈ s, liftComponents (T i ∘ e)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.liftComponents_comp_sub
declarations.doc: `liftComponents` of a difference of relabelled families is the difference of the maps.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_comp_sub {ι : Type*} (e : ComponentIdx (S := S) c ≃ ι) (T T' : ι → B) :
    liftComponents ((fun l => T l - T' l) ∘ e) = liftComponents (T ∘ e) - liftComponents (T' ∘ e)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.map_liftComponents_comp
declarations.doc:
A linear map applied to the map of a relabelled family is the map of its values on the
family.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_liftComponents_comp {ι : Type*} {B' : Type*} [AddCommGroup B'] [Module k B']
    (σ : B →ₗ[k] B') (e : ComponentIdx (S := S) c ≃ ι) (T : ι → B) (t : S.Tensor c) :
    σ (liftComponents (T ∘ e) t) = liftComponents ((fun l => σ (T l)) ∘ e) t

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.liftComponents_smul_of_law
declarations.doc:
A linear map moving the components as `g` moves the basis tensors intertwines
`liftComponents T` with the action of `g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_smul_of_law (T : ComponentIdx (S := S) c → B) {σ : B →ₗ[k] B} (g : G)
    (hσ : ∀ φ, σ (T φ)
      = ∑ ψ, (∏ i, LinearMap.toMatrix (b (c i)) (b (c i)) (rep (c i) g) (ψ i) (φ i)) • T ψ)
    (t : S.Tensor c) :
    σ (liftComponents T t) = liftComponents T (g • t)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.isEquivariant_liftComponents_iff
declarations.doc:
The map of a family is equivariant exactly when the components are moved as the basis
tensors are, with one matrix entry of `g` per index and the summed index first in each
factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_liftComponents_iff {ρ : Representation k G B}
    (T : ComponentIdx (S := S) c → B) :
    S.IsEquivariant c ρ (liftComponents T) ↔ ∀ (g : G) (φ : ComponentIdx (S := S) c), ρ g (T φ)
      = ∑ ψ, (∏ i, LinearMap.toMatrix (b (c i)) (b (c i)) (rep (c i) g) (ψ i) (φ i)) • T ψ

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.isEquivariant_liftComponents_sum
declarations.doc: The map of a finite sum of families is equivariant when the map of each family is.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_liftComponents_sum {ρ : Representation k G B} {α : Type*} (s : Finset α)
    {T : α → ComponentIdx (S := S) c → B}
    (hT : ∀ i ∈ s, S.IsEquivariant c ρ (liftComponents (T i))) :
    S.IsEquivariant c ρ (liftComponents fun φ => ∑ i ∈ s, T i φ)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.fromPairT_injective
declarations.doc: A tensor with two indices determines the element of `V c1 ⊗ V c2` it comes from.
declarations.statement:
lemma fromPairT_injective {c1 c2 : C} :
    Function.Injective (fromPairT (S := S) (c1 := c1) (c2 := c2))

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.fromPairT_surjective
declarations.doc: Every tensor with two indices comes from `V c1 ⊗ V c2`, since the basis tensors do.
declarations.statement:
lemma fromPairT_surjective {c1 c2 : C} :
    Function.Surjective (fromPairT (S := S) (c1 := c1) (c2 := c2))

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.fromTripleT_injective
declarations.doc:
A tensor with three indices determines the element of `V c1 ⊗ (V c2 ⊗ V c3)` it comes
from.
declarations.statement:
lemma fromTripleT_injective {c1 c2 c3 : C} :
    Function.Injective (fromTripleT (S := S) (c1 := c1) (c2 := c2) (c3 := c3))

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.fromTripleT_surjective
declarations.doc:
Every tensor with three indices comes from `V c1 ⊗ (V c2 ⊗ V c3)`, since the basis tensors
do.
declarations.statement:
lemma fromTripleT_surjective {c1 c2 c3 : C} :
    Function.Surjective (fromTripleT (S := S) (c1 := c1) (c2 := c2) (c3 := c3))

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.invariants_eq_map_of_equiv
declarations.doc:
For a linear equivalence `e` onto the tensors intertwining `σ` with the action on tensors, the
invariants of `σ` are the images of the invariant tensors under `e⁻¹`.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_eq_map_of_equiv {W : Type*} [AddCommGroup W] [Module k W]
    {σ : Representation k G W} (e : W ≃ₗ[k] S.Tensor c)
    (he : ∀ (g : G) (w : W), e (σ g w) = g • e w) :
    σ.invariants = (S.tensorRep c).invariants.map (e.symm : S.Tensor c →ₗ[k] W)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.invariants_tensorRep_eq_map_of_equiv
declarations.doc:
For a linear equivalence `e` onto the tensors intertwining `σ` with the action on tensors, the
invariant tensors are the images under `e` of the invariants of `σ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_tensorRep_eq_map_of_equiv {W : Type*} [AddCommGroup W] [Module k W]
    {σ : Representation k G W} (e : W ≃ₗ[k] S.Tensor c)
    (he : ∀ (g : G) (w : W), e (σ g w) = g • e w) :
    (S.tensorRep c).invariants = σ.invariants.map (e : W →ₗ[k] S.Tensor c)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.fromPairTEquiv
declarations.doc: The tensors with two indices as the tensor product of the two representations.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def fromPairTEquiv {c1 c2 : C} : V c1 ⊗[k] V c2 ≃ₗ[k] S.Tensor ![c1, c2]

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.fromPairTEquiv_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma fromPairTEquiv_apply {c1 c2 : C} (x : V c1 ⊗[k] V c2) :
    fromPairTEquiv (S := S) x = Tensor.fromPairT x

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.fromPairTEquiv_tprod
declarations.doc:
`fromPairTEquiv` intertwines the tensor product of the two representations with the action on
tensors.
declarations.statement:
lemma fromPairTEquiv_tprod {c1 c2 : C} (g : G) (x : V c1 ⊗[k] V c2) :
    fromPairTEquiv (S := S) (((rep c1).tprod (rep c2)) g x) = g • fromPairTEquiv x

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.invariants_tprod_eq_span_singleton
declarations.doc:
The invariants of the tensor product of two representations are the line through `v` when the
invariant tensors with two indices are the line through `fromPairT v`.

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.fromTripleTEquiv
declarations.doc: The tensors with three indices as the tensor product of the three representations.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fromTripleTEquiv {c1 c2 c3 : C} :
    V c1 ⊗[k] (V c2 ⊗[k] V c3) ≃ₗ[k] S.Tensor ![c1, c2, c3]

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.fromTripleTEquiv_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma fromTripleTEquiv_apply {c1 c2 c3 : C} (x : V c1 ⊗[k] (V c2 ⊗[k] V c3)) :
    fromTripleTEquiv (S := S) x = Tensor.fromTripleT x

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.fromTripleTEquiv_tprod
declarations.doc:
`fromTripleTEquiv` intertwines the tensor product of the three representations with the action
on tensors.
declarations.statement:
lemma fromTripleTEquiv_tprod {c1 c2 c3 : C} (g : G) (x : V c1 ⊗[k] (V c2 ⊗[k] V c3)) :
    fromTripleTEquiv (S := S) (((rep c1).tprod ((rep c2).tprod (rep c3))) g x)
      = g • fromTripleTEquiv x

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.pairIdx
declarations.doc: The component indices of a tensor with two indices, as the pair of their labels.
declarations.statement: def pairIdx {c1 c2 : C} : ComponentIdx (S := S) ![c1, c2] ≃ basisIdx c1 × basisIdx c2

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.isEquivariant_liftComponents_pair
declarations.doc:
The map of a family `T x y` with two indices is equivariant when each index is moved by the
matrix of `g` in its colour, the summed index first in each factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_liftComponents_pair {c1 c2 : C} {B : Type*} [AddCommGroup B] [Module k B]
    {ρ : Representation k G B} (T : basisIdx c1 → basisIdx c2 → B)
    (hT : ∀ (g : G) x y, ρ g (T x y) = ∑ x', ∑ y',
      (LinearMap.toMatrix (b c1) (b c1) (rep c1 g) x' x *
        LinearMap.toMatrix (b c2) (b c2) (rep c2 g) y' y) • T x' y') :
    S.IsEquivariant ![c1, c2] ρ (liftComponents ((fun p => T p.1 p.2) ∘ pairIdx))

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.range_liftComponents_pair
declarations.doc: The range of the map of a family `T x y` with two indices is the span of its members.
declarations.statement:
lemma range_liftComponents_pair {c1 c2 : C} {B : Type*} [AddCommGroup B] [Module k B]
    (T : basisIdx c1 → basisIdx c2 → B) :
    LinearMap.range (liftComponents (S := S) ((fun p => T p.1 p.2) ∘ pairIdx))
      = Submodule.span k (Set.range fun m : basisIdx c1 × basisIdx c2 => T m.1 m.2)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.invariants_tensorRep_pair_eq_span
declarations.doc:
The invariant tensors with two indices are the line through `fromPairT v` when the invariants
of the tensor product of the two representations are the line through `v`.

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.invariants_tensorRep_pair_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
There are no invariant tensors with two indices but zero when the tensor product of the two
representations has none.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_tensorRep_pair_eq_bot {c1 c2 : C} (h : ((rep c1).tprod (rep c2)).invariants = ⊥) :
    (S.tensorRep ![c1, c2]).invariants = ⊥

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.invariants_tensorRep_triple_eq_span
declarations.doc:
The invariant tensors with three indices are the line through `fromTripleT v` when the
invariants of the tensor product of the three representations are the line through `v`.

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.isReindexing_append_three
declarations.doc:
The colours `Fin.append ![c1] (Fin.append ![c2] ![c3])` of the tensors of a product of three
tensorial types are the plain list `![c1, c2, c3]`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isReindexing_append_three (c1 c2 c3 : C) :
    IsReindexing (Fin.append ![c1] (Fin.append ![c2] ![c3])) ![c1, c2, c3] id

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.permTEquiv
declarations.doc: The reindexing `permT σ h` as a linear equivalence.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def permTEquiv {m : ℕ} {c1 : Fin m → C} {σ : Fin m → Fin n}
    (h : IsReindexing c c1 σ) : S.Tensor c ≃ₗ[k] S.Tensor c1

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.invariants_tensorRep_eq_map_permT
declarations.doc: Reindexing carries the invariant tensors onto the invariant tensors.

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.invariants_tensorRep_eq_span_of_permT
declarations.doc:
A spanning set of the invariant tensors is carried by a reindexing to one of the reindexed
invariant tensors.

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.invariants_tensorRep_eq_bot_of_permT
declarations.doc: A reindexing of colours with no invariant tensors but zero has none either.

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.componentEquiv
declarations.doc:
The components of a tensor, as a function of labels `ι` matched with the component indices
by `e`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def componentEquiv {ι : Type*} (e : ComponentIdx (S := S) c ≃ ι) :
    S.Tensor c ≃ₗ[k] (ι → k)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.componentEquiv_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma componentEquiv_apply {ι : Type*} (e : ComponentIdx (S := S) c ≃ ι) (t : S.Tensor c)
    (a : ι) : componentEquiv e t a = (Tensor.basis c).repr t (e.symm a)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.componentEquiv_smul
declarations.doc:
The components of `g • t` are those of `t` moved by `A g`, when `A g` is the product of the
matrix entries of `g`, one factor per index.
declarations.statement:
lemma componentEquiv_smul {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (e : ComponentIdx (S := S) c ≃ ι)
    {A : G → ι → ι → k} (hA : ∀ g φ ψ, A g (e φ) (e ψ)
      = ∏ i, LinearMap.toMatrix (b (c i)) (b (c i)) (rep (c i) g) (φ i) (ψ i))
    (g : G) (t : S.Tensor c) :
    componentEquiv e (g • t) = fun a => ∑ a', componentEquiv e t a' * A g a a'

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.invariants_tensorRep_eq_map_componentEquiv
declarations.doc:
The invariant tensors are the images of the coefficient functions fixed by every `A g`, for
`A g` the matrix of `g` on the components. A classification of these coefficient functions,
as the members of a submodule `K`, is thereby one of the invariant tensors.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_tensorRep_eq_map_componentEquiv {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (e : ComponentIdx (S := S) c ≃ ι) {A : G → ι → ι → k}
    (hA : ∀ g φ ψ, A g (e φ) (e ψ)
      = ∏ i, LinearMap.toMatrix (b (c i)) (b (c i)) (rep (c i) g) (φ i) (ψ i))
    {K : Submodule k (ι → k)}
    (hK : ∀ x : ι → k, (∀ g, (fun a => ∑ a', x a' * A g a a') = x) ↔ x ∈ K) :
    (S.tensorRep c).invariants = K.map ((componentEquiv e).symm : (ι → k) →ₗ[k] S.Tensor c)

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.invariants_tensorRep_update_eq_map_toDualMapAtIndex
declarations.doc:
Dualising the index `i` carries the invariant tensors onto those with the colour of `i`
dualised.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_tensorRep_update_eq_map_toDualMapAtIndex (i : Fin n) :
    (S.tensorRep (Function.update c i (S.τ (c i)))).invariants
      = Submodule.map (Tensor.toDualMapAtIndex (S := S) (c := c) i)
        (S.tensorRep c).invariants

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.invariants_tensorRep_eq_bot_of_dual
declarations.doc:
Dualising an index of colours with no invariant tensors but zero leaves none, the colours
of the result given up to pointwise equality as `c'`.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_tensorRep_eq_bot_of_dual {c' : Fin n → C} (i : Fin n)
    (hb : (S.tensorRep c).invariants = ⊥) (hc : ∀ j, Function.update c i (S.τ (c i)) j = c' j) :
    (S.tensorRep c').invariants = ⊥

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.restrict
declarations.doc:
The species `S` for the group `H`, with the representation of each colour `c` pulled back
along a homomorphism `φ c : H →* G`, the same for a colour and its dual.

declarations.name: TensorSpecies.restrict_tensorRep_apply
declarations.doc:
An element `h` acts on the tensors of the restricted species as `φ (c i) h` acts on the index
`i` in `S`.
declarations.statement:
lemma restrict_tensorRep_apply (S : TensorSpecies k C G V basisIdx rep b) {H : Type} [Group H]
    {φ : C → H →* G} {hφ : ∀ c, φ (S.τ c) = φ c} {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → C) (h : H) :
    (S.restrict φ hφ).tensorRep c h = PiTensorProduct.map fun i => rep (c i) (φ (c i) h)

modules.title: The representation of `SL(2, ℂ)` on real Lorentz covectors
modules.doc:
The covector representation pulled back along the covering map, and its dual.

## i. Overview

`Physlib.Relativity.Tensors.RealTensor.CoVector.Representation` carries the representation of
the Lorentz group on real Lorentz covectors. Composing it with the covering map
`SL(2, ℂ) →* LorentzGroup 3` gives `sl2Rep`, the representation of `SL(2, ℂ)` on the same
space, which is the form a spinor computation needs. Its dual acts on the dual basis
contravariantly: `sl2Rep_dual_dualBasis` says that `e^μ` goes to the combination given by the
column `μ` of the Lorentz matrix.

## ii. Key results

- `Lorentz.CoVector.sl2Rep` : the representation of `SL(2, ℂ)` on real Lorentz covectors.
- `Lorentz.CoVector.sl2Rep_dual_dualBasis` : dual covectors transform by the columns of the
  Lorentz matrix.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The representation of `SL(2, ℂ)`

## iv. References

The Lorentz-group representation is in
`Physlib.Relativity.Tensors.RealTensor.CoVector.Representation`.

sections.text: ## A. The representation of `SL(2, ℂ)`

declarations.name: Lorentz.CoVector.sl2Rep
declarations.doc:
The representation of `SL(2,ℂ)` on real Lorentz covectors, obtained from the
representation of the Lorentz group through the covering map
`SL(2,ℂ) →* LorentzGroup 3`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def sl2Rep : Representation ℝ SL(2,ℂ) Lorentz.CoVector

declarations.name: Lorentz.CoVector.sl2Rep_dual_dualBasis
declarations.doc:
The dual of the covector representation on the dual basis: dual covectors
transform contravariantly, by the columns of the Lorentz matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma sl2Rep_dual_dualBasis (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    Lorentz.CoVector.sl2Rep.dual Λ (Lorentz.CoVector.basis.dualBasis μ) =
      ∑ j, (Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 j μ •
        Lorentz.CoVector.basis.dualBasis j
